01Chapter 1 · How Data Drives Decision Making in Machine Learning

Data se Decision Making tak — ML Workflow ka Overview

ML ka matlab sirf model banana nahi hai — asli kaam hai data se sahi decision lena. Is chapter mein tum samjhoge ki business ka goal pehle decide hota hai, phir us goal ke hisaab se data collect hota hai, aur phir ek poora enterprise ML workflow us data ko prediction mein badal deta hai.

Data pehle nahi, goal pehle

Bohot saari books ML workflow ki shuruaat data gather karne se karti hain, lekin yeh book ek alag point rakhti hai — data gather karne se pehle tumhe yeh samajhna hoga ki kis type ka data chahiye, aur yeh samajh sirf tab aati hai jab tumhe pata ho ki kaunsi problem solve karni hai ya kaunsa decision lena hai.

Business case ya problem definition aur data understanding se hi tum ek no-code ya low-code ML strategy bana sakte ho. No-code AutoML approach mein domain knowledge wala koi bhi person, bina ek line code likhe, jaldi ML model bana sakta hai. Low-code approach mein thoda coding experience wala person autogenerated basic code ko customize karke jaldi ML application bana sakta hai.

Decision making aur ML workflow ka connection

Decision-making process tumhe tumhari problem ya use case identify karne mein help karta hai, aur ML workflow tumhe us problem ka solution implement karne mein help karta hai. Dono kaam data-driven hain, aur dono mein har step par decision lena padta hai.

  • Decision making: sawaal poochho, data collect karo, aur alternative solutions ko assess karo — phir use case fix karo.
  • ML workflow: usi data se machine ko customer patterns seekhne do, trends spot karne do, aur outcomes predict karne do — AutoML ya low-code AI se.
  • Goal se prediction tak: business case → data source determination → ML framework → prediction, yahi chain har project mein repeat hoti hai.

Is chapter mein kya seekhoge

Tum seekhoge ki goal ya use case kaise define karte hain, enterprise ML workflow ke steps kya hain, data collection, preprocessing, analysis, transformation aur feature selection kaise hoti hai, aur model selection, training, evaluation, testing, deployment aur maintenance kaise kaam karte hain.

Yaad rakho: Har ML project ki shuruaat goal se hoti hai, data se nahi. Galat sawaal par sahi data bhi bekaar hai — pehle problem statement clear karo, phir data ki taraf badho.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — How Data Drives Decision Making in Machine Learning

01.1Chapter 1 · How Data Drives Decision Making in Machine Learning

Use Case ya Goal kya hai?

Businesses, educational institutions, government agencies aur practitioners — sab ke saamne aise decisions aate hain jo ML ke real-world examples hain. Use case clear hoga tohi pata chalega ki kaunsa data chahiye aur kaunsa ML solution sahi rahega.

Real-world decisions jo ML use cases ban jaate hain

  • Patient engagement: diabetes web app ke saath patient engagement kaise badhaayein?
  • Student feedback: course surveys par student feedback numbers kaise badhaayein?
  • Cyberattack detection: company networks ke against cyberattacks detect karne ki speed kaise badhaayein?
  • Spam kam karna: email servers mein aane wale spam emails ki sankhya kaise ghataayein?
  • Downtime kam karna: manufacturing production line ka downtime kaise kam karein?
  • Retention aur churn: customer retention rate kaise badhaayein aur customer churn (attrition) rate kaise ghataayein?

Har ek example mein kai data sources ko examine karna padta hai, tabhi pata chalta hai ki kaunsa ML solution problem solve karne ya decision making mein help karne ke liye sabse appropriate hai.

Churn prediction — ek simple example

Customer churn prediction ka matlab hai un customers ko identify karna jo tumhari service ya product chhodne wale hain. Yeh ek supervised learning problem hai, aur ek classification problem hai jisme do classes hoti hain — Churn-Yes class aur Churn-No class.

Data source ki taraf se tumhe customer profile information (name, address, age, job title, employment statement), purchase information (purchases aur billing history), interaction information (digitally aur physically products ke saath customer experiences), customer service teams, ya digital support services ko examine karna pad sakta hai.

  • Popular data sources: customer relationship management (CRM) systems, ecommerce analytics services, aur customer feedback.
  • Golden rule: customer jo kuch bhi "touch" karta hai, woh har data point track aur capture karna chahiye as a data source.

Umbrella example — price kam karo to sales kitni badhegi?

Maan lo tum ek umbrella banane wali company ke marketing in-charge ho aur business goal hai sales badhana. Agar tum apne existing umbrellas ka selling price kam kar do, to kya tum predict kar sakte ho ki kitne umbrellas bikenge?

Yahan sirf selling price kaafi nahi hai. Tumhe aur bhi data dimensions chahiye honge — specific regions mein rainy seasons, population density, aur kya tumhara inventory price reduction se badhne wali demand ko meet karne ke liye sufficient hai. Historical data ko typically batch kaha jaata hai, aur real-time mein capture hone wale data ko streaming kaha jaata hai.

Yeh dekhte hi business goal ek complex problem ban jaata hai, kyunki in additional dimensions ke liye aur columns chahiye honge. Kisi bhi organization ke paas dozens of discrete data sources ho sakte hain, aur har source ke beech ke relationships samajhne ke liye alag skills chahiye hoti hain.

Business decision-making process

Use case kya hai — yeh "it depends" par depend karta hai. Tumhe ek business decision-making process se guzarna hoga, jo choices banane ka process hai — sawaal poochh kar, data collect karke, aur alternative resolutions ko assess karke.

Jab tum use case ya business goal figure out kar lete ho, to usi data ko use karke machines ko train kar sakte ho taaki woh tumhare customer patterns ke baare mein seekhein, trends spot karein, aur AutoML ya low-code AI se outcomes predict karein.

Yaad rakho: Decision ki nature seedha us data se judi hoti hai jo tumhe decision lene ke liye gather karna hai. Pehle problem statement banao, phir data sources decide karo — ulta karne par tum galat data collect kar loge.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — How Data Drives Decision Making in Machine Learning

01.2Chapter 1 · How Data Drives Decision Making in Machine Learning

Enterprise ML Workflow — 10 Steps

ML workflow steps ki ek series hai, aur in steps ko phases mein combine kiya ja sakta hai. Book mein workflow ko 10 steps mein dikhaya gaya hai, jo 4 phases mein batte hain — decision making, data processing, modeling, aur deployment. Har phase AutoML ya low-code AI se implement ki ja sakti hai.

4 phases — poora workflow ek nazar mein

  1. Phase 1 — Decision making: business objective ya problem statement define karna.
  2. Phase 2 — Data processing: data collection, preprocessing, analysis, transformation aur feature selection.
  3. Phase 3 — Modeling: model selection ya AutoML, training, evaluation, tuning aur testing.
  4. Phase 4 — Deployment: model deployment (serving) aur models ko maintain karna.

Step 1 — Business objective ya problem statement define karo

Workflow ki shuruaat ek specific question ya problem ko defined boundary ke saath define karne se hoti hai. Is phase mein tum scope aur feasibility define karne ki koshish karte ho. Sahi sawaal tumhe yeh batayega ki kaunsa data chahiye aur data ko kaise prepare karna hoga.

Data analyze karte waqt uthne wala koi bhi sawaal 5 ML categories mein se ek mein group kiya ja sakta hai — umbrella example se samjho:

  • Regression problem: is month ya season mein kitne umbrellas sell hone ki expectation hai? (How many?)
  • Classification problem: kya unhone straight umbrellas (A) khareede ya foldable umbrellas (B)?
  • Clustering problem: month ya region ke hisaab se kitne straight umbrellas beche gaye?
  • Anomaly detection problem: kya company ne Mojave Desert mein Portland, OR se zyada umbrellas beche?
  • Reinforcement learning: company policy hai ki sirf un customers ko ship karo jinka balance owed $500 ya usse kam hai — kya manufacturing robot ko train kiya ja sakta hai ki woh straight umbrellas extract, package, load aur ship kare is policy ke basis par?

Umbrella example mein AutoML ka role

Umbrella example mein tum apne data se ek ML model train kar sakte ho, ek AutoML service use karke jo unsupervised ML clustering ke liye no-code solution deti hai. Wahan se tum data points ke clusters examine karke dekh sakte ho ki kaunse patterns derive hue. Ya phir tum sirf historical data par focus karke ek specific target predict kar sakte ho, kuch data input features ke basis par.

Yaad rakho: Sahi sawaal hi sahi data aur sahi model ki taraf le jaata hai. Apne sawaal ko pehle 5 categories mein se ek mein daalo — regression, classification, clustering, anomaly detection, ya reinforcement learning — phir aage badho.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — How Data Drives Decision Making in Machine Learning
← Previous01.1 · Use Case ya Goal kya hai?→ Next01.3 · Data Collection, Preprocessing aur Analysis
01.3Chapter 1 · How Data Drives Decision Making in Machine Learning

Data Collection, Preprocessing aur Analysis

Data processing phase mein data collect karna, saaf karna, analyze karna aur features banana aata hai. Real-world data raw aur messy hota hai, isliye yeh steps skip nahi kiye ja sakte — inhi par model ki quality depend karti hai.

Data collection — on-premises se cloud tak

21st century ke shuru mein companies, universities aur researchers typically local servers ya hard drives ya data centers par apne database applications host karte the aur data store karte the. On-premises data centers ya rented server space costly tha — server infrastructure maintain karni padti thi, software update karna padta tha, security patches install karne padte the, aur physical hardware swap karna padta tha. Kai baar bada data machines ke cluster mein store hota tha.

Aaj costs bachane ke liye enterprises aur educational institutions cloud par move ho gaye hain apne database applications host karne aur data store karne ke liye. Cloud storage ek service hai jo cloud vendors dete hain files store karne ke liye — tum different file formats upload kar sakte ho, ya use configure kar sakte ho taaki woh different data sources se files automatically receive kare.

  • Cloud storage buckets: structured aur unstructured dono data store kar sakte hain, aur kyunki zyada tar ML models files se aane wale data par train hote hain, isliye cloud storage bucket mein data rakhna data collection ko easy bana deta hai.
  • GitHub: coding projects par collaborate karne ke liye bani service, jahan tum data free mein cloud mein store kar sakte ho, changes track kar sakte ho, aur replication ke liye data publicly available bana sakte ho. Isme strict file size limit 100 MB hai, lekin Git Large File Storage (LFS) ka option hai — ek open source GitHub extension jo large files ko version karta hai. Git LFS datasets, audio samples, graphics aur videos jaise large files ko Git ke andar text pointers se replace kar deta hai, jabki file contents remote server jaise GitHub.com ya GitHub Enterprise par store hote hain.

Large organizations mein data collection aur bhi mushkil ho jaata hai, kyunki wahan enterprise resource planning (ERP), customer relationship management (CRM) aur production systems jaise kai types ke operations management software hote hain, jo alag-alag databases par chal sakte hain. Data ko external sources se real time mein bhi pull karna pad sakta hai, jaise delivery trucks ke Internet of Things (IoT) sensor devices se. Isliye organizations ko sirf structured data hi nahi, unstructured aur semistructured data formats bhi batches ya real time (streaming) mein collect karne hote hain.

Ek important distinction yaad rakho — structured versus unstructured data format ki property hai, aur streaming versus batch latency ki property hai. Streaming structured data bhi ho sakta hai.

Data preprocessing — messy data ko saaf karo

Data cleanup karne ke liye tumhe missing data values, duplicates, outlier data, formatting issues, ya human error ki wajah se inconsistent data se deal karna hoga. Real-world data raw aur messy hota hai aur assumptions se bhara hota hai.

Ek assumption yeh ho sakti hai ki tumhare data ka normal distribution hai, matlab data symmetrically distributed hai bina skew ke, aur zyada tar values central region ke aas-paas cluster karti hain, aur values ki frequency center (mean ya average) se door jaate hue kam hoti jaati hai.

  • Outlier example: maan lo tumhare data mein pehli baar Palm Springs (California desert town) mein August mein beche gaye umbrellas ki sankhya mein increase dikha. Kya tumhara data normally distributed hoga, ya yeh ek outlier mana jayega? Kya yeh August mein monthly umbrella sales ke predictions ke results ko skew karega?
  • Normalization: jab data ka normal distribution nahi hota, to use normalize karna padta hai — saare records ko [0,1] ya [–1,1] jaise range mein group karke normal banana. Tum dataset ko normalize isliye karte ho taaki ML model train karna easy aur fast ho jaye.
  • Min-max normalization ka risk: outliers hone par min-max normalization ke detrimental effects ho sakte hain — [0,1] mein scale karte waqt woh essentially outlier ko 1 par map kar deta hai aur baaki saari values ko 0 ki taraf squash kar deta hai. Outliers aur anomalies ko address karna is book ke scope se bahar hai.
  • Scaling: data preprocessing ka matlab normalization (numeric columns ek common scale use karein) aur scaling (data ko transform karna taaki woh ek specific range mein fit ho) bhi ho sakta hai. Normalization aur standardization Python mein sirf kuch simple lines of code se easily perform ki ja sakti hain.

Agar tum kai data sources ko ek file mein aggregate kar rahe ho, to make sure karo ki data formats match karein aur time-series data (ya timestamp aur date ranges jo tumhare ML model ko chahiye) ke baare mein assumptions validate ki gayi hon. Ek common assumption yeh hai ki data stationary hai — matlab statistical properties (mean, variance, etc.) time ke saath change nahi hote.

Data analysis — EDA se patterns dhoondho

Exploratory data analysis (EDA) ek process hai jo data ki structure ko explore aur analyze karne ke liye use hota hai. Is step mein tum trends, patterns, feature relevance aur correlations discover karne ki koshish karte ho — jaise ek variable (feature) dusre se kaise correlate kar sakta hai.

Tumhe apne solve karne wale problem ke type ke basis par ML model ke liye relevant feature data select karna hota hai. Is step ka outcome input variables ki ek feature list hoti hai jo ML ke liye potentially use ki ja sakti hai. Hands-on EDA exercise Chapter 6 mein hai.

  • Seaborn regplot example: ek plot mein x aur y ke beech inverse relationship dikhti hai — temperature kam hone par zyada energy produce hoti hai.
  • Correlation matrix (heat map) example: Temp aur Energy_Production ke beech strong inverse relationship hai, value –0.75.

Data transformation aur feature selection

Data clean aur analyze karne ke baad tumhare paas un features ki list hoti hai jo tumhe lagta hai tumhari ML problem solve karne mein help karenge. Lekin kya aur features relevant ho sakte hain? Yahi par feature engineering aati hai — jahan tum naye features engineer ya create karte ho jo original dataset mein nahi the.

Example ke liye, agar tumhare dataset mein month, day aur year ke liye alag fields ya columns hain, to tum teeno ko combine karke ek "month-day-year" time feature bana sakte ho. Feature engineering feature selection se pehle ka final step hai.

Reality mein feature selection do stages par hoti hai — EDA ke baad aur data transformation ke baad. EDA ke baad tumhare paas potential features ki list hoti hai jo naye features create karne ke candidates ho sakte hain — jaise time aur day of week ko combine karke hour of day nikaalna. Feature engineering karne ke baad tumhare paas features ki final list hoti hai, jinme se tum select karte ho.

Yaad rakho: Data ko pehle samjho, phir saaf karo, phir analyze karo, aur tabhi naye features banao. Feature list EDA ka outcome hai — bina EDA ke seedha model par jaana matlab andhere mein teer chalana hai.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — How Data Drives Decision Making in Machine Learning

01.4Chapter 1 · How Data Drives Decision Making in Machine Learning

Model Selection, Training, Testing aur Deployment

Data ready hone ke baad modeling phase shuru hoti hai — sahi model choose karo ya AutoML ko choose karne do, phir train karo, evaluate karo, tune karo, test karo, aur phir deploy karke maintain karo. AutoML yahan heavy lifting karta hai, lekin tumhe yeh samajhna hoga ki andar kya ho raha hai.

Model selection ya AutoML (no-code solution)

Is step mein tum ya to research karte ho ki tumhare problem ke data type ke liye kaunsa model best rahega — ya phir tum AutoML use karte ho, ek no-code solution jo tumhare upload kiye gaye dataset ke basis par appropriate model select karta hai, train karta hai, test karta hai, aur evaluation metrics generate karta hai.

AutoML use karne par model selection, model training, model tuning aur evaluation metrics generate karne ki heavy lifting tumhare liye ho jaati hai. Chapter 3 AutoML introduce karta hai, aur Chapter 4 mein AutoML ke saath hands-on shuruaat hoti hai. Low-code solution mein tumhe pata hona chahiye ki kaunsa model select karna hai.

AutoML tumhare lagbhag 80% ML problems cover kar sakta hai, lekin agar tumhe zyada customized solution chahiye, to ML algorithms kis type ki problems solve kar sakte hain, iski general understanding helpful hoti hai. Algorithm choose karna sirf problem par depend karta hai:

  • Regression problem: "How much ya how many umbrellas?" — regression algorithms continuous aur numeric output wali problems se deal karte hain, aur usually "how much" ya "how many" jaise sawaalon ke liye use hote hain.
  • Classification problem: "Kya unhone straight umbrellas (A) khareede ya foldable umbrellas (B)?" — output sirf ek fixed number of output classes mein se ek ho sakta hai, jaise Yes/No ya True/False. Output classes ki sankhya ke basis par yeh binary ya multiclass classification problem ho sakta hai.
  • Reinforcement learning: "$500 ya usse kam balance owed wale customers ko hi ship karna hai — kya manufacturing robot ko train kiya ja sakta hai?" — reinforcement algorithms tab use hote hain jab decision experiences se seekh kar lena hota hai. Machine agent trial aur error se seekhta hai, continuously changing environment ke saath interact karke. Yeh rewards aur penalties ke concept se agents ko program karne ka tareeka deta hai, bina yeh specify kiye ki task kaise accomplish karna hai. Game-playing programs aur temperature control ke programs iske popular examples hain.

Model training, evaluation aur tuning

ML model ko production environment mein deploy karne se pehle use train, evaluate aur test karna hota hai. ML model ko train karna ek process hai jisme stored data instances ko ML model (algorithm) mein input ke roop mein feed kiya jaata hai. Har stored data instance ki ek specific characteristic hoti hai — umbrella examples ki different types, prices, regions sold, aur aise hi — aur in data instances ke patterns hundreds of variables use karke detect kiye ja sakte hain, aur algorithm is tarah training data se seekh kar data ke basis par generalized prediction bana sakta hai.

  • Validation dataset: tum data ka ek sample hold out karte ho, jise validation dataset kaha jaata hai. Validation set measure karta hai ki model unseen ya naye data par kitna achha generalize karta hai. Training error yeh determine karne ke liye use hoti hai ki model data ko kitna achha fit karta hai, kyunki model usi par train hota hai.
  • Evaluation metrics: model evaluation metrics aise choose ya define karne chahiye jo problem ya business goals ke saath align karein. Model tuning se model performance improve honi chahiye, jaisa evaluation metrics se measure hota hai. Example — December ke month mein umbrella sales ke predictions kitne accurate the? Kya in predictions ko future forecasting efforts ke liye generalize kiya ja sakta hai?
  • Satisfactory performance: satisfactory performance kya hai, yeh business needs se dictate hona chahiye aur kisi bhi ML engagement ko start karne se pehle is par agreement hona chahiye.
  • Overfitting: validation set yeh determine karne ke liye bhi use hota hai ki model overfitting to nahi kar raha. Overfitting Chapter 8 mein discuss kiya gaya hai.

Model testing — unseen data par check

Bina model ko test kiye yeh jaan ne ka koi tareeka nahi hai ki tumhara umbrella prediction app future forecasting efforts ke liye generalize ho sakta hai ya nahi. Jab training dataset model ko data par fit karne ke liye use ho jaata hai, aur validation dataset model accuracy improve karne ke liye use ho jaata hai, to tum model ko aise data par test karte ho jo usne pehle kabhi nahi dekha. Testing data model performance assess karne ke liye use hota hai.

Example ke liye, maan lo tum ek application banana chahte ho jo umbrellas ki images ke basis par umbrella ka color ya pattern recognize kar sake. Tum model ko train karte ho, use umbrellas ki images dekar, jinme se har ek ko ek certain color ya pattern ke saath tag kiya gaya hai. Tum us model ko ek mobile application mein use karte ho kisi bhi umbrella ka color ya pattern recognize karne ke liye. Test yeh hoga ki model umbrella colors aur patterns ko differentiate karne mein kitna achha perform karta hai.

Training, validation aur testing datasets ka relationship 5 process steps mein dikhaya gaya hai. Simplicity ke liye Step 5 mein dataset ki taraf jaane wala arrow nahi dikhaya gaya, kyunki jab model ek application ke roop mein deploy ho jaata hai aur data collect karna shuru kar deta hai, to naya data pipeline mein enter karta hai jo original model ke results ko skew kar sakta hai. Yahi par tum machine learning operations, ya MLOps, ke fascinating realm mein enter karte ho — jo is book ke scope se bahar hai.

Model deployment (serving)

Jab ML model train, evaluate aur test ho jaata hai, to use ek live production environment mein deploy kiya jaata hai jahan use kiya ja sakta hai. Jab tak model production tak pahunchta hai, uske paas zyada tar ek web app frontend hota hai (browser use karke) jo production system ke saath ek application programming interface (API) ke through communicate karta hai.

Data real time mein capture karke MLOps pipeline mein stream (ingest) kiya ja sakta hai. Ya data batch mein capture karke pipeline mein ingestion ke liye store kiya ja sakta hai. Ya dono.

Maintaining models — stale model aur data drift

Models stale ho sakte hain jab predictions original business goal ya use case metrics ke saath align nahi karte. Staleness tab ho sakti hai jab duniya badal jaati hai ya business requirements badal jaate hain. Yeh changes phir model ko impact karte hain.

Post-deployment, tumhe apne model ko monitor karna hota hai taaki yeh ensure ho ki woh expected tarike se perform karta rahe. Model aur data drift ek phenomenon hai jise tumhe expect bhi karna chahiye aur regular retraining se MLOps ke through mitigate karne ke liye prepared bhi rehna chahiye.

Data drift ka matlab hai tumhare training wale data aur web app se ab receive hone wale data ke beech ke changes. Umbrella example mein, ek region jahan pehle heavy rainfall hoti thi, ab drought conditions experience kar raha hai. Similarly, ek region jahan pehle drought tha, ab heavy rainfall experience kar raha hai. Weather aur climate se judi koi bhi prediction, aur umbrellas aur umbrella type ki need, impact hogi. Is scenario mein tumhe naye data ke saath ek naya model retrain aur test karna hoga.

Yaad rakho: Training, validation aur testing — teeno datasets ka kaam alag hai. Training se model seekhta hai, validation se tuning aur overfitting check hoti hai, aur testing se pata chalta hai ki model unseen data par kaise perform karega. Deployment ke baad bhi kaam khatm nahi hota — drift ke liye monitor karo aur zaroorat par retrain karo.

02Chapter 2 · Data Is the First Step

Data Is the First Step — 8 Project Case Studies

Data hi pehla step hai — is chapter mein tumhe book mein use hone wale use cases aur datasets ka overview milega, saath mein yeh bhi ki aage practice ke liye data sources kahan milenge, data types kya hain, aur batch aur streaming data mein kya farak hai.

Project-based approach — math-first nahi

Book tumhe ML math-first ya algorithm-first approach se nahi, project-based approach se sikhati hai. Chune gaye use cases tumhe actual, real-world data ke saath ML sikhane ke liye design kiye gaye hain, alag-alag sectors mein — healthcare, retail, energy, telecommunications aur finance. Customer churn wala use case kisi bhi sector par apply ho sakta hai.

Har use case project apne aap mein stand-alone hai, agar tumhe thoda data preprocessing experience hai — to tum apni zaroorat ke hisaab se aage skip karke wahi seekh sakte ho jo tumhe upskill karne ke liye chahiye.

8 use cases ek nazar mein

Book ke 8 sections, unke use case, sector aur coding type is tarah hain — Retail product pricing, Healthcare heart disease, Energy utility campaign, Insurance advertising media channel sales, Financial fraud detection, Energy power plant production prediction, Telecommunications customer churn prediction, aur Automotive used-car auction price improvement.

Is chapter mein tumhe data types ka difference bhi samajh aayega — quantitative aur qualitative, structured, semistructured aur unstructured, aur batch aur streaming. Tumhe Google ke free browser-based open source Jupyter Notebook se data preprocessing ki hands-on practice bhi milegi, aur chapter ke end mein GitHub use karke selected projects ke liye ek data repository banana bhi seekhoge.

Yaad rakho: Har project apne aap mein poora hai — tumhe book ko line-by-line follow karne ki zaroorat nahi hai. Jis skill ki tumhe zaroorat hai, us project par seedha jump karo.
Full code — Chapter 2 notebook (GitHub)

GitHub: maabel0712/low-code-ai — Chapter2/Chapter_2.ipynb

# Import Pandas
import pandas as pd

# Download "Heart Disease Mortality Data Among US Adults (35+) by
# State/Territory and County -- 2018-2020" dataset from CDC and load
# into a Pandas dataframe.

url = 'https://data.cdc.gov/api/views/jiwm-ppbh/rows.csv?accessType=DOWNLOAD'
heart_df = pd.read_csv(url, index_col=0)

# Use head() method to view first five rows of hear_df

heart_df.head()

# Use the info() method to see information for each column in the heart_df dataframe.

heart_df.info()

# upload the file to the Colab enviornment using the directions in Chapter 2. Please follow these
# directions your first time through this exercise as this code will be explained in Chapter 8.

!wget $url -O ./heart.csv

# Load downloaded CSV from CDC website into a Pandas Dataframe and view the first five lines.

heart_df = pd.read_csv('/content/heart.csv', error_bad_lines=False,
                       engine="python")

heart_df.head()

02.1Chapter 2 · Data Is the First Step

8 Use Cases aur Datasets — Retail se Automotive tak

Book ke 8 use cases 5 sectors ko cover karte hain aur no-code se lekar custom-code tak ka poora spectrum dikhate hain. Har use case mein tum ek role mein hote ho, ek real dataset ke saath, aur ek clear business goal ke saath.

1. Retail — Product Pricing (umbrella example)

Yeh use case decision making mein data ke role ko illustrate karne ke liye design kiya gaya hai. Tum ek umbrella banane wali company ke marketing in-charge ho, aur business goal hai sales badhana. Agar tum apne existing umbrellas ka selling price kam kar do, to kya tum predict kar sakte ho ki kitne umbrellas bikenge? Price reduction strategy ko impact karne wale data elements mein selling price ke alawa rainy seasons, population density aur inventory bhi aate hain.

2. Healthcare — Heart Disease Campaign

Isme tum ek healthcare consultant ho aur tumhe United States mein 35 saal se zyada age ki populations ke liye heart disease mortality par data diya gaya hai. Goal hai heart disease mortality data ko analyze karna aur heart disease prevention campaign mein ek possible use case suggest karna. Example ke liye, ek possible use case hoga heart disease mortality mein trends ko time ke saath track karna, ya heart disease mortality predict karne ke liye models develop aur validate karna.

Yeh dataset dirty hai — kuch fields mein missing values hain, aur ek field missing hai. In issues par kaam karte hue tum seekhte ho ki Python Jupyter Notebook mein data import kaise karte hain, use analyze kaise karte hain, aur dirty elements ko fix kaise karte hain. Yeh low-code data preprocessing wala project hai.

3. Energy — Utility Campaign

Isme tum ek utility company ke liye kaam karne wale business analyst ho. Tumhe ek marketing aur outreach program develop karna hai jo high electrical energy consumption wali communities ko target kare. Data already preprocessed hai. Tumhare paas ML background nahi hai aur koi programming knowledge nahi hai, isliye tum AutoML ko apna ML framework choose karte ho. Yeh no-code (AutoML) project hai.

4. Insurance — Advertising Media Channel Sales Prediction

Is section mein tum ek team par kaam karte ho jo ek insurance company ke liye media strategy develop kar rahi hai. Team ek ML model develop karna chahti hai jo various media channels mein advertising spend ke basis par sales predict kare. Tumhe exploratory data analysis perform karni hai aur model build aur train karna hai. Tumhare paas ML background nahi hai aur koi programming knowledge nahi hai, isliye tum AutoML choose karte ho. Yeh no-code (AutoML) project hai.

5. Financial — Fraud Detection

Tumhara goal ek model banana hai jo predict kare ki koi financial transaction fraudulent hai ya legitimate. Tumhari nayi company ek mobile payment service hai jo hundreds of thousands of users ko serve karti hai. Fraudulent transactions fairly rare hain aur usually dusri protections se catch ho jaate hain, lekin unfortunate truth yeh hai ki kuch slip ho jaate hain aur tumhare users ko negatively impact karte hain.

Is section ka dataset transaction data hai jo user behavior aur fraudulent transactions ko replicate karne ke liye simulate kiya gaya hai. Tumhare paas ML background nahi hai, isliye tum AutoML choose karte ho. Yeh no-code (AutoML) project hai.

6. Energy — Power Plant Production Prediction

Tumhara goal ek combined cycle power plant (CCPP) ke liye net hourly electrical energy output predict karna hai, plant ke paas ke weather conditions ke basis par. Is section ka dataset ek CCPP se 6-year period (2006–2011) mein collect kiye gaye data points contain karta hai, jab power plant full load par kaam karne ke liye set tha.

Data per hour aggregated hai, lekin recorded weather conditions aur energy production ke liye exact hour dataset mein supplied nahi hai. Practical viewpoint se iska matlab hai ki tum data ko sequence ya time-series data ke roop mein treat nahi kar paoge, jahan tum previous records ki information use karke future records predict karte ho. Tumhare paas databases se kaam karke Structured Query Language (SQL) ka kuch knowledge hai, isliye tum Google BigQuery Machine Learning ko apna ML framework choose karte ho. Yeh low-code (BigQuery ML) project hai.

7. Telecommunications — Customer Churn Prediction

Tumhara goal ek telecommunications company ke liye customer churn predict karna hai. Customer churn ko attrition rate ke roop mein define kiya gaya hai, ya dusre shabdon mein, un customers ki rate jo services use karna band karne ka choose karte hain. Telecom companies aksar apne products monthly rate ya annual contracts par bechti hain, to yahan churn ka matlab hoga jab customer agle month mein apna subscription ya contract cancel karta hai.

Dataset mein numeric variables aur categorical variables dono hain, jahan variable ek discrete set of possibilities mein se ek value leta hai. Tumhare paas kuch Python knowledge hai aur tumhe AutoML bohot powerful lagta hai, lekin tum low-code solutions seekhna chahte ho jo tumhe apne model par thoda zyada control dein. Tum scikit-learn aur Keras ko ML frameworks choose karte ho. Yeh low-code (scikit-learn aur Keras) project hai.

8. Automotive — Improve Custom Model Performance

Is project mein tum ek ML team ke naye member ke roop mein ek ML model ki performance improve karoge, jo used cars ki auction price predict karne ke liye train kiya gaya hai. Initial model scikit-learn mein ek linear regression model hai aur tumhare business goals ko bilkul meet nahi karta.

Tum ultimately scikit-learn, Keras aur BigQuery ML ke tools explore karoge apne model ki performance improve karne ke liye. Linear regression model ko train karne ke liye use hone wale training, validation aur testing datasets tumhe CSV files ke roop mein supply kiye gaye hain. Yeh datasets clean kar diye gaye hain (missing aur incorrect values ko appropriately remedy kiya gaya hai), aur scikit-learn linear regression model banane ke liye use kiya gaya code bhi provide kiya gaya hai. Yeh custom-code (scikit-learn, Keras, BigQuery ML) project hai.

Yaad rakho: No-code, low-code aur custom-code — teeno levels book mein hain. Tumhari coding background jo bhi ho, tumhare liye ek project hai — AutoML se shuru karo, phir BigQuery ML ya scikit-learn ki taraf badho.

02.2Chapter 2 · Data Is the First Step

Data Types — Quantitative, Qualitative, Structured, Unstructured

Data ko samajhna hi pehla step hai, isliye pehle basic terminology aur concepts clear kar lo. Agar tumhe quantitative aur qualitative data, structured, semistructured aur unstructured data, aur batch aur streaming data ka difference pehle se pata hai, to tum seedha GitHub aur Google Colab wale section par jump kar sakte ho.

Quantitative aur qualitative data

Data analysis mein tum do types ke data ke saath kaam karte ho — quantitative aur qualitative. Agar use count ya measure kiya ja sakta hai aur numerical value di ja sakti hai, to woh quantitative data hai. Quantitative data tumhe bata sakta hai how many, how much, ya how often — example ke liye, kitne logon ne product catalog dekhne ke liye website visit ki? Company ne is fiscal year mein kitna revenue banaya? Umbrella handles banane wali machines kitni baar break hoti hain?

Qualitative data ke opposite, qualitative data ko measure ya count nahi kiya ja sakta aur isme lagbhag koi bhi non-numerical data aa sakta hai. Yeh descriptive hota hai, numbers ki bajay language mein express kiya jaata hai. ML mein yeh distinction important kyun hai? Agar tumhare paas qualitative data hai, to tumhe use preprocess karna hoga taaki woh quantitative ban jaaye — kyunki tum qualitative data ko seedha ML model mein feed nahi kar sakte. Kuch qualitative data ko handle karna tum aane wale chapters mein seekhoge.

Structured, unstructured aur semistructured data

Data ko 3 buckets mein group kiya ja sakta hai — structured, unstructured aur semistructured.

  • Structured data: aisi information jo format aur transform karke ek well-defined data model mein daal di gayi hai. Data model data ko organize aur structure karne ka ek tareeka hai taaki use easily samjha aur manipulate kiya ja sake. Data models databases, software applications aur data warehouses jaise kai applications mein use hote hain. Structured data well organized hota hai. Chapter 4 ke Advertising Media Channel Sales Prediction use case ki schema mein column name aur column type hote hain — Digital, Newspaper, Radio aur TV, chaaro numeric (quantitative) columns, jo AutoML model mein feed hote hain. Structured data ke examples hain customer records, product inventory, financial data, transaction logs, website analytics data aur log files.
  • Unstructured data: aisa data jo structured ya tabular nahi hai, ya kisi specific tareeke se format nahi hai. Examples hain social media posts, chats (text), videos, photos, web pages aur audio files.
  • Semistructured data: ek type ka structured data jo structured aur unstructured ke beech mein aata hai. Iska tabular data model nahi hota, lekin isme records aur fields ke liye tags aur semantic markers ho sakte hain. Yeh essentially structured aur unstructured ka combination hai. Videos mein date ya location se related meta tags ho sakte hain, lekin unke andar ki information ka koi structure nahi hota. Examples hain CSV, XML, JSON files, HTML aur email. Emails semistructured maane jaate hain kyunki unme kuch structure hota hai, lekin structured data jitna nahi — email mein typically header, body aur attachments hote hain. Header mein sender, recipient aur message ki date ke baare mein information hoti hai, aur body mein message ka text hota hai.
Yaad rakho: ML model ko numbers chahiye hote hain. Qualitative ya categorical data ko pehle quantitative mein badalna padega — warna model use samajh hi nahi payega.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Data Is the First Step
← Previous02.1 · 8 Use Cases aur Datasets — Retail se Automotive tak→ Next02.3 · Data File Types aur Processing
02.3Chapter 2 · Data Is the First Step

Data File Types aur Processing

Data types samajhne ke baad ab file types aur processing modes ki baari hai. Har file format ka apna purpose hota hai, aur har processing mode ka apna use case — galat mode choose karne par ya to cost badhegi ya predictions late aayenge.

Common data file types

  • Text files: plain text contain karne wali files, typically documents jaise letters, reports aur code store karne ke liye use hoti hain. Common extensions hain .txt, .csv, .tsv, .log aur .json.
  • Spreadsheet files: tabular format mein data contain karne wali files, typically financial data, sales data aur dusra tabular data store karne ke liye use hoti hain. Common extensions hain .xls, .xlsx aur .csv.
  • Image files: images contain karne wali files, typically photos, graphics aur dusra visual content store karne ke liye use hoti hain. Common extensions hain .jpg, .png aur .gif.
  • Audio files: audio recordings contain karne wali files, typically music, podcasts aur dusra audio content store karne ke liye use hoti hain. Common extensions hain .mp3, .wav aur .ogg.
  • Video files: video recordings contain karne wali files, typically movies, TV shows aur dusra video content store karne ke liye use hoti hain. Common extensions hain .mp4, .avi aur .mov.
  • Webpage files: webpages contain karne wali files, typically HTML code, CSS code aur JavaScript code store karne ke liye use hoti hain. Common extensions hain .html, .htm aur .php.

Data kaise process hota hai — batch vs real-time

Data process karne ke 2 main modes hain — batch processing aur real-time processing. Batch processing mein data ek period of time mein collect kiya jaata hai aur phir baad mein process kiya jaata hai. Yeh large datasets ke liye common hai, kyunki data ko batches mein process karna real time mein process karne se zyada efficient ho sakta hai.

Real-time processing mein data jaise hi collect hota hai, waise hi process ho jaata hai. Yeh un applications ke liye common hai jahan data ko jaldi process karne ki zaroorat hoti hai, jaise fraud detection ya stock trading.

Frequency — continuous vs periodic

Data process karne ki frequency bhi vary kar sakti hai. Continuous processing mein data continuously process hota hai, jaise hi collect hota hai — yeh un applications ke liye common hai jahan data real time mein process karna hota hai. Periodic processing mein data regular intervals par process hota hai — yeh un applications ke liye common hai jahan data ko real time mein process karne ki zaroorat nahi hoti, jaise financial reporting.

  • Batch processing — intermittent: data collect karke baad mein process kiya jaata hai.
  • Real-time processing — continuous: data jaise hi collect hota hai, process ho jaata hai.
  • Periodic processing — intermittent: data regular intervals par process hota hai.

Mode aur frequency ka choice application ki specific needs par depend karta hai. Large datasets process karne wali application batch processing use kar sakti hai, jabki real time mein data process karne wali application real-time processing use kar sakti hai.

Batch data vs streaming data

Batch data aur streaming data 2 alag types ke data hain jo alag tareeke se process hote hain. Batch data woh data hai jo ek period of time mein collect kiya jaata hai aur phir baad mein process kiya jaata hai. Batch data ko process, store, analyze aur ML model mein feed karne se pehle batches mein collect karna padta hai.

Streaming data woh data hai jo receive hote hi process hota hai. Streaming data continuously flow karta hai aur generate hote hi process, store, analyze aur act kiya ja sakta hai. Streaming data kai different formats mein, distributed sources ki wide variety se aa sakta hai. Simple shabdon mein, streaming data woh data hai jo continuously aur real time mein generate hota hai.

Is type ke data ko aise ML models train karne ke liye use kiya ja sakta hai jo real time mein predictions bana sakte hain. Example ke liye, ek streaming data model fraud detect karne ya customer churn predict karne ke liye use ho sakta hai.

Yaad rakho: Batch matlab "collect karo, phir process karo" aur streaming matlab "aate hi process karo". Fraud detection jaise kaam mein streaming chahiye, financial reporting jaise kaam mein periodic batch kaafi hai.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Data Is the First Step
← Previous02.2 · Data Types — Quantitative, Qualitative, Structured, Unstructured→ Next02.4 · GitHub aur Google Colab — Apna Data Repository
02.4Chapter 2 · Data Is the First Step

GitHub aur Google Colab — Apna Data Repository

Ab hands-on time hai — GitHub par apna data repository banao aur Google Colab mein Jupyter Notebook se data ko import, validate aur explore karo. Na kuch install karna hai, na apne computer par Python setup karna hai.

GitHub se apne projects ke liye data repository banao

GitHub ek code repository hai jahan tum apne Jupyter notebooks aur experimental raw data free mein store kar sakte ho. GitHub repository tumhare datasets aur low-code project notebooks — jaise is book mein mention kiye gaye Jupyter Notebooks — ko hold kar sakti hai.

  1. GitHub account ke liye sign up karo: GitHub individuals aur organizations ke liye personal accounts offer karta hai. Jab tum personal account banate ho, to woh GitHub.com par tumhari identity ban jaata hai, aur tumhe account ke liye ek billing plan select karna hota hai.
  2. Project ka GitHub repo set up karo: repo ke liye ek short, memorable name type karo — example ke liye, low-code book projects. Description optional hai, lekin is exercise mein "Low-code AI book projects" enter karo. Repository visibility choose karo — is case mein default Public hai, matlab internet par koi bhi is repository ko dekh sakta hai.
  3. README.md banne do: GitHub se ek README.md file create karwao — yahan tum apne project ke liye lamba description likh sakte ho. Baaki defaults rakho — .gitignore se tum choose karte ho ki kaunsi files track nahi karni hain, aur license dusron ko batata hai ki woh tumhare code ke saath kya kar sakte hain aur kya nahi. Jab done ho, "Create repository" par click karo.

GitHub se collaboration kyun easy hoti hai

Colab se notebook save karne par woh GitHub mein Main branch ke under ek file ban jaati hai. GitHub mein file create karna collaboration improve karne ka ek great tareeka hai — isme kai features hain jo teams ko zyada effectively kaam karne mein help karte hain:

  • Version control: GitHub files mein changes track karta hai. Matlab jiske paas bhi file ka access hai, woh dekh sakta hai ki kaunse changes kiye gaye hain, aur zaroorat padne par previous version par revert kar sakta hai.
  • Pull requests: pull requests collaborators ko file mein changes propose karne deti hain. Isse sabko changes ko merge karne se pehle review karne ka chance milta hai.
  • Issues: issues bugs ya feature requests track karne ke liye use kiye ja sakte hain. Isse sab problems solve karne aur naye features add karne par collaborate kar sakte hain.
  • Comments: files par comments add kiye ja sakte hain feedback dene ya sawaal poochhne ke liye. Isse code par kaam karne ka ek zyada collaborative tareeka milta hai.

Google Colaboratory (Colab) — bina install kiye Python

Saalon pehle, agar tumhe Python seekhna hota, to tumhe Python interpreter download karke apne computer par install karna padta tha. Yeh beginners ke liye daunting task ho sakta tha, kyunki iske liye software install karne aur computer configure karne ka knowledge chahiye hota tha.

Aaj Python seekhne ke kai tareeke hain bina apne computer par kuch install kiye. Tum online IDEs (integrated development environments) use kar sakte ho jo tumhe web browser mein Python code likhne aur run karne dete hain, ya cloud-based Python environments use kar sakte ho jo tumhe Python interpreter aur saari zaroori libraries ka access dete hain.

  • No installation required: tum bina koi software download ya install kiye turant Python seekhna shuru kar sakte ho.
  • Access from anywhere: jab tak internet connection hai, tum kahin se bhi online aur cloud-based resources se Python seekh sakte ho.
  • Affordable: online aur cloud-based resources aksar free ya bohot affordable hote hain.
  • Easy to use: online aur cloud-based resources beginners ke liye bhi easy to use hone ke liye design kiye gaye hain.

Tum apna low-code Python Jupyter Notebook Google Colaboratory, ya Colab, se banate ho. Colab ek hosted Jupyter Notebook service hai jise use karne ke liye koi setup nahi chahiye, aur yeh computing resources ka access deti hai, jisme graphical processing units (GPUs) bhi shamil hain. Colab tumhare web browser mein chalta hai aur tumhe Python code likhne aur execute karne deta hai. Colab notebooks Google Drive mein store hote hain aur Google Docs ya Sheets ki tarah share kiye ja sakte hain. Google Colaboratory free hai, aur kisi account ke liye sign up karne ya koi subscription pay karne ki zaroorat nahi hai.

Colab mein notebook banao aur heart disease dataset import karo

Colab par jao aur ek naya Python Jupyter notebook create karo. Notebook ko title bar mein title do, table of contents expand karo, phir + Code button par click karke code hold karne ke liye ek cell add karo. + Text button se tum text add kar sakte ho, jaise documentation.

Code cell add karne ke baad tumhe zaroori libraries import karni hoti hain. Is simple example mein tum sirf Pandas import karoge — cell mein import pandas as pd type karo aur arrow par click karke run karo. Pandas library data analysis ke liye use hoti hai. pd Pandas ke liye ek shorthand name (alias) hai, jo convention se module aur submodule names ko shorten karne ke liye use hota hai.

Dataset data.gov website se hai — "Heart Disease Mortality Data Among US Adults" naam ka. File ko download karke import karne ke 2 tareeke hain — file ko desktop par download karo aur phir import karo, ya URL use karo. Yahan URL method use hota hai — Comma Separated Values File par click karo, URL copy karo, aur Colab notebook mein ek naye cell mein woh code type karke run karo jo URL ko Pandas DataFrame mein read karta hai. Pandas DataFrame ek two-dimensional data structure hai jo data ko table format mein store karta hai — spreadsheet jaisa.

  • heart_df.head(): DataFrame ki pehli 5 rows dikhata hai.
  • heart_df.info(): dataset ki information deta hai — columns ki sankhya, column labels, column data types, memory usage, range index, aur har column mein cells ki sankhya (non-null values). Output mein 15 string object columns (qualitative data) aur 4 numeric columns (quantitative data) dikhte hain. int64 ko decimal ke bina number samjho (example 25) aur float64 ko decimal wala number (25.5).

Data validation — URL wala file aur downloaded file match karte hain?

Best practice ke roop mein, koi bhi data jo tum URL se import karte ho, use validate karo — khaas karke agar tumhare paas compare karne ke liye CSV file format hai. Data.gov page se CSV file apne computer par download karo, phir use Colab notebook mein upload karo aur Pandas DataFrame mein read karo.

Upload karte waqt ek warning message aata hai — basically yeh kehta hai ki tum jo bhi file upload karoge, woh save nahi hogi agar runtime terminate ho jaata hai (jo ho sakta hai agar tum Colab close kar do). Runtime program ko woh environment provide karta hai jo use run karne ke liye chahiye hota hai.

File upload karne ke baad use rename karo — right-click karke heart.csv naam do. Phir file ka path copy karo, kyunki Pandas read_csv method mein parameter ke roop mein exact location input karni hogi. Code kuch is tarah hota hai: heart_df = pd.read_csv('/content/heart.csv', error_bad_lines=False, engine="python") aur phir heart_df.head().

Ab compare karo — URL se import kiye gaye DataFrame mein 19 columns the, aur uploaded file wale mein 20 columns hain. Matlab file upload karne se ek Year column add ho gaya. Year ka datatype numeric value nahi hai — usme numbers hain, lekin woh numbers calculate karne ke liye nahi, rank aur order karne ke liye hain. Year int64 ke roop mein dikh raha hai — yeh tumhare ML use case ke liye dirty data ka pehla case hai.

Dirty data — missing values aur galat data types

heart_df.isnull().sum() type karke run karo — kya koi null values hain? Null value woh value hai jo kisi value ki absence indicate karti hai. Tumhare paas dirty data ka dusra case hai — 3 columns mein null values hain. Missing values se deal karna tum aane wale chapter mein seekhoge.

  • Missing values: zyada tar algorithms missing values accept nahi karte. Jab dataset mein missing values dikhte hain, to rows ko bas "drop kar do" ki tendency ho sakti hai, lekin missing values handle karne ke 2 main approaches hain — deletion ya imputation. Deletion mein missing values wali rows ya columns remove kar dete hain. Imputation mein missing values ko estimates se fill karte hain — mean imputation (observed values ke mean se replace karna), median imputation (median se replace karna), mode imputation (sabse frequent value se replace karna), aur regression imputation (dusre variables ke observed values ke basis par regression model se missing values predict karna). Pandas blank space ko NaN (not a number) se fill karega, lekin hume use kisi na kisi tareeke se handle karna chahiye.
  • Data type incorrect: Year int64 data type ke roop mein dikh raha hai aur use string object hona chahiye — jahan tumhe use qualitative, categorical feature ke roop mein handle karna hoga.
  • Categorical columns: kaafi saare string object features hain — jo numeric nahi hain. Tum aisi values ko ML model mein feed nahi kar sakte. In features ko one-hot encoded karna hoga — yeh tum aane wale chapter mein dekhoge.

Features woh input data hain jo model ko train karne ke liye use hota hai. Model phir predictions banane ke liye features use karta hai. Feature selection tum aane wale chapter mein seekhoge.

Thoda sa exploratory data analysis (EDA)

Section conclude karne se pehle, data explore karne ke kuch simple tareeke dekh lo. Ek feature ke saare unique values dekhna chahte ho, jaise Stratification2? Ek naye cell mein heart_df.Stratification2.unique() type karke run karo.

Is feature ko visualize karne ke liye Seaborn ka violin plot use karo. Seaborn statistical graphics banane ke liye ek Python library hai. Is code mein Data_Value feature x ke roop mein aur Stratification2 y ke roop mein use hota hai. Data_Value feature har region aur group ke hisaab se heart disease ka count hai.

Violin plot mein "long tails" indicate karte hain ki us particular feature ke liye data mein zyada outliers hain. Violin body ka bada shape indicate karta hai ki race ke hisaab se kitne heart disease cases distributed hain. Seaborn ka violin plot numerical data ke distribution ko visualize karne ka ek achha tareeka hai — box plot ke opposite, jo sirf summary statistics dikha sakta hai, violin plots summary statistics aur har variable ki density dono depict karte hain.

Notebook ko GitHub par save karo

Ab apna notebook GitHub par save karo. Colab menu mein File > Save a copy in GitHub par click karo. Repository drop-down se repo select karo jisme notebook save karna hai. Branch ke under Notebooks select karo. Default "Include a link to Colaboratory" rakho — yeh GitHub mein ek link dikhayega jo tumhe notebook ko seedha GitHub se open karne deta hai. Colab notebook ko GitHub par copy karne ke baad tumhe seedha GitHub par le jaata hai, aur repo refresh karne par tumhe apna Colab Jupyter notebook dikhega.

Yaad rakho: Data import karne ke baad seedha model par mat jao — pehle validate karo ki file sahi aayi hai, phir .info() aur .isnull().sum() se dirty data dhoondho. Missing values, galat data types aur categorical columns — teeno ko handle karna hi preprocessing ki shuruaat hai.

← Previous02.3 · Data File Types aur Processing→ Next03 · Machine Learning Libraries aur Frameworks
03Chapter 3 · Machine Learning Libraries and Frameworks

Machine Learning Libraries aur Frameworks

ML model banana aur train karna typically mathematics, statistics aur ML ke underlying working principles samajhne ki maang karta hai. ML frameworks tumhari help karte hain, time-consuming ML workflow tasks jaise feature selection, algorithm selection, code writing, pipeline development, performance tuning aur model deployment ko automate karke.

3 levels — no-code, low-code aur full-code libraries

  • Noncoders ke liye: graphical user interface (GUI) wale automated no-code ML frameworks hain, jinse tum bina ek line code likhe ML model build aur train kar sakte ho.
  • Light coders ke liye: low-code ML frameworks hain jo sirf thoda sa code likh kar ML model build aur train karne ki ability dete hain.
  • Seasoned coders ke liye: ML libraries hain jo ML workflow ke har phase ko code karne ki flexibility aur control deti hain.

Is chapter mein tum AutoML, Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS), low-code aur SQL ML frameworks, aur open source ML libraries ke baare mein seekhoge — aur samjhoge ki kaunsa tool kis level ke coder ke liye sahi hai.

Yaad rakho: Framework ka kaam tumhara time bachana hai, tumhari samajh replace karna nahi. No-code se shuru karo, lekin andar kya ho raha hai, yeh samajhna bhi utna hi zaroori hai.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Machine Learning Libraries and Frameworks
← Previous02.4 · GitHub aur Google Colab — Apna Data Repository→ Next03.1 · No-Code AutoML — Kaise Kaam Karta Hai
03.1Chapter 3 · Machine Learning Libraries and Frameworks

No-Code AutoML — Kaise Kaam Karta Hai

Imagine karo tum ek utility company ke liye kaam karne wale business analyst ho. Tumhara project hai company ko marketing aur outreach programs develop karne mein help karna, jo high electrical energy consumption wali communities ko target karein. Data comma separated value (CSV) file format mein hai, aur tumhare paas ML background ya programming knowledge nahi hai — phir bhi team lead ne tumhe yeh project diya hai kyunki tumhe ML mein interest hai.

Use case — total kWh predict karna

Data aur use case ke basis par tum determine karte ho ki tumhara target multiple variables ke basis par total kilowatt-hours (kWh) predict karna hai — zip code, month, year, aur customer class (Residential, Commercial, Industrial aur Agricultural).

Agar tumhe jaldi ek baseline prediction chahiye, to yeh AutoML ke liye ek excellent use case hai. GUI-based AutoML framework use karne mein sabse easy hai. Example mein Google Vertex AI use hota hai, jo ek ML platform hai jo tumhe ML models build, deploy aur scale karne mein help karta hai. Overall, Google AutoML, Microsoft Azure AutoML aur AWS SageMaker AutoML — teeno powerful AutoML solutions hain jo bina code likhe ML models build aur deploy karne mein help kar sakte hain. Tumhare liye best solution tumhari specific needs aur requirements par depend karega.

Vertex AI workflow — step by step

File format CSV hai, isliye tum Tabular tab select karte ho. Total kWh output hai aur woh numeric value hai jise tum predict karna chahte ho, to tum note karte ho ki yeh ek regression task hai — aur kyunki multiple variables ke liye column names (labels) hain, isliye yeh ek supervised ML problem hai. Bina labels wale data ke liye unsupervised ML task chahiye hota hai, jaise clustering.

Vertex AI tabular data ke liye ye model types create karne deta hai:

  • Binary classification models: ye models binary outcome predict karte hain (2 classes mein se ek). Yes ya no wale sawaalon ke liye is type ka use karo.
  • Multi-class classification models: ye models 3 ya zyada discrete classes mein se ek class predict karte hain. Categorization ke liye is type ka use karo.
  • Regression models: ye models continuous value predict karte hain. Sales predict karne ke liye is type ka use karo.
  • Forecasting models: ye models values ki ek sequence predict karte hain. Daily demand forecast karne ke liye is type ka use karo.

Kuch frameworks data load hone ke baad statistics generate karte hain. Dusre frameworks manually data clean karne ki zaroorat kam karne mein help karte hain, missing values, anomalous values aur duplicate rows aur columns ko automatically detect aur clean karke. Data load hone ke baad use review karke missing values check karne aur data statistics dekhne jaise kuch additional steps bhi tum employ kar sakte ho.

Data statistics aur categorical features

Google Vertex AI framework se generate ki gayi tumhare energy utility dataset ki statistics mein koi missing values nahi hain, aur har column ke liye distinct values ki sankhya dikhayi gayi hai. Example ke liye, 145 zip codes hain. Kyunki zip code ek number hai, Transformation column use "Numeric" ke roop mein dikhata hai. Lekin zip code ek categorical feature hai, kyunki har zip code dusre se alag hai aur isliye use apni khud ki "category" mein daala ja sakta hai. ZipCode ko numeric se categorical mein badalna drop-down se transformation customize karke select karne jitna easy hai.

AutoML har feature ka data profile present karta hai. Zip code 92694 sabse common feature hai, jo indicate karta hai ki us zip code area mein zyada customers rehte hain. Tum is information ko apne marketing campaigns ke liye leverage kar sakte ho. Far right column mein tum training ke liye include karne ke liye kisi feature ko select ya deselect bhi kar sakte ho.

Model train karna aur results dekhna

Step 3 mein tum kuch training parameters select karke ek naya model train karte ho. Vertex AI ka "Train new model" window tumhe training method, model details, training options aur compute aur pricing select karne deta hai. Dataset aur objective (Regression) inputs ke roop mein "Training method" parameter mein dikhaye jaate hain. AutoML default se select hota hai. Saare parameters enter karne ke baad tum training job start karte ho.

Training mein kai ghante tak lag sakte hain, tumhare data ke size aur tumhare choose kiye gaye model objective ke type par depend karke. Image aur video data types ko process karne mein structured data type jaise CSV file se zyada time lag sakta hai. Training samples ki sankhya bhi training time ko impact karti hai. AutoML training time intensive bhi hai, AutoML ke kaam karne ke nature ki wajah se.

Training ke baad model training results present kiye jaate hain. Ab tum apne preliminary findings team ko present kar sakte ho, next steps se pehle — jinme aur experimentation ya model ko web page ke roop mein deploy karna shamil ho sakta hai, jahan user customer class aur zip code select karta hai aur predicted total kWh dikhaya jaata hai.

  • Model feature attribution: yeh batata hai ki har feature ne model training ko kitna impact kiya. Attribution values percentage ke roop mein express ki jaati hain — percentage jitni zyada, correlation utna strong, matlab us feature ne model training ko utna zyada impact kiya. Model feature attribution sampled Shapley method use karke express ki jaati hai.
  • Model metadata: isme model ke baare mein kai information dikhti hai — model ID, date created, training time, use kiya gaya dataset, target column, data splitting percentage allocation, aur use kiya gaya model evaluation metric — is case mein root mean squared error (RMSE). "Model" ya "Trials" par click karke tum retrieve kar sakte ho ki AutoML ne kaunsa model use kiya hai.

Tumhe kya-kya nahi karna pada — yahi AutoML ki power hai

Utility marketing outreach project ke workflow mein phases 2, 3 aur 4 mein koi coding nahi chahiye thi. Samjho tumne kya nahi karna pada:

  • Environment setup nahi: Python Jupyter Notebook run karne ke liye environment set up nahi karna pada, koi software libraries install nahi karni padi — install karne ke liye kuch tha hi nahi.
  • Data load aur split ka code nahi: CSV data file Vertex AI mein upload karne ke baad file cloud mein store ho gayi. Python aur Pandas use karne par dataset load karne ya dataset ko training, validation aur testing files mein split karne ke liye code likhne ki zaroorat nahi padi.
  • One-hot encoding ka code nahi: data clean tha, lekin 2 categorical features the — zip code aur customer class. Agar tumne in 2 features ke liye code kiya hota, to tumhe har ek ko one-hot encode karna padta. One-hot encoding categorical data variables ko numerical values mein convert karne ka process hai. Sample code mein from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder use karke zip code feature ko encode kiya jaata hai. One-hot encoding feature transformation ya engineering ka ek example hai. Tumhe target (output) select karne ya features ko deselect karne — ya drop karne — ki ability bhi easily mili, bina aisa code likhe jo Pandas DataFrame se "id" column drop karta hai.
  • Neural network ka code nahi: dataset mein zyada features hone se zyada complex relationships banti hain jo nonlinear ho sakti hain. Neural networks nonlinear relationships ke saath kaam karne ke liye perfect hain. Yeh prediction problem hai kyunki tum jaanna chahte the ki average kWh, customer class, month, year aur zip code ke basis par future total kWh predict kiya ja sakta hai ya nahi. Thoda deeper theory mein, yeh use case input features ki sankhya ki wajah se complex mana ja sakta hai — isme multiple variables hain aur yeh multivariate hai. Is type ke complex relationships nonlinear maane jaate hain kyunki tum known total kWh aur dusre multiple variables ke beech "best fit" wali ek seedhi line simply draw nahi kar sakte. Yeh dataset neural network ke liye ek excellent candidate hai. Ek typical neural network mein input layer, hidden layers aur output layer hote hain. Python mein neural network code karna mushkil hai — Network class, weight matrices, neurons, learning rate — sab kuch manually define karna padta hai. Keras se coding kuch easy ho jaati hai — Sequential() model, Dense layers aur Activation('relu') se — lekin phir bhi layers, neurons, activation functions aur optimizers samajhne padte hain.
  • Regression algorithm choose nahi karna pada: regression analysis ki kai types hain, aur har method ka use kai factors par depend karta hai — target variable ka type, regression line ka shape, aur independent variables ki sankhya. Linear regression, logistic regression, ridge regression, lasso regression, polynomial regression aur Bayesian linear regression jaise types hain.
  • Classical ML vs neural networks samajhna nahi pada: commonly use hone wale neural-network building blocks jaise layers, neurons (nodes), objectives, activation functions ya optimizers ko samajhne ki zaroorat nahi padi.
  • Training process ya model optimization strategies samajhna nahi pada: training ke dauraan AutoML sirf model weights ko hi nahi, architecture ko bhi optimize karne par focus karta hai. Appropriate architecture select karna AutoML karta hai.
  • Compute resources specify nahi karne pade: jab tumne "one node" choose kiya, to AutoML ne sahi machine type select kar liya.
Yaad rakho: AutoML tumhara kaam isliye easy karta hai kyunki woh model selection, training, tuning aur evaluation metrics — sab kuch sambhal leta hai. Tumhara kaam sirf itna hai — sahi target choose karo, features ko sahi type do (jaise zip code ko categorical), aur results ko business goal se compare karo.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Machine Learning Libraries and Frameworks
← Previous03 · Machine Learning Libraries aur Frameworks→ Next03.2 · Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS)
03.2Chapter 3 · Machine Learning Libraries and Frameworks

Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS)

AutoML cloud providers ke machine learning as a service (MLaaS) platform ka hissa hai. Top 3 cloud providers hain Google, Amazon aur Microsoft. MLaaS ka matlab hai poora ML workflow — training se lekar deployment aur monitoring tak — cloud par managed service ke roop mein milna.

Cloud platform pyramid — IaaS, PaaS, SaaS

Cloud architecture ko ek pyramid ke roop mein samjho:

  • Bottom layer — IaaS (infrastructure as a service): is layer ko hardware aur storage layer samjho, jahan customers cloud provider ke servers use karte hain actual computation aur storage services handle karne ke liye — dataset files, models, containers aur aise hi cheezein store karne ke liye.
  • Middle layer — PaaS (platform as a service): is layer ko platform samjho (operating systems jaise Linux ya Windows) jise customers apna khud ka software run karne ke liye use karte hain.
  • Top layer — SaaS (software as a service): iska best example AutoML hai — tumhe server configure nahi karna hai ya code nahi likhna hai, tum bas browser kholte ho aur use karte ho.

Google, Amazon aur Microsoft poore ML workflow ko support karne ke liye services offer karte hain, jisme ML learning algorithm training aur tuning, data visualization, data preprocessing aur deep learning shamil hain. Woh scikit-learn, Keras, TensorFlow aur PyTorch jaise frameworks use karne ke liye managed Jupyter Notebooks bhi provide karte hain.

MLaaS ke benefits

  • Data extraction aur exploration: Jupyter Notebook ya kuch cases mein cloud provider ke apne data visualization tools use karke dataset extract aur clean karo. Data transformations aur feature engineering apply karo, aur data ko training, validation aur test sets mein split karo. GUI tool ya Jupyter Notebook use karke data explore aur visualize karo.
  • Model training: tabular, image, text aur video data ke liye AutoML use karo — automatic featurization aur algorithm selection. Shared notebooks, compute resources, data aur environments. PyTorch, TensorFlow ya scikit-learn jaise open source platforms se custom training. Hyperparameters optimize karo. Different techniques use karke different model versions run karke experiment karo aur results compare karo. Multinode distributed training offer karo.
  • Distributed training: multinode distributed training se bade models ko fast train karo.
  • Model evaluation aur iteration: evaluation metrics provide karo taaki tum apne data mein adjustments kar sako aur apne model par iterate kar sako.
  • Model explainability: samjho ki har feature model prediction mein kaise contribute karta hai (feature attribution).
  • Model serving: apne model ko production mein deploy karo aur predictions lo.
  • Model monitoring: deployed model ki performance ko training-serving skew aur prediction drift ke liye monitor karo, aur jab incoming prediction data training baseline se zyada skew ho jaaye to alerts bhejo.

Businesses mein AutoML kaise use ho raha hai

  • Telecom: AutoML telecom companies mein customer churn prediction, fraud detection aur network optimization improve karne ke liye use ho raha hai.
  • Manufacturing: AutoML manufacturing companies mein product quality improve karne, production processes optimize karne aur equipment failure predict karne ke liye use ho raha hai.
  • Retail: AutoML retailers mein customer experiences personalize karne, products recommend karne aur inventory levels optimize karne ke liye use ho raha hai.
  • Healthcare: AutoML healthcare companies mein diseases diagnose karne, patient outcomes predict karne aur treatment plans personalize karne ke liye use ho raha hai.

Yeh sirf kuch examples hain ki AutoML businesses mein aaj kaise use ho raha hai. Jaise-jaise AutoML technology mature hoti jaayegi, AutoML ke aur bhi innovative applications dekhne ki expectation rakho.

AutoML ke 4 bade benefits

  • Improved accuracy: AutoML businesses aur organizations ko zyada accurate ML models banane mein help kar sakta hai, kyunki AutoML ek human data scientist se zyada wide range ke algorithms aur hyperparameters ke saath experiment kar sakta hai.
  • Democratized ML: AutoML ML ko nonexperts ke liye zyada accessible banata hai, kyunki AutoML ML models build aur deploy karne ke liye ek simple, user-friendly interface provide karta hai.
  • Reduced time to market: AutoML businesses aur organizations ko apne ML models jaldi up aur running karne mein help kar sakta hai, kyunki AutoML data cleaning, feature engineering aur model training jaise time-consuming tasks ko automate karta hai.
  • Reduced risk: AutoML businesses aur organizations ko biased ya inaccurate ML models banane ke risk ko kam karne mein help kar sakta hai, kyunki AutoML model validation aur testing mein involve steps mein se kai ko automate karta hai.

Teeno bade solutions ke interfaces alag hain, lekin idea same hai — Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Azure ML Studio aur Amazon SageMaker AutoML — teeno mein tum dataset upload karte ho, target select karte ho, aur model train karke results dekhte ho.

Yaad rakho: MLaaS ka matlab hai tum infrastructure ki tension chhodo aur ML par focus karo. IaaS hardware deta hai, PaaS platform deta hai, aur SaaS (jaise AutoML) ready-to-use software deta hai — tumhe sirf browser chahiye.
