03.3Chapter 3 · Machine Learning Libraries and Frameworks

Low-Code aur SQL ML Frameworks

Low-code AutoML mein libraries ki installation aur configuration chahiye hoti hai, plus Python ka kuch knowledge ya Structured Query Language (SQL) ka kuch knowledge. Low-code ka matlab hai thoda code likh kar zyada kaam karwana.

Low-code kya hai — definition

Is book mein low-code ko is tarah define kiya gaya hai:

  • Abstraction layer wale ML frameworks: aise ML frameworks jo existing ML framework ke upar ek "abstraction layer" provide karte hain.
  • SQL se ML karne wale databases: aise databases jo tumhe SQL use karke ML models run karne dete hain, ya aise databases jo tumhe Python code run karne dete hain jisme ML code shamil hai.

Examples mein cloud providers (SQL) ki taraf Google BigQuery, Amazon Aurora aur Redshift, aur Microsoft Azure SQL Server aate hain. Open source ki taraf AutoKeras, Auto-sklearn aur Auto-PyTorch aate hain.

SQL ML frameworks — SQL jaante ho to ML bhi kar sakte ho

Data analysts aur data scientists typically data analysis ke liye SQL use karte hain. Woh apne existing SQL skills aur expertise ko leverage karke ML par apply kar sakte hain — bina kisi ML programming background ke. Agar woh SQL jaante hain lekin Python, Java ya R mein code nahi kar sakte, to woh apne ML projects ke liye SQL-ML framework ke andar kaam kar sakte hain. Isi liye SQL-ML frameworks ko low-code mana jaata hai — zyada SQL coding ki zaroorat nahi hoti.

Databases ya data warehouses ko SQL-ML ke liye use karne ke benefits:

  • Large datasets ke saath model building: jab tum ML model wahi build kar sakte ho jahan data "rehta" hai, to ML SQL code data ke "paas" rehta hai aur latency (data transmission times) kam ho jaati hai. Yeh khaas karke large datasets ke liye deep learning use karne par crucial hai, jahan training mein data ke ek percentage ke through training, validation aur testing ke liye iteration chahiye hoti hai.
  • Backend integration with existing ML systems: cloud provider ke backend ML framework ke saath integrate karo (example ke liye, Google Vertex AI, Amazon SageMaker aur Microsoft Azure).
  • Common model build statements: sab CREATE MODEL SQL command use karte hain aur training data ko table ya SELECT statement ke roop mein specify karte hain. Phir woh trained model ko data warehouse ke andar compile aur import karte hain aur ek SQL inference function prepare karte hain jo SQL queries mein turant use kiya ja sakta hai.
  • Use cases: typical use cases mein fraud detection, product recommendations aur ad targeting shamil hain, low-latency, real-time requirements ki wajah se.

Database data ya information ka ek collection hai. Database term commonly database ko bhi refer karta hai aur database management system (DBMS) ko bhi. Data warehouses alag-alag sources se current aur historical data ki badi amounts store karte hain.

Google BigQuery ML

Google BigQuery ek data warehouse hai. Yeh apne ML tool se predictive analytics ke through decision-making guidance provide kar sakta hai. Tum BigQuery se data export kiye bina hi model create aur train kar sakte ho. Vertex AI ki tarah, BigQuery ML mein environment aur dependency setup ki zaroorat nahi hoti. BigQuery ML browser-based aur serverless hai, matlab use run karne ke liye tumhe server ki zaroorat nahi hai. Agar tumhara data pehle se BigQuery ke data warehouse mein hai, to tum use apne ML projects ke liye use kar sakte ho.

Amazon Aurora ML aur Redshift ML

Amazon Aurora ek relational database management system (RDBMS) hai jo cloud ke liye bana hai, full MySQL aur PostgreSQL compatibility ke saath. Amazon Aurora ML tumhe SQL use karke applications mein ML-based predictions add karne deta hai. Jab tum ek ML query run karte ho, to Aurora wide variety ke ML algorithms ke liye Amazon SageMaker ko call karta hai.

Redshift ML ek data warehouse hai. Tum SQL statements use karke Redshift data se Amazon SageMaker ML models create aur train karte ho, aur phir in models ko predictions banane ke liye use karte ho. Redshift ML model ko Redshift data warehouse ke andar ek SQL function ke roop mein available banata hai.

Yaad rakho: Agar tum SQL jaante ho to tumhe Python seekhne ka wait nahi karna hai — BigQuery ML, Aurora ML ya Redshift ML mein CREATE MODEL se seedha model banao, jahan data rehta hai wahi model banao, taaki data ko idhar-udhar move na karna pade.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Machine Learning Libraries and Frameworks
← Previous03.2 · Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS)→ Next03.4 · Open Source ML Libraries
03.4Chapter 3 · Machine Learning Libraries and Frameworks

Open Source ML Libraries

Open source AutoML ka matlab hai AutoKeras, Auto-sklearn aur Auto-PyTorch jaise open source frameworks, jo existing open source libraries ke upar ek additional layer of abstraction add karte hain. Yahan tumhe thoda code likhna padta hai, lekin AutoML phir bhi kaafi heavy lifting sambhal leta hai.

Open source AutoML ke 8 steps

Typically, Jupyter notebook use karke tumhe ye code karna hoga:

  1. Install the AutoML package: package install karo.
  2. Import the package: package import karo.
  3. Load a dataset: dataset load karo.
  4. Split the data: data ko split karo.
  5. Fit the model: model fit karo.
  6. Predict: predict karo.
  7. Evaluate: evaluate karo.
  8. Export the model: model export karo.

Step 4 ke baad, har open source framework ka model fit, prediction aur evaluation karne ka apna tareeka hota hai. Pehle 4 steps — install, import, load aur split — sab frameworks mein lagbhag same hote hain.

AutoKeras

AutoKeras, ek Keras-based open source AutoML framework, nonexperts ko minimal code ke saath jaldi neural networks build karne ke liye develop kiya gaya tha. AutoKeras use karte waqt tumhe sirf training data specify karna hota hai, aur AutoKeras data preprocessing independently perform karta hai.

Example ke liye, agar data mein categorical variables hain, to woh use one-hot encoding mein convert karega, depend karke ki yeh classification task hai ya regression task. Agar input data mein text hai, to AutoKeras use embedding mein transform karta hai.

Auto-sklearn

Auto-sklearn ek open source Python package hai jo scikit-learn ML library par based hai. Auto-sklearn ek naye ML dataset ke liye sahi learning algorithm automatically search karta hai aur uske hyperparameters optimize karta hai. Yeh framework sirf sklearn-based models support karta hai.

Auto-PyTorch

Auto-sklearn ke alawa, usi AutoML group ne PyTorch par based ek AutoML bhi develop kiya jo deep learning par focus karta hai. Auto-PyTorch rapid prototyping mein excellent mana jaata hai. Yeh distributed training bhi support karta hai.

Kaun kiske liye sahi hai

  • AutoKeras: neural networks chahiye aur minimal code se kaam karna hai — Keras ke upar bana hai.
  • Auto-sklearn: scikit-learn models chahiye aur algorithm selection plus hyperparameter optimization automatic chahiye.
  • Auto-PyTorch: deep learning par focus hai, rapid prototyping karni hai, ya distributed training chahiye.

Business analysts, data analysts, citizen data scientists, data scientists, software developers aur ML engineers — sab AutoML frameworks use karke development process ko streamline kar sakte hain. Pehle tum ek dataset load karte ho jisme target variable aur predictions ke liye use hone wala input feature data shamil hai. Data load hone ke baad, har data column ke liye ek data profile generate hota hai. Training job submit karne ke liye tum sirf kuch parameters select karte ho. AutoML phir multiple models ke saath experiment karta hai aur model optimization perform karta hai. Results present kiye jaate hain, saath mein feature attribution bhi.

Cloud vendors MLaaS provide karte hain taaki day-to-day ML workflows accelerate aur automate ho sakein, models ko applications ya services mein integrate karne ke tools mil sakein, aur models ko production mein deploy karne ke tools mil sakein.

Yaad rakho: Open source AutoML mein pehle 4 steps tumhare hain — install, import, load, split — uske baad framework fit, predict aur evaluate sambhalta hai. AutoKeras neural networks ke liye, Auto-sklearn scikit-learn models ke liye, aur Auto-PyTorch deep learning aur rapid prototyping ke liye hai.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Machine Learning Libraries and Frameworks
← Previous03.3 · Low-Code aur SQL ML Frameworks→ Next04 · AutoML se Advertising Media Channel Sales Predict Karna
04Chapter 4 · Use AutoML to Predict Advertising Media Channel Sales

AutoML se Advertising Media Channel Sales Predict Karna

Is chapter me tum ek AutoML model banate ho jo advertising media channel sales ko predict karta hai — matlab, alag-alag channels par kharcha karne se kitni sales hogi. Pehle tum data ko Pandas se explore karte ho, phir Vertex AI me no-code model train karte ho, uski performance check karte ho, aur aakhir me usse predictions lete ho.

Business use case — media channel sales prediction

Businesses apne products, services ya brand ko promote karne ke liye advertising media channels use karte hain — digital, TV, radio aur newspaper. Is scenario me tum ek midsize solar energy company ke marketing department me media planner ho.

Company ka media budget modest hai, aur use ye samajhna hai ki kaunsa channel sabse zyada fayda deta hai sabse kam cost par. Ye ek spend optimization problem hai.

  • Kaam kya hai: agle saal ki product sales badhane ke liye ek marketing plan banana hai, aur iske liye ye samajhna hai ki har media channel ke advertising budget ka overall sales par kya impact padta hai.
  • Normally ye kaam kisko milta: data scientist ya data analyst ko. Lekin is baar team lead ne tumse — jiske paas coding experience nahi hai — AutoML se sales predictive model banane ko kaha hai, jo team pehli baar try kar rahi hai.
  • Model ka goal: har media channel par kharch ki gayi rakam ke basis par kitni sales volume generate hogi, ye predict karna.

Paाँच business questions jo model se answer karne hain

  1. Kya model predict kar sakta hai ki har media channel par kharch ke basis par kitni sales volume generate hogi?
  2. Advertising budget aur sales ke beech koi relationship hai ya nahi?
  3. Kaunsa media channel sales me sabse zyada contribute karta hai?
  4. Kya model ko future sales forecast karne ke liye use kiya ja sakta hai, proposed budget ke basis par?
  5. Model future sales ko kitni accurately predict kar sakta hai?

Ye ek simple regression problem hai, sirf paाँच variables ke saath — chaar media channels (digital, TV, radio, newspaper) aur sales. Regression ka matlab hai ek continuous value — yahan ek number, sales — predict karna, koi label ya category nahi.

Project workflow

Workflow Chapter 3 wala typical AutoML no-code workflow hai: pehle data extraction aur analysis, phir dataset ko AutoML platform me upload karna, phir advertising budgets ko model me feed karna, phir AutoML results ko evaluate karna, aur aakhir me model ko deploy karke predictions lena.

Ek important baat — is workflow me data preprocessing ka step nahi hai. Is chapter ka dataset pehle se clean hai, aur preprocessing ka hands-on experience tumhe baad wale chapters me milega.

Is chapter ke hands-on exercise ke baad tum apni team ke liye ek strategic marketing plan bana sakoge — kaunse channel par kitna kharch karna hai, iska data-driven jawab tumhare paas hoga.

Yaad rakho: Regression tab use karo jab tumhe ek number predict karna ho — jaise sales. Classification tab use hota hai jab tumhe ek label predict karna ho — jaise spam ya not spam. Is chapter me target sales hai, isliye ye regression hai.

04.1Chapter 4 · Use AutoML to Predict Advertising Media Channel Sales

Dataset Explore Karna — Pandas, Matplotlib, Seaborn

Model banane se pehle data ko samajhna zaroori hai. Is section me tum advertising dataset ko Google Colab me Pandas se load karte ho, uski basic checks karte ho, aur Matplotlib aur Seaborn se uske patterns dekhte ho.

Dataset kya hai

Dataset ka naam advertising_2023 hai. Ye historical marketing channel data hai — alag-alag markets me har channel par kitna kharch hua aur kitni sales hui.

  • 1,200 markets: original dataset me 200 markets the, is book ke liye badha kar 1,200 kar diye gaye hain, aur ek digital variable bhi add kiya gaya hai.
  • Paाँच columns, sab numeric: Digital (digital ads par kharch), Newspaper, Radio, TV — ye chaaro advertising budgets hain, thousands of dollars me — aur Sales (total media channel sales, thousands of units me).
  • Data pehle se clean hai: isme koi missing values ya strange characters nahi hain. Tumhara kaam sirf ye validate karna hai ki data clean hai, aur variables ke beech relationships explore karna hai.
  • CSV file se load hota hai: data pehle CSV file me diya gaya hai, isliye use Pandas me load karna padta hai.

Colab me data load karna

Pehle Google Colab me naya notebook kholo aur use meaningful naam do, jaise Advertising_Model.ipynb. Phir packages import karo:

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats
import seaborn as sns
%matplotlib inline

Phir CSV ko seedha internet se DataFrame me load karo, download kiye bina:

url = "https://github.com/maabel0712/low-code-ai/blob/main/advertising_2023.csv?raw=true"
advertising_df = pd.read_csv(url, index_col=0)

advertising_df.head() se pehli paाँच rows dekho — isse tumhe features, unki possible values, aur ye pata chalta hai ki wo numeric hain ya nahi.

Descriptive analysis — data check karna

  • advertising_df.info(): columns ki sankhya, column labels, data types, memory usage, range index aur har column me non-null values ki sankhya batata hai. Isse check karo ki Pandas ne jo types infer kiye hain, wo Table 4-1 ke expected types se match karte hain ya nahi.
  • advertising_df.describe(): har numeric variable ki summary statistics — mean, maximum, minimum aur standard deviation — dikhata hai.
  • advertising_df.isnull().sum(): har column me null values ginata hai. Is dataset me output har column ke liye zero hai — matlab koi null values nahi hain.

Heat map — correlation dekhna

Heat map data ko colours se dikhane ka tareeka hai. Correlation ek statistical measure hai jo batata hai ki do ya zyada variables kis had tak saath-saath move karte hain.

plt.figure(figsize=(10,5))
sns.heatmap(advertising_df.corr(), annot=True, vmin=0, vmax=1, cmap='viridis')
  • Correlation coefficient 0 ka matlab hai koi relationship nahi; 1 ka matlab perfect positive relationship; -1 ka matlab perfect negative relationship.
  • Sales aur TV ka correlation 0.78 hai — sabse strong. Uske baad sales aur radio ka 0.58 hai.
  • Sales aur newspaper ka correlation sirf 0.23 hai — sabse weak. Ye hint deta hai ki newspaper ko model me feature ke roop me include karna chahiye ya nahi, ye sochna padega.
  • Multicollinearity: jab regression model me do ya zyada predictor variables aapas me highly correlated hote hain. Example ke liye, agar TV aur radio dono highly correlated hote (value 0.7 se zyada), to multicollinearity hoti. Asliyat me TV aur radio ka correlation sirf 0.056 hai, isliye yahan ye problem nahi hai. Multicollinearity me algorithm ke liye ye decide karna mushkil ho jata hai ki kis predictor ka sales par kitna weight hai.

Scatterplots — do variables ke beech relationship

Scatterplots do numeric variables ke beech relationship dikhate hain, aur outliers detect karne me bhi help karte hain. advertising_df.plot(kind='scatter', x=['digital'], y='sales') se digital aur sales ka scatter banta hai.

Saare features ko ek hi plot me sales ke against dikhane ke liye loop use hota hai, jisme har feature par ek regression line (laal rang me) bhi banayi jati hai. Result ye hai:

  • TV aur sales ka strong linear relationship hai — TV budget badhne par sales volume par positive impact dikhta hai.
  • Newspaper aur sales ke beech strong relationship nahi dikhta — ye correlation value 0.23 se match karta hai, TV wale 0.78 se bilkul alag.

Histogram — distribution dekhna

Histogram ek bar plot hai jisme target variable ko discrete bins me baanta jata hai, aur har bin me observations ki count bar ki height se dikhayi jati hai.

  • Sales ka histogram kuch had tak bell curve jaisa hai, thoda left-skewed. Sabse common sales amount $11,000 hai.
  • Baaki features: digital left-skewed dikhta hai, aur TV, radio aur newspaper normally distributed nahi hain. Features ko model me daalne se pehle standardize karke normally distributed banana behtar results dega — lekin ye transformations Chapter 7 me cover hote hain, is chapter ke scope se bahar hain.

Dataset export karna

Explore karne ke baad file ko export karo taaki use AutoML me upload kiya ja sake:

import os
if not os.path.isdir("/content/data"):
    os.makedirs("/content/data")
advertising_df.to_csv('/content/data/advertising.csv', encoding='utf-8', index=False)

Phir !head /content/data/advertising.csv se verify karo ki file sahi export hui hai, aur file par right-click karke Download select karo. Ab tum AutoML ke liye ready ho.

Yaad rakho: ML ka zyada kaam data ko samajhne aur prepare karne me jata hai, model train karne me nahi — kyunki model banana to AutoML sambhal leta hai. EDA se tumhe pehle hi pata chal gaya tha ki TV sabse strong hai aur newspaper sabse weak — aur aage model ke results yehi confirm karenge.

04.2Chapter 4 · Use AutoML to Predict Advertising Media Channel Sales

Vertex AI me No-Code Linear Regression Model

Ab tum Google ke Vertex AI me code likhe bina — sirf clicks se — linear regression model banate ho. Vertex AI Google ka GUI-based AutoML aur custom training framework hai. Google, Microsoft aur AWS — teeno bade cloud vendors AutoML offer karte hain, aur kai vendors trial period bhi dete hain.

Managed dataset banana

  • Vertex AI API on karo: Dashboard par "Enable All Recommended APIs" button se API enable karo, phir left navigation se Datasets select karo.
  • Dataset ka naam: Create button dabao aur dataset ka naam do, jaise advertising_automl. Default region us-central1 hi rakho.
  • Model objective select karo: Tabular tab ke under Regression/classification select karo — kyunki tumhe ek target column (sales) ki value predict karni hai.

Regression kya hai

Regression ek supervised ML process hai. Ye classification jaisa hi hai, lekin label predict karne ke bajay tum ek continuous value predict karte ho. Linear regression target variable (y) aur predictive features (x) ke beech ka relationship define karta hai.

  • Number predict karna ho to regression use karo: yahan linear regression sales ki real value predict karta hai, independent variables digital, TV, radio aur newspaper ke basis par.
  • Best-fit line: linear regression maan kar chalta hai ki har feature ke saath linear relationship hai. Predicted values line par data points hote hain, aur true values scatterplot me hote hain. Goal hai best fitting line dhoondhna, taaki naye data aane par model predict kar sake ki naya data point line ke relative kahan hoga.

Data upload karna

Dataset banane ke baad data add karo. Data source ke options hain: apne computer se CSV upload karo, Cloud Storage se CSV select karo, ya BigQuery se table ya view select karo. Yahan "Upload CSV files from your computer" select karke advertising.csv upload karo.

Phir Cloud Storage path select karna padta hai — file ko ek cloud storage bucket me store karna hota hai. Do reasons hain: (1) bade-scale ML training me terabytes ya petabytes data store karna pad sakta hai; (2) cloud storage buckets scalable, reliable aur secure hote hain.

  • Generate Statistics: data load hone ke baad statistics generate hoti hain. Is dataset me koi missing values nahi hain, aur har column ke distinct values ki sankhya dikhayi jati hai.
  • Feature profile: kisi feature ke naam par click karke uska distribution histogram dekh sakte ho. Sales feature ka mean 14.014 hai — jo describe() se mile value ke bahut kareeb hai.

Training model banana — chaar steps

Training jobs and models section me "Train New Model" select karo, aur "Other" chuno — AutoML on Pipelines nahi, wo is book ke scope se bahar hai. Train new model window me chaar steps hain:

  1. Step 1 — Training method: Objective dropdown se Regression chuno, aur Model training method me AutoML select karo. Continue dabao.
  2. Step 2 — Model details: model ka naam aur description do, aur Target column dropdown se sales select karo. Continue dabao.
  3. Step 3 — Training options: training options review karo. Standardization jaise data transformations automatically handle ho jate hain. Continue dabao.
  4. Step 4 — Compute and pricing: Budget field me maximum node hours ke liye 3 enter karo — ye sirf ek estimate hai. Tum sirf use kiye gaye compute hours ke liye pay karte ho; agar training kisi user-initiated cancellation ke alawa kisi aur reason se fail hoti hai, to tumhe bill nahi milta. Agar tum cancel karte ho, to training time ka charge lagta hai.
  • Early stopping: agar ye option enable hai, to training tab khatm ho jayegi jab AutoML decide kare ki ab aur model improvement nahi ho sakta. Agar disable hai, to AutoML budget hours khatm hone tak train karega.
  • Training time: training me kai ghante lag sakte hain, data ke size aur model objective ke type par depend karta hai. Image aur video data types ko structured data jaise CSV se zyada time lagta hai. Training samples ki sankhya bhi training time ko affect karti hai.
  • AutoML time-intensive kyun hai: AutoML algorithms bahut saare alag-alag models aur hyperparameters try karte hain, har model ko poore dataset par train karna padta hai, phir holdout dataset par har model ki performance evaluate karke best model select karna padta hai — ye sab computationally expensive hai.

Saare parameters enter karne ke baad Start Training dabao. Training ke baad model model registry me register ho jata hai.

Yaad rakho: Vertex AI me dataset banate waqt tum ek initial objective pick karte ho, lekin dataset banne ke baad use alag objectives ke saath models train karne ke liye bhi use kar sakte ho. Managed datasets tabular, image, text aur video data types ke liye available hote hain.

04.3Chapter 4 · Use AutoML to Predict Advertising Media Channel Sales

Model Evaluation aur Feature Importance

Model train hone ke baad sabse important sawaal ye hai — model kitna achha hai? Is section me tum paाँच regression evaluation metrics samajhte ho aur dekhte ho ki kaunsa media channel model ke liye sabse important tha.

Kaunsa metric kab important hai

Metric ki importance teen cheezon par depend karti hai:

  • Model ka purpose: agar model predictions karne ke liye hai, to MSE ya RMSE jaise metrics par focus karo. Agar model variables ke beech relationship samajhne ke liye hai, to R-squared ya adjusted R-squared par focus karo.
  • Data ki characteristics: agar data noisy hai (unwanted information ya errors hain), to MAE jaise noise-robust metrics par focus karo. Agar data noisy nahi hai, to MSE jaise zyada sensitive metrics use kar sakte ho.
  • Practitioner ki preference: kuch log easy-to-understand metrics pasand karte hain, kuch zyada accurate metrics. Koi ek sahi jawab nahi hai — jo metrics tumhare liye sabse important hain, unhe chuno.

Common linear regression evaluation metrics

  • R-squared (R2): model data ko kitni achhi tarah fit karta hai, ye measure karta hai. Ye observed aur predicted values ke beech Pearson correlation coefficient ka square hai. Range 0 se 1 tak hai — zyada value ka matlab behtar fit. Tumhara R2 lagbhag 0.997 hona chahiye.
  • Adjusted R-squared: R-squared ka modified version hai jo independent variables ki sankhya ko account me leta hai. Zyada value ka matlab behtar fit, lekin ye R-squared se kam sensitive hota hai independent variables ki sankhya ke prati.
  • Mean squared error (MSE): predicted values aur actual values ke beech average squared error. Kam MSE ka matlab behtar fit.
  • Root mean squared error (RMSE): MSE ka square root — MSE ka zyada interpretable version. Kam RMSE ka matlab behtar fit, aur 0 ka matlab model ne koi error nahi kiya. RMSE ko interpret karna series ki values ke range par depend karta hai. Tumhara RMSE lagbhag 0.345 hona chahiye.
  • Root mean squared log error (RMSLE): RMSE se outliers ke prati kam responsive hota hai, aur underestimations ko overestimations se thoda zyada penalize karta hai. Tumhara RMSLE lagbhag 0.026 hona chahiye.
  • Mean absolute error (MAE): predicted aur actual values ke beech average absolute error. Kam MAE ka matlab behtar fit. Tumhara MAE lagbhag 0.304 hona chahiye.
  • Mean absolute percentage error (MAPE): range 0% se 100% tak, kam value ka matlab zyada quality wala model. Ye absolute percentage errors ka average hai. Tumhara MAPE lagbhag 2.28 hona chahiye.

Model feature importance (attribution)

Model feature importance batata hai ki har feature ne model training ko kitna impact kiya. Attribution values percentage me express ki jati hain — jitni zyada percentage, utna hi strong correlation, matlab us feature ne training ko utna zyada impact kiya.

  • Newspaper ka contribution sirf 0.2% hai — ye EDA phase ki discovery ko support karta hai ki sales aur newspaper advertising spend ke beech relationship sabse weak hai.
  • Radio, digital aur TV sales me sabse zyada contribute karte hain, aur newspaper advertisements ka sales par bahut kam effect hai.
  • Yehi wajah hai ki feature importance check karna stakeholders aur debugging dono ke liye useful hai — tum dekh sakte ho ki model ne kya seekha, aur kya wo tumhari EDA findings se match karta hai.
Yaad rakho: R2 0.997 ka matlab hai model data ko bahut achhi tarah fit karta hai, lekin koi bhi single metric poori kahani nahi batata. RMSE, MAE aur MAPE ko saath me dekho — aur hamesha ye bhi check karo ki feature importance tumhari domain understanding se match karti hai ya nahi.

04.4Chapter 4 · Use AutoML to Predict Advertising Media Channel Sales

Model se Predictions Lena

Model train aur evaluate karne ke baad use deploy karna padta hai, taaki dusre log use karke inferencing kar sakein — matlab naye data par predictions le sakein. Is section me tum model ko endpoint par deploy karte ho aur test prediction lete ho.

Endpoint aur deployment kya hote hain

  • Endpoint ek service hai jo model ko online prediction ke liye expose karti hai — ek HTTPS path jahan clients input data bhej kar trained model ki inferencing (scoring) output pa sakte hain. Endpoints typically real-time predictions ke liye use hote hain.
  • Deployment model ko endpoint ke roop me available banane ka process hai — jaise production environment me deploy karna taaki customers ya employees use kar sakein.

Deploy karne ke chaar steps — is chapter me pehle do hi chahiye

  1. Endpoint define karo.
  2. Model settings configure karo.
  3. Model monitoring configure karo — is exercise ke liye zaroori nahi hai, aur monitoring logging ka extra charge bhi add karta hai.
  4. Model objectives configure karo — is exercise ke liye zaroori nahi hai.

Model Registry me jao, Deploy and Test select karo, aur apna model chuno. Step 1 me endpoint define karo — region select karo aur decide karo ki endpoint kaise access hoga. Step 2 me model add karo aur traffic split add karo.

Traffic split kya hai

Traffic split Vertex AI me ek tareeka hai ek hi endpoint par deploy kiye gaye multiple models ke beech traffic distribute karne ka. Iske uses hain:

  • A/B testing: alag-alag models ko test karke dekhna ki kaunsa behtar perform karta hai.
  • Canary deployments: naye model ko pehle chhote percentage users par deploy karna, taaki koi problem ho to wo zyada users ko affect karne se pehle pakdi jaye.
  • Rollouts: naye model ko users tak gradually roll out karna, taaki kisi problem ka impact kam ho.

Compute resources aur settings

Step 3 me chuno ki kaunse compute resources predictions serve karenge. Is exercise ke liye minimum number of compute nodes use karo, aur Machine type me Standard select karo. Machine types teen cheezon me differ karte hain: (1) per node vCPUs ki sankhya, (2) per node memory ki amount, (3) pricing.

  • Compute resources chunte waqt kya dekho: model ka size aur complexity, kitni predictions karni hain, latency requirements (real-time ya bahut low latency chahiye ya nahi), aur cost.
  • CPUs sabse common compute resource hain — jo models bahut bade ya complex nahi hain, unke liye achhe hain. GPUs CPUs se zyada powerful hote hain aur bade complex models ki training aur inference speed up kar sakte hain. TPUs ML workloads ke liye designed specialized hardware accelerators hain — sabse powerful option.
  • Logging enable mat karo is exercise me — endpoint logging enable karne par charges lagte hain.
  • Explainability options: inka koi charge nahi hai. "Enable feature attributions for this model" ko check karo.
  • Model monitoring: is project ke liye enable mat karo.

Saari configurations ke baad Deploy button highlight ho jayega. Deploy dabao. Endpoint create hone aur model deploy hone ke baad tumhe deployment status ke baare me email milega.

Model ko test karna — prediction aur prediction interval

Predictions lene ke liye: Model Registry me jao, apna model select karo, uska version select karo, aur neeche scroll karke "Test your model" page par jao. Media channel values input karo aur Predict button dabao.

  • Prediction value 14.63: sales prediction result 14.63 hai — jo sales histogram aur feature profile ke mean (14.014) ke bahut kareeb hai.
  • Prediction interval 13.58 se 15.53: ye values ki range hai jisme model ko 95% confidence hai ki actual result hoga. Matlab, tum 95% certain ho sakte ho ki koi bhi prediction result is range ke andar hoga.
  • Prediction interval vs confidence interval: confidence interval past ya current events par focus karta hai aur ek population parameter (jaise mean ya standard deviation) estimate karne ke liye use hota hai. Prediction interval ek future observation ki value predict karne ke liye use hota hai — ek single naye observation ki value kis range me ho sakti hai, ye batata hai. Prediction intervals confidence intervals se wider hote hain, kyunki ye ek individual value predict karne ki uncertainty ko account karte hain, population parameter ki nahi.
  • Prediction intervals decisions me help karte hain: jaise company decide kar sakti hai ki naye product ya service me invest kare ya nahi, ya advertising media channel budget badhaye ya ghataaye.

Business questions ke jawab

  • Kya model sales volume predict kar sakta hai? Haan. Vertex AI me har media channel ki values input karke future budget allocation ke decisions liye ja sakte hain — jaise results ke basis par digital channel ka budget badhana.
  • Advertising spend aur sales ke beech relationship hai? Haan. Digital, TV aur radio ke liye positive linear relationship hai. Newspaper spend ka sales se weak relationship hai.
  • Kaunsa channel sabse zyada contribute karta hai? TV — EDA ke scatterplots aur Vertex AI ke feature attribution bar chart, dono se ye pata chalta hai.
  • Model future sales kitni accurately predict kar sakta hai? Regression model input values par prediction value aur prediction interval return karta hai — 95% certainty ke saath future sales prediction is range me hoga.

Important: chapter khatm hone ke baad model ko undeploy karna mat bhoolo. Deployed models cost incur karte hain jab wo use me nahi bhi hote, kyunki wo hamesha quick predictions return karne ke liye available rehte hain. Undeploy karne ke liye Vertex AI Endpoints me jao, endpoint name par click karo, "More actions" three-dot menu par click karo, aur "Undeploy model from endpoint" select karo.

Yaad rakho: Model banana sirf aadhi kahani hai — use deploy karke predictions lena aur un predictions ko business decisions me use karna hi asli goal hai. Aur deployed model ko kaam khatm hone par undeploy karna ek cost-saving habit hai jo har project me follow karni chahiye.

05Chapter 5 · Using AutoML to Detect Fraudulent Transactions

AutoML se Fraudulent Transactions Detect Karna

Is chapter me tum ek Vertex AI AutoML model banate ho jo predict karta hai ki koi financial transaction fraudulent hai ya nahi. Pehle tum dataset ko Google Colab me clean aur explore karte ho, phir Vertex AI me managed dataset banate ho, aur phir AutoML se ek classification model train karte ho.

Business use case — fraud detection

Tumhari nayi company ek mobile payment service hai jo hundreds of thousands of users ko serve karti hai. Fraudulent transactions fairly rare hain aur usually dusri protections se pakde jate hain — lekin kuch transactions cracks se slip ho jate hain aur users ko negatively impact karte hain.

  • Problem: company baad me in transactions ko rectify kar sakti hai, lekin darr hai ki users ko ye transactions report karni padti hain, isliye customers kho sakte hain.
  • Goal: machine learning se ek bespoke model bana kar company ke fraud-detection software ko improve karna.
  • Normally ye kaam kisko milta: data scientist ko, jo koi advanced model jaise autoencoder banata. Lekin tumhe ek quick benchmark model banana hai jise fraud-detection system ke baaki parts ko prototype karne ke liye use kiya ja sake. Ye model engineering team ke liye starting point hoga — aur ho sakta hai ki yehi model production me bhi chala jaye.

Complicating factor — highly unbalanced dataset

Dataset highly unbalanced hai — vast majority transactions legitimate hain. Iska matlab ye hai ki ek simple model jo predict kare ki saari transactions legitimate hain, wo equally accurate hoga — aur bilkul useless bhi.

  • Sirf 0.129% transactions fraudulent hain — lagbhag har 800 me se 1 transaction. Isliye accuracy alone tumhe model ki performance ke baare me galat picture de sakti hai.
  • Isliye dusre metrics chahiye: accuracy ke saath precision, recall, F1 aur ROC/AUC jaise metrics use karne padenge, taaki model ki performance ko sahi tarike se samjha ja sake.

Project workflow aur dataset

Overall workflow Chapter 4 jaisa hi hai — data extraction aur analysis, phir dataset ko AutoML platform me upload karna, features ko model me feed karna, AutoML results evaluate karna, aur phir model deploy karke predictions lena. Isliye is chapter me kai jagah details concise hain — agar kahin atak jao, to Chapter 4 wapas dekh lo.

  • Dataset simulated hai: transaction data ko PaySim naam ke open source tool se simulate karke user behavior aur fraudulent transactions ko replicate kiya gaya hai. Financial transaction data ko real users ki information expose kiye bina use karna mushkil hota hai, isliye simulated data use kiya gaya hai.
  • Representative data: company ke data analysts ne confirm kiya hai ki ye dataset distribution me company ke real application data ke bahut similar hai, isliye tum maan kar chal sakte ho ki ye prediction time par use hone wale real-world data ko represent karta hai.
  • 10 columns, CSV file: dataset Google Cloud Storage me CSV file ke roop me diya gaya hai, aur BigQuery me ek table ke roop me bhi available hai.
Yaad rakho: Fraud detection ek classification problem hai — output ek category hai (fraudulent ya legitimate), ek number nahi. Aur jab ek class bahut rare ho, to accuracy dekh kar khush hona sabse badi galti hai — purana model 99% se zyada accurate tha, lekin fraud pakadne me lagbhag bilkul fail tha.
Full code — Chapter 5 notebook (GitHub)

GitHub: maabel0712/low-code-ai — chapter5/Fraud_Detection.ipynb

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns


%matplotlib inline

url = 'https://storage.googleapis.com/low-code-ai-book/financial_transactions.csv'

transaction_df = pd.read_csv(url)

transaction_df.head()

transaction_df.info()

transaction_df.describe()

cols = ['type', 'nameOrig', 'nameDest']
transaction_df[cols].describe()

transaction_df['isCorrect'] = (transaction_df['isFraud']==transaction_df['isFlaggedFraud'])
transaction_df['isCorrect'].sum()

(transaction_df['isFraud']*transaction_df['isCorrect']).sum()

transaction_df.groupby('type')['isFraud'].mean().plot.bar()

transaction_df.groupby('type')['isFraud'].value_counts()

                        duplicates='drop')

transaction_df.groupby('newbalanceOrigBkts')['isFraud'].mean().plot.bar()

                                              duplicates='drop')

cashout_df = transaction_df.query("type == 'CASH_OUT' & newbalanceDest < 1e8")

05.1Chapter 5 · Using AutoML to Detect Fraudulent Transactions

Fraud Dataset — Explore aur Export

Model train karne se pehle tum fraud dataset ko Colab me explore karte ho — kitna data hai, kaunse columns hain, fraud kitna rare hai, aur kaunse features fraud se related lagte hain. Ye exploration hi tumhe batayega ki AutoML ko kaunse features dene hain.

Dataset schema — 10 columns

  • step (Integer): simulated data generate hone ke baad se kitne hours hue hain.
  • type (String): transaction ka type — paाँच unique values hain.
  • amount (Float): transaction ki amount.
  • nameOrig (String): transaction originate karne wale customer ka anonymized naam.
  • oldbalanceOrg / newbalanceOrig (Float): originator ka transaction se pehle aur baad ka balance.
  • nameDest (String): destination account ke owner ka anonymized naam.
  • oldbalanceDest / newbalanceDest (Float): destination account ka transaction se pehle aur baad ka balance.
  • isFraud (Integer): 1 agar transaction fraudulent thi, 0 otherwise — ye tumhara target (label) hai.

Colab me data load karna

Notebook ka naam do, jaise Fraud_Detection_Model.ipynb, packages import karo, aur CSV ko seedha DataFrame me load karo:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
%matplotlib inline

url = ('https://storage.googleapis.com/' +
       'low-code-ai-book/financial_transactions.csv')
transaction_df = pd.read_csv(url)

transaction_df.head() se pehli paाँच rows dekho. Do cheezein turant notice karne layak hain:

  • step column sab rows me 1 hai — kyunki data step ke ascending order me sorted hai, sirf pehli paाँच rows dekh kar ye clear nahi hota.
  • PAYMENT ya TRANSFER type par oldbalanceDest aur newbalanceDest dono zero hain — ye coincidence bhi ho sakta hai, lekin explore karne layak pattern hai.
  • Ek extra column hai — isFlaggedFraud — jo original schema me nahi tha. Ye pichle model ki prediction ka output tha ki transaction legitimate hai ya fraudulent. Ye tumhare model ke liye ek bura feature hoga, kyunki prediction time par tumhare paas isFlaggedFraud nahi hoga — ideally ye us model se aa raha hai jise tum naye aur behtar model deploy hone ke baad deprecate kar doge. Lekin ye discovery useful hai: purane model ko benchmark ke roop me use karke tum check kar sakte ho ki tumhara naya model improvement dikhata hai ya nahi.

Descriptive analysis — kitna data hai, fraud kitna rare hai

  • transaction_df.info(): 6,362,620 rows aur 11 columns hain. Data types expected types se match karte hain (Pandas me String ke liye object type dikhta hai).
  • transaction_df.describe(): count dekh kar lagta hai koi null values nahi hain. step field 1 se 743 tak fairly uniformly vary karti hai. amount aur balance columns bahut bade range me vary karte hain — financial transactions ke liye ye expected hai.
  • isFraud ka mean 0.129% hai: 0 aur 1 values wale field ka mean us proportion ke barabar hota hai jo 1 ke equal hain. Matlab sirf lagbhag 0.129% transactions fraudulent thi — har 800 me se lagbhag 1. Total fraudulent transactions 8,213 thi.
  • Categorical columns: describe() sirf numeric features ki statistics deta hai. type, nameOrig aur nameDest ke liye alag se transaction_df[cols].describe() chalao. type ke paाँच unique values hain, lekin nameOrig ke 6,353,307 unique values hain 6,362,620 transactions me — lagbhag one-to-one relationship. Aisa feature jo lagbhag har row ko identify karta ho, achha feature nahi hota, kyunki model sirf usi value ko dekhne lag sakta hai aur features ke beech complex relationships seekhna band kar dega. nameDest ke liye ye risk kam hai, lekin unique values ki badi sankhya ke kaaran phir bhi risk hai.

Purana model kitna achha tha — accuracy ka dhokha

Ek naya column isCorrect banao — 1 agar isFraud aur isFlaggedFraud same hain, 0 otherwise — aur ginno ki purana model kitni baar sahi tha:

transaction_df['isCorrect'] = (
    transaction_df['isFraud'] == transaction_df['isFlaggedFraud']
)
transaction_df['isCorrect'].sum()
  • Result 6,354,423 hai — total 6,362,620 rows me se. Matlab 99.87% transactions correctly flagged thi. Purana model bahut achha lagta hai, hai na?
  • Lekin fraud me se kitne pakde? (transaction_df['isFraud'] * transaction_df['isCorrect']).sum() se pata chalta hai ki sirf 16 fraudulent transactions correctly flag hui thi — total 8,213 me se. Matlab sirf 0.19% fraudulent transactions successfully flag hui.
  • Ye recall hai: overall accuracy bahut achhi dikhne ke bawjood, model relevant sawaal — kitne fraud pakde gaye — par bahut kharab tha. isFlaggedFraud column me flagged fraudulent transactions ki sankhya actual fraudulent transactions se lagbhag double thi — ye buri baat nahi hai, kyunki tum fraud pakadna chahte ho aur kuch extra legitimate transactions check karna chhoti keemat hai. Lekin agar bahut zyada extra transactions flag kar do, to legitimate transactions explore karne me time aur resources waste honge.

Exploratory analysis — fraud kahan milta hai

  • Transaction type ke hisaab se fraud: transaction_df.groupby('type')['isFraud'].mean().plot.bar() se pata chalta hai ki sirf do transaction types me fraudulent transactions hain — CASH_OUT (4,116 fraud) aur TRANSFER (4,097 fraud). CASH_IN, DEBIT aur PAYMENT me zero fraud hai. Ye bahut useful feature ho sakta hai — lekin agar naye types ki fraudulent transactions aane lagi, to model unhe miss kar dega kyunki usne aisa example kabhi dekha hi nahi. Isliye transaction types ko time ke saath monitor karna aur zaroorat padne par model retrain karna important hai.
  • Bucketization: numeric variable ko value ranges ya "buckets" me baantna aur har bucket me fraud ka percentage dekhna. pd.qcut(transaction_df['amount'], 10) amount ko 10 buckets (deciles) me baant ta hai — pehla bucket 0th se 10th percentile tak, dusra 10th se 20th percentile tak, aur aise hi aage. Result: transaction amount jitni badi, fraud ki likelihood utni zyada — khaas taur par 90th percentile se upar amount wali transactions me fraudulent transaction rate me sevenfold jump dikhta hai.
  • oldbalanceOrg: generally, originator account me old balance jitna zyada, fraud ka chance utna zyada — lekin sirf ek point tak; 90th se 100th percentile bucket me fraud ka chance phir kam ho jata hai. duplicates='drop' argument duplicate buckets ko merge kar deta hai — yahan oldbalanceOrg ka 30th percentile 0 hai, isliye pehle teen buckets identical hote aur merge ho jate hain.
  • Scatterplot — CASH_OUT: oldbalanceDest vs newbalanceDest ko isFraud se colour karke plot karne par ek region dikhta hai jahan fraudulent transactions zyada hain. Ye cross-correlation ka sign hai — aisa relationship jo feature crossing se capture kiya ja sakta hai. Feature crossing do ya zyada preexisting categorical features ko concatenate karke synthetic features banane ka process hai, jo AutoML feature selection aur engineering ke part ke roop me use karega.

Dataset export karna

Explore karne ke baad DataFrame ko CSV me export karo:

transaction_df.to_csv('transactions.csv', encoding='utf-8', index=False)

!head transactions.csv se contents check karo, aur Colab se download karne ke liye from google.colab import files aur files.download('transactions.csv') use karo. Ek warning — Colab programmatically files download kar sakta hai, isliye koi bhi notebook run karne se pehle uska code carefully padh lo, taaki tumhari machine par koi unexpected ya malicious file download na ho.

Note karo ki data pehle se Google Cloud Storage me CSV file me aur BigQuery me table ke roop me stored hai, isliye agle section ke liye tumhe exported dataset load karne ki zaroorat nahi hai.

Yaad rakho: nameOrig aur nameDest jaise near-unique identifier columns ko model me feature ke roop me dena risky hai. Behtar approach ho sakta hai unhe Boolean column me transform karna — True agar value ek se zyada baar repeat hui ho, False otherwise — lekin ye sahi hai ya nahi, ye domain experts se poochh kar aur alag transformations experiment karke verify karna chahiye.

05.2Chapter 5 · Using AutoML to Detect Fraudulent Transactions

Classification Models aur Metrics

Model train karne se pehle ye samajh lo ki classification models kya hote hain aur unhe sahi tarike se kaise evaluate karte hain. Fraud jaise unbalanced problem me galat metric chunna tumhe ye lagne de sakta hai ki model achha hai, jabki wo fraud pakad hi nahi raha.

Classification model kya hai

Classification model ek categorical output return karta hai — jaise cat, dog, fish, ya fraudulent. Tum pehle se jante ho ki kin classes ko distinguish karna hai. Yahan classes 0 aur 1 hain — legitimate aur fraudulent transactions.

  • Models probabilities return karte hain: practice me classification models predicted class nahi, balki har possible class ki probability return karte hain. Usually predicted class simply sabse likely class hoti hai.
  • Threshold ek business decision hai: binary classification me tum decide karte ho ki kis probability se upar transaction ko fraudulent classify karna hai. Agar tum sirf tab fraud kaho jab fraud ki chance 50% se zyada ho, to tum fraud ke cases miss kar sakte ho. Agar threshold bahut low rakho — jaise 5% — to tum bahut saari transactions ko fraudulent flag kar doge aur unhe explore karne me bahut resources kharch honge. Threshold kahan rakhna hai, ye modeling problem bhi hai aur business problem bhi.

Accuracy — useful lekin kaafi nahi

Accuracy ek simple aur easy-to-understand metric hai jo classification models ke liye commonly use hoti hai. Lekin tum pehle hi iska khatra dekh chuke ho — purana model 99% se zyada accurate tha, lekin barely koi fraudulent transactions pakad paya.

Ye issues tab aate hain jab classes unbalanced hoti hain — matlab ek class dusri classes se bahut zyada common hoti hai. Yahan sirf 0.129% transactions fraudulent thi, fraudulent aur legitimate ka ratio lagbhag 1:800 hai. Aise scenario me accuracy jaise metrics se issues easily mask ho jate hain. Fraud detection jaise cases me, jahan positive class bahut rare hai, accuracy akele unreliable ho jati hai.

Recall aur precision

  • Recall (true positive rate): fraudulent transactions ka wo percentage jo model successfully predict karta hai. Purane model ka recall sirf 0.19% tha — 8,213 me se sirf 16 fraud pakde gaye. Agar tumhara goal fraudulent transactions ko proactively flag karke review karwana hai, to recall bahut important metric hai. Tum thodi accuracy ya precision sacrifice karke recall improve karne ke liye taiyaar rahoge.
  • Precision: model jab positive case predict karta hai, to uske sahi hone ki probability — matlab predicted fraudulent transactions ka wo percentage jo waqai fraudulent thi. Precision batata hai ki tum kitni baar sahi the jab tumne fraud kaha.
  • Trade-off: positive class ke liye lower threshold rakhne se zyada false positives aur kam false negatives honge — matlab kam precision aur zyada recall. Higher threshold rakhne se zyada false negatives aur kam false positives honge — matlab zyada precision aur kam recall.
  • Precision ya recall — kaunsa zyada important hai? Ye aksar ek business decision hota hai. Agar company fraudulent transactions ko zyada se zyada capture karna chahti hai aur kuch legitimate transactions check karne ke liye taiyaar hai, to wo recall ko evaluation metric ke roop me favour karegi.

Confusion matrix

Confusion matrix predictions ko predicted class aur actual class ke basis par ek table me break down karta hai:

  • True positives (TP): actual positives jo positive predict kiye gaye.
  • False negatives (FN): actual positives jo negative predict kiye gaye — fraud jo miss ho gaya.
  • False positives (FP): actual negatives jo positive predict kiye gaye — legitimate transaction jo galat tareeke se flag hui.
  • True negatives (TN): actual negatives jo negative predict kiye gaye.

Recall = TP / (TP + FN) — actual positives ka wo percentage jo positive predict kiya gaya. Precision = TP / (TP + FP) — predicted positives ka wo percentage jo waqai positive tha.

F1-score

F1-score precision aur recall ka harmonic mean hai. Harmonic means ko ratios ke liye "best average" mana jata hai. Agar P precision hai aur R recall hai, to F1-score = 2 × P × R / (P + R).

F1-score precision aur recall me se chhote wale ki taraf zyada skewed hota hai. Isliye ye ek achha metric hai ye ensure karne ke liye ki tum ek metric ko optimize karne ke liye dusre ko bahut zyada sacrifice na kar do.

ROC AUC aur PR AUC — threshold se independent metrics

Precision aur recall dono set threshold par heavily depend karte hain. Lekin underlying model ko decide karne ke liye aise metrics bhi hain jo sirf underlying model par depend karte hain — jaise ROC AUC aur PR AUC. Dono 0 aur 1 ke beech vary karte hain, aur 1 ke jitne kareeb, model utna behtar.

  • ROC curve: recall (true positive rate) vs false positive rate (negative examples ka wo percentage jo positive classify kiye gaye) plot karti hai. Curve ke alag-alag points alag-alag thresholds ko correspond karte hain — matlab curve poori tarah se saare possible thresholds ko dekhti hai. ROC AUC ko is tarah socha ja sakta hai: model (threshold se independent) positive example ko negative example ke mukable me zyada probability de ki wo positive hai, iski chance kitni hai.
  • ROC AUC ki limitation: unbalanced datasets me ya jahan false negative ki cost false positive se zyada hai, ROC AUC utna useful nahi hota — aur fraud detection me exactly yehi situation hai, kyunki ek fraudulent transaction miss karna ek legitimate transaction check karne se zyada costly hoga.
  • PR curve: isme precision vs recall plot kiya jata hai. PR curve unbalanced datasets me stronger metric hoti hai, kyunki precision aur recall dono positive class par focused hote hain, aur agar positive class ko rarer class set kar do, to metrics is class ko predict karne ki success par based hote hain, poore dataset par nahi.
Yaad rakho: Accuracy ko akele kabhi trust mat karo jab classes unbalanced hon. Fraud detection me recall hi wo metric hai jo batata hai ki tumne kitna fraud pakda — aur purane model ki kahani (99.87% accuracy, 0.19% recall) iska sabse achha saboot hai.

05.3Chapter 5 · Using AutoML to Detect Fraudulent Transactions

AutoML Classification Model Train Karna

Data explore karne aur metrics samajhne ke baad tum Vertex AI me managed dataset banate ho aur AutoML se classification model train karte ho. Kai steps Chapter 4 jaisi hi hain, isliye yahan unki treatment halki hai — details ke liye Chapter 4 wapas dekho.

Managed dataset banana aur model objective select karna

  • Dataset banao: console.cloud.google.com par jao, Vertex AI kholo, Datasets select karo, Create button dabao, aur autogenerated naam ko fraud_detection se replace karo.
  • Data type aur objective: tabular data hai aur classification problem solve karni hai, isliye Tabular aur phir "Regression/classification" chuno.
  • Data source: do choices hain — Google Cloud Storage me CSV file, ya BigQuery me table jisme wahi data pehle se prepared hai. BigQuery wala approach use karo, kyunki usme additional schema information aati hai — jaise har column ke data types — jo CSV me nahi hoti. "Select a table or view from BigQuery" select karo aur ye BigQuery path type karo: ma-low-code-ai.low_code_ai.financial_transactions
  • Load time: data load aur preprocess hone me lagbhag 15–20 minutes lagte hain. AutoML training job se pehle data ko analyze aur prepare karne ke liye bahut saara additional preprocessing karta hai.

Dataset statistics explore karna

Data load hone ke baad Generate Statistics button par click karo — statistics generate hone me kuch minutes lagenge. Phir alag-alag columns par click karke unki statistics explore karo.

  • type column: koi missing values nahi hain, paाँच distinct values hain jo pehle dekhe the, aur har value kitni baar appear hoti hai, iska breakdown dikhta hai — ek visualization ke saath jo jaldi batata hai ki total values ka kitna portion har value comprise karti hai.
  • Habit banao: training shuru karne se pehle har column ko check karo — data types aur statistics ko tumhari pehle ki analysis se match karna chahiye, koi surprise nahi hona chahiye. Is baar koi surprise nahi hai, lekin ye check karna best practice hai.

Model train karna

Train New Model button par click karo aur Other option select karo. Objective ke roop me Classification chuna hona chahiye aur model training method ke roop me AutoML — phir Continue dabao.

  1. Model details: "Train new model" select karo, model ka naam fraud_detection rakho, aur target column ke roop me isFraud chuno. Continue dabao.
  2. Training options: chuno ki kaunse features train karne ke liye use karne hain, aur ensure karo ki features ko categorical ya numeric ke roop me sahi tareeke se treat kiya jaye. Screen ke right side par isFlaggedFraud, nameDest aur nameOrig features ke paas minus signs par click karke in features ko training process se hata do. Ye important hai:
    • isFlaggedFraud: pichle model ki prediction hai — prediction time par available nahi hogi, isliye use feature ke roop me use karna galat hoga.
    • nameOrig aur nameDest: lagbhag unique identifiers hain — model sirf inhe dekhne lag sakta hai aur real patterns seekhna band kar dega.
    • step ko categorical treat karo: step ek time period represent karta hai, numeric value nahi. step 10 ko step 5 se twice as influential count nahi karna chahiye.
  3. Compute and pricing: training budget set karo. Pricing per hour training ke hisaab se compute hoti hai — up-to-date pricing ke liye Vertex AI documentation dekho. Budget 1 hour set karo. Early Stopping select karna mat bhoolo — ye model training process ko terminate kar dega jab improvement dikhna band ho jaye. Ye bahut useful hai agar tumne zyada budget set kiya ho lekin aakhir me utna time chahiye hi na ho.

Phir Start Training dabao. Model training complete hone ke baad tumhe email notification milegi, aur model model registry me register ho jayega.

Yaad rakho: Feature selection me jo features tum hataate ho, wo utne hi important hain jitne jo tum rakhte ho. isFlaggedFraud ko rakhna data leakage hota — model ko aisi information mil jati jo prediction time par kabhi available nahi hogi — aur isse model ki real performance ka galat andaza milta.

05.4Chapter 5 · Using AutoML to Detect Fraudulent Transactions

Evaluation, Feature Importance aur Predictions

Model train hone ke baad tum uski evaluation metrics dekhte ho, feature importances check karte ho, aur phir use deploy karke ek test transaction par prediction lete ho. Yahan metrics ki kahani Chapter 4 se alag hai — kyunki yahan classification hai aur classes unbalanced hain.

Model performance evaluate karna

Vertex AI Model Registry me jao, apna model fraud_detection par click karo, aur version 1 select karo. Kyunki tumhe fraudulent transactions predict karne ki sabse zyada parwah hai, class 1 par click karo taaki AutoML ne test dataset par model ne kaisa perform kiya, ye dekh sako.

  • Note: model training process me randomness ki wajah se tumhare model ki evaluation metrics is chapter me dikhayi gayi metrics se differ kar sakti hain.
  • Confidence threshold slider: is slider ko move karke dekh sakte ho ki precision aur recall kaise affect hote hain. Ye threshold decide karta hai ki kis probability se upar transaction ko fraudulent flag karna hai.
  • Example — 50% precision target: maan lo tumhari company willing hai ki flagged transactions me se 50% tak legitimate hon, taaki wo zyada se zyada fraud capture kar sake aur phir bhi flagged transactions check karne ke resources rakhe. Is model ke liye 50% precision se correspond karne wala threshold 0.06 hai — matlab agar model predict karta hai ki fraud ki chance 6% se zyada hai, to tum use fraud ke roop me flag karke check karna chahoge.
  • Us threshold par recall 95.2% hai: matlab sirf 20 me se 1 fraudulent transaction miss hone ki expectation hai. Purane model ke 0.19% recall se ye ek bahut bada improvement hai.
  • Best confidence threshold business needs par depend karta hai — iska koi single sahi jawab nahi hai.

Model feature importances

UI me "All labels" par click karo aur page ke neeche scroll karo — wahan model ki feature importances dikhengi. Feature importances features ka model predictions par impact measure karti hain.

  • Sabse important features: oldbalanceOrg aur newbalanceOrig sabse important the, aur amount aur type teesre aur chauthe number par the.
  • Ye EDA se match karta hai: notebook exploration me inhi features ke values aur fraudulent transactions ke percentage ke beech sabse clear patterns dikhe the. Ye check karna achha hai — ensure karo ki model ne kuch nonsensical to nahi seekha. Example ke liye, agar taxi fare predict karne wala model ye seekhe ki ride ki distance sabse kam important feature hai, to ye data ko aur closely explore karne ka reason ho sakta hai.
  • Stakeholders aur debugging dono ke liye useful: stakeholders samajh sakte hain ki model predictions kaise banata hai, aur data scientists aur ML engineers surprising ya nonsensical predictions ke case me model ko debug kar sakte hain.

Model se predictions lena — deploy karna

Deploy karne ka process Chapter 4 jaisa hi hai. In steps ko follow karo, unmentioned options ko default value par chhod do:

  1. Define your endpoint: endpoint ka naam fraud_endpoint rakho.
  2. Model settings: Machine type ke roop me n1-standard-2, 2vCPUs, 7.5GiB memory select karo. Chhota machine type use karne se deployed model ki cost kam hogi aur is example ke liye tumhari needs meet ho jayengi.
  3. Explainability options: "Enable feature attributions for this model" checkbox par click karo.
  4. Model monitoring: disable kar do, kyunki yahan iski zaroorat nahi hai.

Deploy dabao. Model deploy hone me kuch minutes lagenge. Deploy hone ke baad page ke neeche model ko test kar sakte ho.

Test prediction — ek example transaction

Model ko in values se test karo — tumhare exact results dikhaye gaye model se vary kar sakte hain:

step: 14
type: CASH_OUT
amount: 1000000
oldbalanceOrg: 1000000
newbalanceOrig: 0
oldbalanceDest: 0
newbalanceDest: 0

Predict button dabao. Predicted probability dekhne ke liye "Selected label" ko 1 par change karo.

  • Confidence score 91%: dikhaye gaye model ke liye confidence score predicted probability hai — is case me transaction ke fraudulent hone ki 91% chance. Thresholds wali pehle ki discussion ke basis par is transaction ko fraudulent mark kiya jayega.
  • Local feature importances: sabse zyada feature importance value oldbalanceOrg feature se correspond karti hai. Is case me account me exactly 1,000,000 dollars hone par CASH_OUT transaction hua hai — model ke hisaab se iske fraudulent hone ki high chance hai.
  • Exercise: feature values ke alag-alag combinations explore karo aur dekho ki predicted probabilities aur corresponding feature attributions kya hain.

Important: chapter khatm hone ke baad model ko undeploy karna mat bhoolo — deployed models cost incur karte hain jab wo use me nahi bhi hote. Undeploy karne ke liye Vertex AI Endpoints me jao, endpoint name fraud_endpoint par click karo, "More actions" three-dot menu par click karo, aur "Undeploy model from endpoint" select karo.

Yaad rakho: Naye model ka recall 95.2% (50% precision threshold par) purane model ke 0.19% recall se bahut behtar hai — matlab naya model transactions ko behtar tareeke se flag karega aur customers ke accounts bachaega. Yahi farak hai ek benchmark model jo kaam karta hai aur ek model jo sirf accuracy me achha dikhta hai.

06Chapter 6 · Using BigQuery ML to Train a Linear Regression Model

BigQuery ML se Linear Regression Model

Is chapter me tum SQL se data analysis karke, Jupyter Notebook se data explore karke, aur BigQuery ML se model train karke ek combined cycle power plant ke production ko forecast karte ho. Tum ek linear regression model aur ek neural network model, dono scratch se banate ho.

Business use case — power plant production

Tumhara goal hai ek combined cycle power plant (CCPP) ka net hourly electrical energy output predict karna, plant ke paas ke weather conditions ke basis par.

  • CCPP kya hai: ye gas turbines, steam turbines aur heat recovery steam generators se bana hota hai. Electricity gas aur steam turbines se generate hoti hai, jo ek cycle me combined hote hain. Vacuum steam turbine se collect hota hai, jabki baaki teen ambient variables — temperature, ambient pressure aur relative humidity — gas turbine performance ko affect karte hain.
  • Dataset: CCPP se chhah saal ki period (2006–2011) me collect kiye gaye data points hain, jab power plant full load par kaam kar raha tha. Data per hour aggregate kiya gaya hai, lekin recorded weather conditions aur energy production ke liye exact hour dataset me supplied nahi hai.
  • Iska practical matlab: tum data ko sequence ya time-series data ke roop me treat nahi kar sakte — jahan pichle records ki information se future records predict kiye jate hain.
  • 5 columns, 9,590 rows: Temperature, Ambient pressure, Relative humidity, Exhaust vacuum aur Energy production (target variable).

Expected value ranges — engineers ki technical report se

ColumnMinimumMaximum
Temperature1.81°C37.11°C
Ambient pressure992.89 millibar1,033.30 millibar
Relative humidity25.56%100.16%
Exhaust vacuum25.36 cm Hg81.56 cm Hg
Energy production420.26 MW495.76 MW

Ye expected ranges power plant engineers ne ek technical report ke through share kiye hain. Ye data explore karte waqt bahut helpful honge — ye ensure karne ke liye ki null values ya magic numbers jaise issues to nahi hain.

BigQuery aur BigQuery ML kya hain

  • BigQuery Google Cloud ka serverless data warehouse solution hai. Serverless ka matlab hai ki tum servers provision kiye bina jaldi data load karke SQL data analysis shuru kar sakte ho.
  • BigQuery ML se tum BigQuery me stored data par ML kar sakte ho — neural network models train karne ke liye BigQuery ML Vertex AI ke resources use karta hai.
  • Free tier: SQL queries se process kiya gaya pehla 1 TB data per month aur 10 GB storage per month free hain. Linear regression jaise certain types ke ML models banane ke liye process kiya gaya pehla 10 GB data bhi free hai. Neural network model train karne ke liye free trial ya billing account par charges lagenge.
  • SQL nahi aati to: Google ka "Prepare Data for Exploration" course (Coursera, free) ek achha starting point hai, aur deeper dive ke liye Learning SQL (3rd edition) ek achha resource hai.

Is chapter me tum data ko SQL se clean aur explore karoge, feature selection aur correlation seekhoge, CREATE MODEL statement se linear regression model banaoge, Explainable AI se model ko samjhoge, aur aakhir me ek deep neural network train karoge.

Yaad rakho: Ye regression problem hai — goal ek real number predict karna hai: energy production megawatts (MW) me. Aur BigQuery ML me model banana sirf SQL likhne jitna simple hai — tumhe Python me model code likhne ki zaroorat nahi hai.

GitHub: maabel0712/low-code-ai — chapter6/bq_examples.sql

-- SQL queries which are used in Chapter 6 in the book "Low-Code AI"
-- If you wish, you can do a "Find and Replace" to replace your-project-id with your Google Cloud Project.

-- Check for NULL values in Temp column

SELECT 
  IF(Temp IS NULL, 1, 0) AS is_temp_null
FROM
  `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_raw`

-- Check for NULL values in all columns

SELECT
  SUM(IF(Temp IS NULL, 1, 0)) AS no_temp_nulls,
  SUM(IF(Exhaust_Vacuum IS NULL, 1, 0)) AS no_ev_nulls,
  SUM(IF(Ambient_Pressure IS NULL, 1, 0)) AS no_ap_nulls,
  SUM(IF(Relative_Humidity IS NULL, 1, 0)) AS no_rh_nulls,
  SUM(IF(Energy_Production IS NULL, 1, 0)) AS no_ep_nulls
FROM
  `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_raw`

-- Compute the MIN and MAX values of the Temp column 

SELECT
  MIN(Temp) as min_temp,
  MAX(Temp) as max_temp
FROM
  `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_raw`

-- Compute the MIN and MAX values for all columns

SELECT 
  MIN(Temp) as min_temp,
  MAX(Temp) as max_temp,
  MIN(Exhaust_Vacuum) as min_ev,
  MAX(Exhaust_Vacuum) as max_ev,
  MIN(Ambient_Pressure) as min_ap,
  MAX(Ambient_Pressure) as max_ap,
  MIN(Relative_Humidity) as min_rh,
  MAX(Relative_Humidity) as max_rh,
  MIN(Energy_Production) as min_ep,
  MAX(Energy_Production) as max_ep
FROM
  `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_raw`

-- Create table for preprocessed data

CREATE TABLE
  `data_driven_ml.ccpp_cleaned`
AS
  SELECT 
    *
  FROM 
    `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_raw`
  WHERE
    Temp BETWEEN 1.81 AND 37.11 AND
    Ambient_Pressure BETWEEN 992.89 AND 1033.30 AND
    Relative_Humidity BETWEEN 25.56 AND 100.16 AND
    Exhaust_Vacuum BETWEEN 25.36 AND 81.56 AND
    Energy_Production BETWEEN 420.26 AND 495.76

-- Compute Pearson Correlation coefficient between the Temp and Exhaust_Vacuum columns

SELECT
  CORR(Temp, Exhaust_Vacuum)
FROM
  `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_cleaned`

-- Compute Pearson Correlation coefficient between the Temp and other feature columns

SELECT 
  CORR(Temp, Ambient_Pressure) AS corr_t_ap,
  CORR(Temp, Relative_Humidity) AS corr_t_rh,
  CORR(Temp, Exhaust_Vacuum) AS corr_t_ev
FROM 
  `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_cleaned`

-- Statement to create a linear regression model in BigQuery ML

CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL data_driven_ml.energy_production 
  OPTIONS(model_type='linear_reg',
          input_label_cols=['Energy_Production']) AS
SELECT
  Temp,
  Ambient_Pressure,
  Relative_Humidity,
  Exhaust_Vacuum,
  Energy_Production
FROM
  `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_cleaned`

-- Evaluate the newly trained linear regression model

SELECT
  *
FROM
  ML.EVALUATE(MODEL data_driven_ml.energy_production)

-- Serve a prediction on a single example

SELECT
  *
FROM
  ML.PREDICT(MODEL `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.energy_production`,
    (
    SELECT
      27.45 AS Temp,
      1001.23 AS Ambient_Pressure,
      84 AS Relative_Humidity,
      65.12 AS Exhaust_Vacuum) )

-- Train a linear regression model in BigQuery ML with global explanability enabled

CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL data_driven_ml.energy_production
  OPTIONS(model_type='linear_reg',
          input_label_cols=['Energy_Production'],
          enable_global_explain=TRUE) AS
SELECT
  Temp,
  Ambient_Pressure,
  Relative_Humidity,
  Exhaust_Vacuum,
  Energy_Production
FROM
  `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_cleaned`

-- Use the ML.GLOBAL_EXPLAIN function 

SELECT 
  *
FROM
  ML.GLOBAL_EXPLAIN(MODEL `data_driven_ml.energy_production`)

-- Serve predictions with explanations

SELECT
  *
FROM
  ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT(
    MODEL `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.energy_production`,
    (
    SELECT
      Temp,
      Ambient_Pressure,
      Relative_Humidity,
      Exhaust_Vacuum
    FROM
      `your-project-id.some_dataset.some_table`),
    STRUCT(3 AS top_k_features) )

-- Train a neural network regressor

CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL data_driven_ml.energy_production_nn
  OPTIONS 
    (model_type='dnn_regressor',
     hidden_units=[32,16,8],
     input_label_cols=['Energy_Production']) AS
SELECT
  Temp,
  Ambient_Pressure,
  Relative_Humidity,
  Exhaust_Vacuum,
  Energy_Production
FROM
  `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_cleaned`

-- Evaluate the newly trained neural network model

SELECT
  *
FROM
  ML.EVALUATE(MODEL data_driven_ml.energy_production)

-- Serve a prediction on a single example with the neural network model

SELECT
  *
FROM
  ML.PREDICT(MODEL `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.energy_production`,
    (
    SELECT
      27.45 AS Temp,
      1001.23 AS Ambient_Pressure,
      84 AS Relative_Humidity,
      65.12 AS Exhaust_Vacuum) )

06.1Chapter 6 · Using BigQuery ML to Train a Linear Regression Model

SQL se Dataset Clean aur Explore Karna

ML model ki quality heavily dataset ki quality par depend karti hai. Agar dataset erroneous data ya missing values se bhara ho, to ML model sahi insights seekh nahi payega. Is section me tum SQL aur BigQuery se CCPP dataset ko load, check aur clean karte ho.

Dataset BigQuery me load karna

  • Dataset banao: Google Cloud Console me BigQuery SQL workspace kholo, project name select karo, "View actions" (three vertical dots) par click karo, aur "Create dataset" select karo. Dataset ID me data_driven_ml type karo, data location ke liye US select karo — kyunki load karne wala data US-based Cloud Storage bucket me hai — phir Create Dataset dabao.
  • Table banao: dataset select karo, "View actions" se "Create table" select karo. Choices ye hain: Create table from — Google Cloud Storage; file — low-code-ai-book/ccpp.csv; File format — CSV; Table — ccpp_raw; Schema — Auto detect. CSV me header hai aur saari values floating-point numbers hain, isliye BigQuery schema detect kar sakta hai.
  • Table partitioning aur clustering: partitioning bade tables ko "chhoti tables" (partitions) me break karne ka method hai jinhe filters se alag se access kiya ja sakta hai — query me reference na kiye gaye partitions read nahi hote, isse query ki cost kam hoti hai aur performance improve hoti hai. Clustered tables me user-defined column sort order hota hai — ye bhi query performance improve kar sakte hain aur costs kam kar sakte hain.
  • Schema aur Preview tabs: table banne ke baad Schema tab se schema aur Preview tab se data preview dekh sakte ho.

Null values check karna — IF aur SUM functions

BigQuery me IF(expr, true_result, else_result) teen arguments leta hai: agar expr TRUE return kare to true_result, warna else_result. Temp column me null check karne ke liye IF(Temp IS NULL, 1, 0) use hota hai — 1 agar Temp NULL hai, 0 agar nahi hai.

Ek-ek result ko scroll karke dekhna inefficient hai — 9,000 se zyada values me sirf do 1s milte hain. Iske bajay SUM() use karo taaki saare columns ke nulls ek saath gin sakein:

SELECT
  SUM(IF(Temp IS NULL, 1, 0)) AS no_temp_nulls,
  SUM(IF(Exhaust_Vacuum IS NULL, 1, 0)) AS no_ev_nulls,
  SUM(IF(Ambient_Pressure IS NULL, 1, 0)) AS no_ap_nulls,
  SUM(IF(Relative_Humidity IS NULL, 1, 0)) AS no_rh_nulls,
  SUM(IF(Energy_Production IS NULL, 1, 0)) AS no_ep_nulls
FROM
  `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_raw`

Result: Ambient_Pressure ke alawa saare columns me null values hain. In rows ka kya karna chahiye? Sabse easy approach hai in rows ko omit kar dena. Dusra option hai imputation — missing data ko substituted values se replace karna, aksar aise tareeke se ki substituted values us context me realistic hon. Ye Chapter 7 me explore hota hai.

  • Omit karna kab reasonable hai: yahan null values wali rows worst case me data ka lagbhag 0.1% hongi, isliye unhe omit karna bilkul reasonable strategy hai.
  • Impute kab karna chahiye: agar dataset chhota ho ya missing values wali rows dataset ka significant percentage hon, to rows phenkna model performance ko bahut affect kar sakta hai. Ek aur subtle issue bias hai — statistical bias ka matlab hai tumhare data ke distribution aur data ke real distribution me systematic difference. Agar null values kisi specific subset ke examples me aati hain, to un rows ko hatane se model important information seekhne se reh jayega.

MIN aur MAX se acceptable data ranges check karna

MIN aur MAX aggregate functions hain — ek column lekar ek single value return karte hain. Temp par query karne se minimum 1.81°C aur maximum 37.11°C milta hai — jo expected range se match karta hai. Saare columns ke liye ek hi query likhi ja sakti hai:

SELECT
  MIN(Temp) as min_temp, MAX(Temp) as max_temp,
  MIN(Exhaust_Vacuum) as min_ev, MAX(Exhaust_Vacuum) as max_ev,
  MIN(Ambient_Pressure) as min_ap, MAX(Ambient_Pressure) as max_ap,
  MIN(Relative_Humidity) as min_rh, MAX(Relative_Humidity) as max_rh,
  MIN(Energy_Production) as min_ep, MAX(Energy_Production) as max_ep
FROM
  `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_raw`

Results me do suspicious values dikhti hain: minimum ambient pressure 0.0 aur minimum energy production -1.0. Communicated range aur common sense ke hisaab se inme se koi bhi value sense nahi banati.

  • Magic number: -1.0 ek distinctive unique value hai jo standard meaning se alag kuch represent karne ke liye hoti hai — yahan likely missing data ko represent karne ke liye magic number hai, kyunki -1.0 energy production value ke roop me sense nahi banata.
  • Default value: 0.0 ambient pressure likely ek default value hai — applications me aksar aisi value record ki jati hai jab koi value report nahi hoti, NULL values se hone wale issues avoid karne ke liye.

Cleaned table banana — CREATE TABLE aur BETWEEN

Query results ko save karne ke liye DDL (data definition language) statement use hoti hai — BigQuery me datasets me objects create aur modify karne ka syntax. Basic syntax hai:

CREATE TABLE
  table_name
AS
  query_statement

Agar table pehle se exists karti hai, to wo overwrite nahi hogi — overwrite karne ke liye CREATE TABLE ki jagah CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE use karo. BETWEEN operator query ko simplify karta hai: Field_name BETWEEN min_value AND max_value TRUE return karta hai agar value range ke andar hai, warna FALSE. Expected ranges se filter karne se NULL values bhi eliminate ho jayengi, kyunki wo bhi ranges ke andar nahi hain:

CREATE TABLE
  `data_driven_ml.ccpp_cleaned`
AS
SELECT
  *
FROM
  `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_raw`
WHERE
  Temp BETWEEN 1.81 AND 37.11 AND
  Ambient_Pressure BETWEEN 992.89 AND 1033.30 AND
  Relative_Humidity BETWEEN 25.56 AND 100.16 AND
  Exhaust_Vacuum BETWEEN 25.36 AND 81.56 AND
  Energy_Production BETWEEN 420.26 AND 495.76
  • Result: nayi ccpp_cleaned table me 9,576 rows hain, jabki original ccpp_raw me 9,590 rows thi. Matlab sirf 14 rows (lagbhag 0.15% data) filter out hui. Bahut kam data khoya, lekin kuch galat values — khaas taur par extreme outliers — model performance ko bahut harm kar sakti hain, isliye ye process karna achha hai.
  • Baad me save karna ho to: query execute hone ke baad console me Save Results par jao, BigQuery Table select karo, aur dataset aur table names bhar do. Query results ek temporary table me store hote hain jo query complete hone ke 24 hours tak retained rehti hai — Personal History tab se us job par click karke "Temporary table" access kar sakte ho.

Deep dive — Cloud Shell se Cloud Storage file dekhna

Cloud Shell Google Cloud ki free service hai jo Google Cloud CLI preinstalled ke saath ek chhoti virtual machine par terminal access deti hai. Activate Cloud Shell button se ise kholo, phir project set karo: gcloud config set project your-project-id.

CSV file ki pehli kuch lines download kiye bina dekhne ke liye: gcloud storage cat -r 0-250 gs://low-code-ai-book/ccpp.csv — cat file ko read karke terminal output par likhta hai, aur -r 0-250 sirf pehle 250 bytes read karta hai. Output me header dikhta hai: Temp,Exhaust_Vacuum,Ambient_Pressure,Relative_Humidity,Energy_Production aur pehli rows, jaise 14.96, 41.76, 1024.07, 73.17, 463.26.

File me kitni lines hain, ye ginne ke liye pipe operator use karo: gcloud storage cat gs://low-code-ai-book/ccpp.csv | wc -l — result 9,590 lines hai. Note karo ki har baar Cloud Shell kholne par underlying virtual machine alag hoti hai, lekin persistent disk wahi rehti hai — tumhara data hamesha available rahega, lekin tumhare install kiye hue tools ko reopen karne par reinstall karna padega.

Yaad rakho: Data cleaning me expected ranges jaanna sabse powerful tool hai. Bina technical report ke tumhe pata hi nahi chalta ki -1.0 energy production aur 0.0 ambient pressure galat values hain — domain knowledge hi tumhe batata hai ki kya filter karna hai.
