06.2Chapter 6 · Using BigQuery ML to Train a Linear Regression Model

Linear Regression aur Feature Selection

Data clean karne ke baad tum seedha model train karne ke liye taiyaar nahi ho — pehle ye samajhna hai ki linear regression kaise kaam karta hai aur kaunse features use karne hain. Is section me tum model ka maths, weights dhoondhne ke tareeke, aur Pearson correlation se feature selection seekhte ho.

Linear regression model kya hai

Goal hai energy production predict karna, temperature, ambient pressure, relative humidity aur exhaust vacuum pressure ke basis par. Ye regression problem hai, kyunki goal ek real number predict karna hai — energy production megawatts (MW) me.

Maan lo tumhare paas numeric features x1 se xn tak hain, aur unke basis par koi real number y predict karna hai. Linear regression model is form ka function hai:

f(x) = w0 + w1 × x1 + ... + wn × xn

  • Weights: w0, w1 se wn tak real numbers hain, inhe weights kaha jata hai; w0 ko aksar model ka bias kaha jata hai. Tum koi bhi random weights chun sakte ho aur ek function pa sakte ho — lekin wo kitna achha model hoga?
  • Line of best fit: simple example me dots examples hote hain — x value feature hai aur y value label hai — aur dotted line line of best fit represent karti hai.

RMSE aur loss function

Model ki quality measure karne ke liye Chapter 4 wala root mean squared error (RMSE) yahan bhi use hota hai. Dataset D me N examples hon, to RMSE loss function hai jo model ke predictions aur actual labels ke beech ke difference ko measure karta hai. RMSE dataset par bhi depend karta hai, sirf model par nahi.

Loss function ka goal ye measure karna hai ki tumhara algorithm dataset par kitni achhi tarah perform karta hai. Agar predictions bilkul galat hain, to loss function zyada number output karega; agar predictions kaafi achhi hain, to kam number output karega. Best weights wo hain jo loss function (RMSE) ko jitna ho sake utna chhota banayein.

Best weights kaise dhoondhein — normal equation vs gradient descent

  • Normal equation: dataset aur corresponding labels se normal equation solve karne se exact analytical solution milta hai — kaunse weights best model dete hain. Kai analytics packages aur products (BigQuery samet) is approach ko apne toolkit me include karte hain.
  • Normal equation hamesha kyun use nahi hoti: pehla reason computational complexity hai — normal equation solve karne ki complexity O(n³) se thodi kam hoti hai. Matlab dataset 1,000 se 10,000 examples tak badhaye — tenfold — to kaam lagbhag 10³ = 1,000 guna badh jayega. Bade datasets ke saath ye jaldi out of hand ho jata hai. Dusra reason hai ki computation me bahut bade numbers involve ho sakte hain, aur computers par floating-point arithmetic ki wajah se ye issues create kar sakte hain — technical term me system ill-conditioned ho jata hai.
  • Gradient descent: agar examples ki sankhya bahut zyada hai ya normal equation solve karne me issues aate hain, to gradient descent naam ka dusra approach use kiya ja sakta hai. Iska detail yahan cover nahi kiya gaya hai, lekin lagbhag saare ML frameworks me gradient descent aur uske variations available hote hain.

Feature selection — kaunse features use karein

Prepared dataset me chaar columns hain jo energy production predict karne ke liye use ho sakte hain: Temp, Ambient_Pressure, Relative_Humidity aur Exhaust_Vacuum. Features select karte waqt teen basic guidelines follow karo:

  1. Feature problem objective se related hona chahiye.
  2. Feature prediction time par known hona chahiye.
  3. Feature numeric hona chahiye, ya numeric value me transform ho sakna chahiye.

Teesri condition important hai, kyunki linear regression model — aur practice me use hone wale zyada tar model types — ek mathematical function hai jo numeric features ko inputs ke roop me leta hai aur ek real number output karta hai. Numeric values jinme meaningful magnitudes nahi hote, unhe alag tareeke se treat karna padta hai — jaise car ka colour number ke roop me record ho (0 red, 1 blue, 2 silver), to ye kehna sense nahi banata ki silver ki value blue se double hai. Aise features ko properly encode karne ke liye one-hot encoding jaise techniques baad ke chapters me aate hain.

Pearson correlation se relationship samajhna

Features objective se related hain ya nahi, ye samajhne ke do tareeke hain: domain expertise leverage karna, aur correlation jaise statistical methods use karna. Yahan domain experts ne report me communicate kiya hai ki ye features objective se related hain — aur ML practitioner ke roop me tumhe aksar domain ko samajhne walon par rely karna padta hai.

Pearson correlation coefficient, Corr(X, Y), -1 aur 1 ke beech ek number hai jo measure karta hai ki do variables ke beech ka relationship linear hone ke kitne kareeb hai:

  • Exactly 1: X aur Y ka perfectly linear relationship hai — Y = m × X + b, jahan m positive number hai.
  • Exactly -1: wahi idea, lekin m negative hai.
  • 0 ke kareeb: variables linear relationship se utne hi door hain.

BigQuery me correlation CORR function se compute hota hai:

SELECT
  CORR(Temp, Exhaust_Vacuum)
FROM
  `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_cleaned`
  • Temp aur Exhaust_Vacuum ka correlation lagbhag 0.844 hai — moderate to strong positive linear relationship. Physical perspective se ye sense banata hai, kyunki pressure temperature badhne ke saath badhta hai (baaki variables constant maan kar).
  • Temp aur Ambient_Pressure ka correlation -0.508 hai — moderate negative correlation, matlab temperature kam karne se ambient pressure badhega, ya vice versa.
  • Temp aur Energy_Production ka correlation -0.948 hai — bahut strong negative (inverse) relationship. Temperature jitna kam, energy output utna zyada.

Colab me correlation matrix aur heat map

Ek-ek pair ka correlation compute karna time-consuming hai — 5 columns (label samet) ke liye total 10 correlation coefficients chahiye hote hain, aur ye sankhya columns badhne ke saath jaldi badhti hai. Behtar tareeka hai Google Colab use karna:

  • Explore with Python notebook: BigQuery me SELECT * FROM ccpp_cleaned query chalao, phir Query Editor ke neeche Explore Data me "Explore with Python notebook" select karo. Isse ek templated notebook Colab me create hota hai jo query results ko notebook environment me load karta hai. Pehle cell (Setup) me do import statements add karo: import matplotlib.pyplot as plt aur import seaborn as sns. Cells ko order me ek-ek karke run karo — skip mat karo.
  • Correlation matrix: naye cell me results.corr().round(2) type karo — round method correlations ko do decimal places tak round karta hai readability ke liye. Matrix read karna easy hai: do features ke beech correlation dhoondhne ke liye ek feature ke column aur dusre ki row par jao.
  • Heat map: plt.figure(figsize=(10,6)); sns.heatmap(results.corr()) se matrix ko visualize karo. Darker colours bade negative correlations ko aur lighter colours bade positive correlations ko correspond karte hain.

Feature relationships ko label ke saath plot karna

Seaborn ke regplot se har feature aur Energy_Production ke beech ka relationship visualize karo:

  • Temp vs Energy_Production: negative linear relationship dikhta hai — correlation -0.948 se match karta hai.
  • Ambient_Pressure vs Energy_Production: vaguely positive relationship lagta hai, lekin Temp jitna clear nahi hai.
  • Relative_Humidity vs Energy_Production: weakly positive relationship lagta hai, lekin visualization se bahut clear nahi hai.
  • Exhaust_Vacuum vs Energy_Production: negative linear relationship lagta hai.

Knowledge check: kaunse features ka Energy_Production se strong correlation hai, aur kyun? Kaunse features ka weak correlation hai, aur kyun? Kaunse features ka moderate correlation hai, aur kyun?

Multicollinearity: jab regression model me do ya zyada predictors moderately ya highly correlated hote hain, to use multicollinearity (ya collinearity) kehte hain. Isse ye determine karna mushkil ho jata hai ki correlated variables me se har ek kya role play kar raha hai, standard errors badh jate hain, aur regression coefficients ke unreliable aur unstable estimates milte hain. Multicollinearity research conclusions ko limit kar sakti hai, khaas taur par linear regression jaise linear models use karte waqt.

Ek sawaal bhi socho: kya weak correlations wale features ko discard kar dena chahiye? Isse multivariate model se univariate model ban jayega — sirf ek feature (Temp) se label predict karna. Kya ye model generalizable hoga? Feature importance determine karne ke liye kya additional data collect kiya ja sakta hai? Chapter 1 ke business decision model ko use karke in sawaalon par socho.

Yaad rakho: Correlation sirf linear relationship measure karta hai — 0 correlation ka matlab ye nahi hai ki koi relationship hi nahi hai, sirf ye hai ki linear relationship nahi hai. Aur correlation causation nahi hota — Temp aur Exhaust_Vacuum ka 0.844 correlation dono ke beech physical link dikhata hai, lekin ye akele ye prove nahi karta ki ek dusre ko cause karta hai.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 6 — Using BigQuery ML to Train a Linear Regression Model
← Previous06.1 · SQL se Dataset Clean aur Explore Karna→ Next06.3 · CREATE MODEL Statement — Model Banana
06.3Chapter 6 · Using BigQuery ML to Train a Linear Regression Model

CREATE MODEL Statement — Model Banana

Data clean aur explore karne ke baad model banana bahut straightforward hai — sirf ek SQL statement likhni hai. Is section me tum BigQuery ML me linear regression model train karte ho, uski evaluation metrics dekhte ho, aur ML.PREDICT se predictions lete ho.

CREATE MODEL statement se linear regression model banana

BigQuery console par wapas jao aur Editor window me ye SQL statements enter karo:

CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL data_driven_ml.energy_production OPTIONS
(model_type='linear_reg',
input_label_cols=['Energy_Production']) AS
SELECT
  Temp,
  Ambient_Pressure,
  Relative_Humidity,
  Exhaust_Vacuum,
  Energy_Production
FROM
  `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_cleaned`
  • CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL: data_driven_ml dataset me energy_production naam ka ek naya ML model create karega, ya same naam ke model ko replace karega. BigQuery me ML models datasets me tables ki tarah objects hote hain.
  • model_type='linear_reg': model type specify karta hai — yahan linear regression.
  • input_label_cols=['Energy_Production']: wo column specify karta hai jo label ke roop me serve karta hai — yahan Energy_Production.
  • Training time: query run karo — model train hone me sirf kuch minutes lagne chahiye. Aage badhne se pehle model ke training finish hone ka wait karo.

Trained model ki evaluation metrics dekhna

Model table create hone ke baad Evaluation tab select karke evaluation metrics dekh sakte ho. Tumhare metrics figure me dikhaye gaye metrics se thode differ kar sakte hain.

ML.EVALUATE function bhi evaluation metrics deta hai:

SELECT
  *
FROM
  ML.EVALUATE(MODEL data_driven_ml.energy_production)
  • Console aur ML.EVALUATE ka output same hai — ek additional output ke alawa. ML.EVALUATE ek metric aur deta hai jise "explained variance" kehte hain, explained_variance column ke through.
  • Explained variance: is sawaal ka jawab hai — "label me variance ka kitna hissa hamara model apne outputs me capture karta hai?" Agar average label value aur average predicted value same hon, to explained variance aur R2 score same hone ki expectation hai — ise unbiased estimator kehte hain, aur linear regression aisa hi example hai.
  • Yahan scores alag kyun hain? Kyunki tum model ko training dataset par evaluate nahi kar rahe ho! BigQuery ML tumhare dataset ko automatically training aur evaluation datasets me split kar deta hai jab tum model train karte ho. Evaluation dataset par, jab tak evaluation aur training datasets statistically similar hon, tum sirf ye expect karte ho ki ye metrics ek dusre ke kareeb hon. Data split ko zyada control karne ke options Chapter 7 me explore hote hain.

ML.PREDICT function se predictions serve karna

ML ka ultimate goal sirf best model train karna nahi hai — apne use cases ke liye predictions serve karna hai. BigQuery ML me ML.PREDICT function se predictions serve karna bahut straightforward hai. Note karo ki ML.PREDICT sirf us data par predictions ke liye kaam karega jo BigQuery ke liye processing ke liye available hai.

Maan lo tumhe ek hour ka power production jaanna hai jahan average temperature 27.45°C hai, ambient pressure 1,001.23 millibar hai, relative humidity 84% hai, aur exhaust vacuum pressure 65.12 cm Hg hai:

SELECT
  *
FROM
  ML.PREDICT(MODEL `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.energy_production`,
  (
  SELECT
    27.45 AS Temp,
    1001.23 AS Ambient_Pressure,
    84 AS Relative_Humidity,
    65.12 AS Exhaust_Vacuum) )
  • AS keyword se alias karna best practice hai — taaki values model me sahi tareeke se plug hon. Agar tum extra columns include karte ho jo features se correspond nahi karte, to wo simply result me pass through ho jayenge — ye useful ho sakta hai jab tum predicted label ko result table me column ke roop me include karna chahte ho, saath me wo columns bhi jo model me use nahi hote.
  • Predicted energy production 433.35 MW thi — predicted_label column me predicted energy production hoti hai. Tumhare model ki predicted label dikhaye gaye result se thodi differ kar sakti hai.
  • Batch predictions: ye method single predictions ke liye achha hai, lekin agar tumhe feature values ki table par predict karna ho to bhi ML.PREDICT use kar sakte ho — dusre SELECT statement ki jagah ek table specify karo. Is tarah ki queries BigQuery ko batch predictions ke liye ek wonderful tool bana deti hain — jahan ek saath badi sankhya me instances par predictions chahiye hoti hain.
SELECT
  *
FROM
  ML.PREDICT(MODEL `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.energy_production`,
  (
  SELECT
    Temp,
    Ambient_Pressure,
    Relative_Humidity,
    Exhaust_Vacuum
  FROM
    `your-project-id.some_dataset.some_table`) )
Yaad rakho: Is chapter me tumne saare chaaro features use karke model train kiya hai. Exercise ke roop me features ke subset se naye models train karo — correlations aur collinearity ke baare me jo seekha hai, use karke features select karo — phir in naye models ko evaluate karo aur dekho ki kaunse feature sets ne best perform kiya.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 6 — Using BigQuery ML to Train a Linear Regression Model
← Previous06.2 · Linear Regression aur Feature Selection→ Next06.4 · Explainable AI BigQuery ML me
06.4Chapter 6 · Using BigQuery ML to Train a Linear Regression Model

Explainable AI BigQuery ML me

Deep learning aur complex models ke growth ke saath explainable AI (XAI) research ka ek tezi se badhta hua field ban gaya hai. Iska goal hai model ke behavior ko human-understandable terms me describe karna — taaki model ki performance improve ki ja sake, issues samjhe ja sakein, aur compliance ya ethical reasons se model kuch biases avoid kare, ye ensure kiya ja sake.

Local vs global explanations

  • Local explanations: ek single instance ya chhote group of instances par focus karte hain. Goal hota hai: "Mere model ne is specific example ke liye ye prediction kyun di?"
  • Global explanations: ek certain dataset par model ke behavior ko overall dekhte hain. Example ke liye: "Kaunse features model ki predictions me sabse zyada contribute karte hain?"

Explanations kaise compute hoti hain

  • Post hoc methods: zyada tar methods post hoc hote hain — matlab model train hone ke baad use kiye jate hain. Ye methods certain model types ke liye specific ho sakte hain ya model-agnostic ho sakte hain. Generally, post hoc methods ek specific dataset (jaise evaluation dataset) lete hain aur model us dataset par kaise behave karta hai aur perturbations ka use karke explanations dete hain.
  • Intrinsically explainable models: kuch models intrinsically explainable hote hain, jaise linear regression models. Is case me explanations ko alag dataset use kiye bina seedha model se hi derive kiya ja sakta hai. Lekin ek trade-off hai — generally, jitne zyada complex models hote hain, wo utne kam intrinsically explainable hote hain. Deep neural networks jaise zyada complex model types ko model definition se explain karna impossible hai, aur tumhe post hoc methods par rely karna padta hai.

BigQuery ML me Explainable AI

ML.EVALUATE function evaluation metrics deta hai, lekin BigQuery ek function bhi offer karta hai jo model aur uske predictions ko explain karne ka tareeka deta hai. BigQuery me global aur local explanations Google Cloud ki Explainable AI service use karti hain. Explainable AI BigQuery me "feature attributions" deti hai jo dikhati hain ki kaunse input features model ke liye overall aur specific predictions ke liye sabse important hain.

  • Global explainability: global explanations compute karne ke liye CREATE MODEL query ko modify karke ek additional option add karna padta hai jo global explainability enable karta hai: enable_global_explanation = TRUE. Global explainability feature ka model par overall influence return karta hai, jo aksar pure dataset par feature attributions ko aggregate karke milta hai. Higher absolute value ka matlab hai feature ka model ki predictions par zyada influence tha.
  • Local explanations: local explanations ko global explanations enable kiye bina bhi compute kiya ja sakta hai.

CREATE MODEL statement modify karna

Original CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL query ko naye query window me copy karo aur enable_global_explain=TRUE add karke modify karo:

CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL data_driven_ml.energy_production OPTIONS
(model_type='linear_reg',
input_label_cols=['Energy_Production'],
enable_global_explain=TRUE) AS
SELECT
  Temp,
  Ambient_Pressure,
  Relative_Humidity,
  Exhaust_Vacuum,
  Energy_Production
FROM
  `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_cleaned`

Is altered query ko run karke global explanations enabled ke saath model ka naya version train karo — isme sirf kuch minutes lagne chahiye.

ML.GLOBAL_EXPLAIN function — global explanations

SELECT
  *
FROM
  ML.GLOBAL_EXPLAIN(MODEL `data_driven_ml.energy_production`)

ML.GLOBAL_EXPLAIN function model ko call karke results retrieve karti hai. Results me features unke largest importance scores ke saath dikhte hain. Correlation se pehle ki analysis ke basis par tum expect karoge ki Temp feature ka sabse bada attribution score hoga — aur yahan ye confirm hota hai. ML.GLOBAL_EXPLAIN global feature attributions return karta hai jo evaluation dataset ki saari rows ke liye har feature ko milne wale mean absolute attribution se milte hain.

ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT function — local explanations

Yaad karo pehle wala example: temperature 27.45°C, ambient pressure 1,001.23 millibar, relative humidity 84% aur exhaust vacuum 65.12 cm Hg par energy production 433.35 MW predict hui thi. Tum expect karte ho ki global feature attributions ke basis par temperature ka sabse bada impact hoga — lekin global explanations poore dataset par aggregate karte hain. Is specific example ke baare me kya?

ML.PREDICT method ko ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT method se replace karo taaki prediction ke saath local feature attributions bhi return hon:

SELECT
  *
FROM
  ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT(
  MODEL `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.energy_production`,
  (
  SELECT
    Temp,
    Ambient_Pressure,
    Relative_Humidity,
    Exhaust_Vacuum
  FROM
    `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_cleaned`),
  STRUCT(3 AS top_k_features) )
  • STRUCT(3 AS top_k_features): ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT ka additional argument hai jo feature attributions ke output ko top three features tak restrict karta hai. STRUCT ko SQL me values (ya columns) ki list ke roop me socha ja sakta hai, jinke specific naam aur possibly alag types hote hain.
  • top_feature_attributions: ye khud ek STRUCT hai jisme do fields hain — feature (corresponding feature name) aur attribution (us instance ke liye attribution value).
  • baseline_prediction_value: ye ek baseline deta hai jisse local feature attributions ke liye apne instance ko compare kiya ja sake. Linear regression models ke case me ye baseline dataset ke across average label value (energy production) hai.
  • Is example me interpretation: predicted label baseline prediction se kam hai, aur attributions sab negative hain. Temperature value baseline value se lagbhag 18.52 MW ki decrease ke liye account karti hai, relative humidity lagbhag 2.16 MW ki, aur ambient pressure lagbhag 0.31 MW ki. Exhaust vacuum pressure top three me nahi tha, lekin is example ke liye uska contribution ambient pressure se bhi chhota tha. Matlab, is example me baseline energy production se zyada tar deviation temperature ki wajah se tha, baaki features ke kuch minor contributions ke saath.

Shapley values: "on average" phrase thoda odd lag sakta hai. BigQuery ML linear models ke liye attributions compute karne ke liye Shapley values use karta hai. Shapley values coalitional game theory ka ek tool hai jo alag-alag coalitions — tumhare interested feature value aur kisi baseline feature value ke alag-alag combinations — ke across feature values ke average contribution ko compute karta hai. Linear models ke liye inhe local explanations ke liye simply us feature se corresponding weight aur feature value ke terms me compute kiya ja sakta hai.

Jupyter Notebooks me explainability ke liye LIME aur SHAP jaise popular Python libraries bhi hain, jo alag-alag use cases me commonly use hoti hain. Inki full discussion is book ke scope se bahar hai.

Yaad rakho: Global explanation batata hai ki model overall kis feature par bharosa karta hai, local explanation batata hai ki is ek prediction me kis feature ne kya kiya. Dono ko saath me dekhna chahiye — ek prediction me temperature dominate kar sakta hai, jabki kisi aur prediction me koi aur feature aage aa sakta hai.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 6 — Using BigQuery ML to Train a Linear Regression Model
← Previous06.3 · CREATE MODEL Statement — Model Banana→ Next06.5 · Neural Networks BigQuery ML me
06.5Chapter 6 · Using BigQuery ML to Train a Linear Regression Model

Neural Networks BigQuery ML me

Linear regression ke baad ab tum ek aur popular ML model type dekhte ho — neural networks. Ye pichle decade me bahut popular hue hain, additional compute resources, naye model architectures, aur transfer learning ke roop me ek problem se dusri problem me knowledge apply karne ki flexibility ki wajah se.

Neural networks kya hain — linear regression se shuru karo

Linear regression ki tarah, neural networks bhi mathematical functions hain jo numeric feature values ko inputs ke roop me lete hain aur label ke liye prediction output karte hain. Neural networks regression aur classification, dono problems ke liye use ho sakte hain, lekin is section me focus regression models par hai.

Energy production predict karne ke problem ke liye chaar features hain — temperature, ambient pressure, relative humidity aur exhaust vacuum pressure. Inhe x1, x2, x3 aur x4 kaho. In chaar features ko use karne wala linear regression model is form ka hoga: f(x) = y = w0 + w1x1 + w2x2 + w3x3 + w4x4. Ise ek network ke roop me visualize karo: har feature ke liye ek vertex aur output y ke liye ek vertex banao, feature vertices se output vertex tak arrows banao, aur un edges ko weights w1, w2, w3 aur w4 se label karo. Bias w0 ko is representation me aksar draw nahi kiya jata.

Hidden layer kya hai

Ab maan lo tum original features ko combine karke naye hidden features z1 aur z2 banana chahte ho, jahan har hidden feature original features ka linear combination hai — matlab features ka weighted sum, jaise z1 = c0 + c1x1 + c2x2 + c3x3 + c4x4, jahan ci kuch real numbers hain. Hidden feature z2 ki similar definition hogi, alag constants (di) ke saath.

  • Hidden features ko saath me hidden layer kehte hain. Ye hidden hain kyunki tum inhe model ke input ya output me nahi dekhte, lekin ye inputs se output compute karne me role play karte hain.
  • Visual representation: feature vertices hidden features z1 aur z2 se connect hote hain, aur hidden features output y se connect hote hain. Ye ek hidden layer wala neural network hai.
  • Best values kaise dhoondhein: ci aur di ki best values kaise pata karein? Neural networks ke liye koi normal equation nahi hai, lekin tum gradient descent use kar sakte ho — ci aur di ko linear regression ke baaki weights ki tarah treat karo aur model ko train karke best weights dhoondho.

Activation functions aur nonlinearity — sabse important idea

Abhi neural network puzzle ka ek piece missing hai. Maan lo f(x) = 3 + 2x aur g(x) = 1 + 5x hain. g(f(x)) kya hoga? Inner function ka output lekar dusre function me plug karo: g(f(x)) = g(3 + 2x) = 1 + 5(3 + 2x) = 16 + 10x. Dhyaan do — f(x) aur g(x) mx + b form ke linear functions hain, aur final answer g(f(x)) bhi usi form ka linear function hai (sirf alag m aur b ke saath). Ye coincidence nahi hai — generally, linear functions ka composition hamesha linear hota hai.

Neural network se iska kya connection hai? Hidden features z1 aur z2 x1, x2, x3 aur x4 ke linear functions hain; y, z1 aur z2 ka linear function hai. Tum apne neural network ko do linear functions ke composition ke roop me soch sakte ho — pehla x1, x2, x3, x4 ko z1, z2 me le jata hai, aur dusra z1, z2 ko y me le jata hai. Dono functions linear hain, isliye composition bhi linear hai. Tumne y ko x1, x2, x3 aur x4 ke linear function ke roop me likhne ka ek zyada complicated tareeka dhoondh liya — bas!

  • Toh kya hidden layers wale neural networks bekaar hain? Bilkul nahi — lekin unhe interesting banane ke liye ek aur cheez add karni padti hai: ek nonlinear activation function.
  • Activation functions: ye functions hidden layers ke features par apply kiye jate hain, un values ko agle layer me pass karne se pehle. Isse ek layer se dusre layer tak jaane wale functions ab linear nahi rehte, aur model zyada interesting behavior seekh sakta hai.
  • ReLU: neural networks ke liye sabse common (aur sabse simple) activation function rectified linear unit function hai, ya ReLU. ReLU ek bahut simple function hai jo ek single value leta hai aur wo value return karta hai agar wo positive hai, ya 0 return karta hai agar wo negative hai.
  • Activation functions kahan apply hote hain: activation functions aksar hidden layers par apply honge, lekin regression problems ke liye output par nahi. ReLU activation wale resulting functions ab bhi piecewise linear hote hain, lekin linear na hone ka matlab hai ki tum zyada complicated functions model kar sakte ho.
  • Multiple hidden layers: tum jitni chaho utni hidden layers wala neural network bana sakte ho. Do hidden layers hone par pehli hidden layer ke features original input features se seekhe jate hain, aur dusri hidden layer ke features pehli hidden layer ke hidden features se seekhe jate hain. Tum ise model ke inputs aur outputs ko dekh kar seedha nahi dekh sakte, lekin ye correspond karta hai ki neural networks ek layer se dusri layer tak concepts kaise build karte hain aur aakhir me inhe final output compute karne ke liye apply karte hain.
  • Trade-off: zyada hidden layers se zyada powerful models bante hain, lekin unme optimize karne ke liye zyada weights hote hain aur isliye train karne ke liye zyada data aur time chahiye hota hai. Chhote neural networks (kam hidden layers) train karne me easy hote hain, lekin bade networks ke mukable me utne complex relationships seekh nahi sakte.

Deep neural network train karna BigQuery ML me

Concepts thode zyada complicated hain, lekin SQL syntax pehle jitna hi simple hai — sirf kuch chhote differences ke saath:

CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL data_driven_ml.energy_production_nn
OPTIONS
(model_type='dnn_regressor',
hidden_units=[32,16,8],
input_label_cols=['Energy_Production']) AS
SELECT
  Temp,
  Ambient_Pressure,
  Relative_Humidity,
  Exhaust_Vacuum,
  Energy_Production
FROM
  `your-project-id.data_driven_ml.ccpp_cleaned`
  • model_type='dnn_regressor': deep neural network regression models ke liye model type hai. Yahan "deep" ka matlab hai ki neural network me koi bhi sankhya me hidden layers ho sakti hain — matlab ye kai layers deep ho sakta hai.
  • hidden_units=[32,16,8]: hidden unit ya neuron, hidden features ke liye zyada technical aur commonly use hone wala term hai. hidden_units option integers ka array expect karta hai — is case me array [32,16,8] diya gaya hai. Iska matlab hai neural network me teen hidden layers hain: pehli hidden layer me 32 neurons, dusri me 16 neurons, aur teesri me 8 neurons.
  • Training time zyada hai: ye model train hone me zyada time lega, model zyada complex hone ki wajah se aur isliye bhi kyunki BigQuery data ko Vertex AI me export karke Vertex AI training se neural network train kar raha hai.

Results — neural network linear regression se thoda worse kyun raha

Model train hone ke baad model par jao aur Evaluation tab me evaluation metrics dekho. Tumhare metrics figure me dikhaye gaye metrics se differ kar sakte hain.

  • Naya neural network model linear regression model se mean squared error (aur RMSE, kyunki RMSE mean squared error ka square root hai) ke basis par slightly worse perform kiya. Ye overfitting ka ek example hai.
  • Overfitting: model training set ke data ke labels ko zyada accurately predict kar sakta hai, lekin ye overall trend miss karne ki keemat par aata hai. Example ke liye, ek overfitting model data points ko closely follow karta hai lekin overall quadratic trend ko miss kar deta hai.
  • Underfitting: model bahut simple hai aur data ke trends seekh nahi sakta. Example ke liye, agar linear model use kiya gaya ho, to model data ke quadratic trend ko seekh nahi payega.
  • Overfitting check karna: ML models train karte waqt tumhe training dataset aur evaluation dataset par performance compare karni chahiye, taaki ensure ho sake ki model overfit to nahi kar raha. Tum isse model architecture alter karke, early stopping use karke, ya alag-alag regularization techniques se approach kar sakte ho. Regularization un techniques ka blanket term hai jo models me overfitting se ladte hain. Chapter 8 me inme se kuch techniques ko BigQuery ML samet alag-alag frameworks ke liye detail me discuss kiya gaya hai.

Hyperparameters kya hain

Ek bada sawaal ye hai: tumhe kaise pata chalega ki hidden layers aur neurons ki best sankhya kya hai? Tum hidden_units option ke liye alag-alag lists try kar sakte ho aur dekh sakte ho ki kya best perform karta hai, lekin theory me infinite possibilities hain.

  • Hyperparameters: hidden layers ki sankhya, per layer neurons ki sankhya, aur kaunsa activation function use hota hai — ye sab hyperparameters ke examples hain. Hyperparameters parameters (jaise weights) se alag hote hain — ye model train hone se pehle set kiye jate hain. Hyperparameters model architecture, training process aur aur bhi bahut kuch define karte hain, aur parameters wo hote hain jo training process ke dauraan optimize kiye jate hain taaki in hyperparameters se defined best model dhoondha ja sake.
  • Chapter 8 me: BigQuery ML, Vertex AI aur dusre popular ML frameworks me apne model ke liye best hyperparameters dhoondhne ke alag-alag methods explore kiye jate hain.
  • Exercises: ek bada neural network train karo — har layer me additional neurons add karo ya additional layers add karo — model performance par kya effect pada? Ek chhota neural network train karo — neurons ya layers hatao — performance par kya effect pada? Discuss kiye gaye explainability functions use karke explore karo ki kaunse features ne model ki performance me globally aur locally sabse zyada contribute kiya — koi surprises hain?
Yaad rakho: Zyada complex model hamesha behtar nahi hota. Is chapter me simple linear regression ne deep neural network ko hara diya — kyunki data me relationship lagbhag linear hi thi, aur bada model sirf training data ko yaad karne (overfit karne) laga. Hamesha simple model se shuru karo aur use baseline banao.

07Chapter 7 · Training Custom ML Models in Python

Python me Custom ML Models Train Karna

Is chapter me tum customer churn predict karne ke liye classification models banate ho — Python ki do popular libraries, scikit-learn aur Keras, se. Pehle Pandas se data explore aur clean karte ho, phir scikit-learn se logistic regression train karte ho, aur phir wahi kaam Keras neural network se karte ho.

Business use case: customer churn prediction

  • Churn ka matlab: customer churn woh rate hai jis par customers service chhod dete hain — yahan matlab hai ki customer agle month me apna subscription ya contract cancel kar de.
  • Dataset: IBM Telco Customer Churn dataset — ML seekhne ke liye ek bahut popular dataset. Isme 7,043 rows aur 21 columns hain, aur data CSV file me milta hai.
  • Columns: customerID, gender, SeniorCitizen, Partner, Dependents, tenure, PhoneService, MultipleLines, InternetService, OnlineSecurity, OnlineBackup, DeviceProtection, TechSupport, StreamingTV, StreamingMovies, Contract, PaperlessBilling, PaymentMethod, MonthlyCharges, TotalCharges, aur label Churn.
  • Numeric ya categorical: kuch columns numeric hain (jaise tenure, MonthlyCharges, TotalCharges) aur baaki categorical hain, jahan value ek fixed set me se ek hoti hai.

No-code, low-code ya custom code — kab kya chunna hai

  • No-code solutions: best hain jab tumhare paas ML expertise nahi hai, ya jab tumhe rapid prototyping karni hai. AutoML jaise solutions feature engineering aur hyperparameter tuning khud sambhalte hain, isliye jaldi benchmark model mil jata hai. Aksar ye production me bhi kaafi hote hain.
  • Low-code solutions: best hain jab tumhe thodi customization chahiye aur tumhara data tool ki constraints me fit hota hai. Jaise structured data aur supported problem type ho to BigQuery ML bahut accha choice hai — model banane me kam time, data aur tuning par zyada time.
  • Custom code solutions: sabse flexible hain. TensorFlow, XGBoost, PyTorch aur scikit-learn se tum kisi bhi type ke data par, apne objective ke saath model bana sakte ho. Custom transformation ho ya web app me deploy karna ho — sab possible hai. Sahi data, expertise aur time ho to best results bhi yahi deta hai.
  • Kaise decide karo: koi ek sahi jawab nahi hai. Dekho tumhare paas train, tune aur deploy karne ka kitna time hai, dataset aur problem objective kya hai, aur tumhari apni expertise kya hai. Agar tum SQL bahut acchi tarah jante ho lekin Python me naye ho, to BigQuery ML behtar ho sakta hai — agar woh tumhara problem support karta ho.

Colab me shuruaat: packages aur data load karna

  • Notebook: Google Colab par naya notebook kholo aur uska naam rakho, jaise Customer_Churn_Model.ipynb.
  • Imports: Matplotlib, NumPy, Pandas, Seaborn, scikit-learn aur TensorFlow import karte ho.
  • scikit-learn: pehli baar 2007 me release hua tha, NumPy aur SciPy par bana hai. Linear models, tree-based models aur support vector machines ke liye easy-to-use framework hai.
  • TensorFlow: deep neural networks train aur deploy karne ke liye high-performance numerical computation library hai. Keras uska hissa hai, jo neural networks banana aasan karta hai.
  • Version check: har package ka __version__ attribute version batata hai — isse confirm karte ho ki imports sahi chale.
  • CSV seedha internet se: Pandas CSV file ko download kiye bina seedha URL se DataFrame me load kar sakta hai — pd.read_csv() se.
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import sklearn
import tensorflow as tf

file_loc = 'https://storage.googleapis.com/low-code-ai-book/churn_dataset.csv'
df_raw = pd.read_csv(file_loc)
df_raw.head()

Pehle kuch rows dekhna (head()) ek accha quick first step hai, lekin poora dataset sirf kuch rows se zyada hai — problems aisi jagah bhi chhupi ho sakti hain jo tumne dekhi hi nahi.

Yaad rakho: Custom code sabse zyada flexible hai, lekin usme sabse zyada seekhne aur time lagane ki cost bhi hai. No-code se jaldi benchmark milta hai, aur incremental performance gain aksar production me jaldi pahunchne ke fayde se chhota hota hai.

def transform_fn(df):

  df = df.replace({'TotalCharges': {' ': 0.0}})
  df = df.astype({'TotalCharges':'float64'})

  df['AvgMonthlyCharge']= df['TotalCharges'].div(df['tenure'],
                                                      fill_values=0.0)

  df['DiffCharges'] = df['MonthlyCharges']-df['AvgMonthlyCharge']

  df['DiffBuckets'] = pd.cut(df['DiffCharges'], bins=5)

  df = df.drop(columns=['AvgMonthlyCharge', 'gender','StreamingTV',
                            'StreamingMovies','PhoneService',
                            'customerID', 'DiffCharges'])
  return df

numeric_columns = ['SeniorCitizen', 'tenure', 'MonthlyCharges']
categorical_columns = ['Partner', 'Dependents', 'MultipleLines',
                      'InternetService','OnlineSecurity',
                      'OnlineBackup', 'DeviceProtection',
                      'TechSupport','Contract',
                      'PaperlessBilling','PaymentMethod',
                      'DiffBuckets']

from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.preprocessing import FunctionTransformer


fn_transformer = FunctionTransformer(transform_fn)
col_transformer = ColumnTransformer(
  [('ohe', OneHotEncoder(drop='if_binary'), categorical_columns),
  ('sca', MinMaxScaler(), numeric_columns)])
model = LogisticRegression()

from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline

pipe = Pipeline([('preproc', fn_transformer),
                 ('col_trans', col_transformer),
                 ('model', model)])

y_test_enc = le.transform(y_test)

le.inverse_transform([1])

import tensorflow as tf
import tensorflow.keras as keras

train_dataset = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((X_train_scaled, y_train_enc)).batch(128)

test_dataset = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((X_test_scaled, y_test_enc)).batch(1)

keras.layers.Dense(
            units=64, input_shape=(29,), activation="relu",
            name="input_layer"
        )

model = keras.Sequential(
    [
        keras.layers.Dense(
            units=64, input_shape=(29,), activation="relu",
            name="input_layer"
        ),
        keras.layers.Dense(units=32, activation="relu",
                           name="hidden_1"),
        keras.layers.Dense(units=16, activation="relu",
                           name="hidden_2"),
        keras.layers.Dense(units=1, activation="sigmoid",
                           name="output"),
    ]
)

loss_fn = keras.losses.BinaryCrossentropy()
metrics = [tf.keras.metrics.BinaryAccuracy(),
           tf.keras.metrics.Precision(),
           tf.keras.metrics.Recall()]

model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss=loss_fn, metrics=metrics)

history = model.fit(
    x=train_dataset,
    epochs=20,
    validation_data=test_dataset
)

early_stopping = keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(patience=5,restore_best_weights=True)

history = model.fit(
    x=train_dataset,
    epochs=100,
    validation_data=test_dataset,
    callbacks = [early_stopping]
)

model.evaluate(x=test_dataset)

07.1Chapter 7 · Training Custom ML Models in Python

Customer Churn Dataset — Clean aur Transform

Model train karne se pehle sabse zyada kaam data ko samajhne aur saaf karne me jata hai. Is section me tum data types check karte ho, ek chhupi hui missing-value problem pakadte ho, summary statistics dekhte ho, aur features ke beech ke relationships explore karte ho.

Data types check karna — TotalCharges ki problem

  • df_raw.dtypes: ye property (function nahi, isliye parentheses nahi) har column ka data type batati hai. Jo float ya integer nahi tha, woh object ke roop me aaya — ye Pandas me normal hai.
  • Problem: lagbhag har column expected type se match karta hai, sirf TotalCharges nahi — woh float64 hone ki bajay object hai. Ye sign hai ki is column me kuch alag hai.
  • describe(): TotalCharges par describe() chalane se pata chalta hai ki sabse frequent value ek khaali string hai — ek single space — jo 11 baar aati hai.
  • Mask se jaanch: mask = (df_raw['TotalCharges']==' ') se un rows ko dekhte ho. In sabhi rows me tenure ki value 0 hai.
  • Wajah: tenure 0 ka matlab hai ye customer ka telco ke saath pehla month hai — unhe abhi tak charge hi nahi kiya gaya, isliye TotalCharges khaali hai.
  • Fix: khaali string ko float 0.0 se replace karte ho, phir astype({'TotalCharges':'float64'}) se column ko float bana dete ho.
df_1 = df_raw.replace({'TotalCharges': {' ': 0.0}})
df_2 = df_1.astype({'TotalCharges': 'float64'})
df_2.describe()

Summary statistics — numeric columns

  • 7,043 rows: har column me 7,043 elements hain, aur koi null values nahi hain.
  • tenure: mean 32.37 months, min 0, max 72 months.
  • MonthlyCharges: mean 64.76, min 18.25, max 118.75.
  • TotalCharges: mean 2,279.73, min 0, max 8,684.80.
  • SeniorCitizen: mean 0.162 hai — matlab lagbhag 16.2% customers senior citizens hain. Ye binary 0/1 column hai, isliye mean bhi useful information deta hai.
  • Categorical stats: describe(include='object') se categorical columns ki count, unique values, sabse frequent value aur uski frequency milti hai.
  • Churn label: thoda unbalanced hai — No aur Yes ka ratio lagbhag 5:2 hai.
  • customerID: unique values utne hi hain jitni rows — har value unique hai.

Categorical columns ke combinations dekhna

  • PhoneService vs MultipleLines: value_counts() se pata chalta hai ki MultipleLines ki value "No phone service" sirf tabhi aati hai jab PhoneService "No" ho. Matlab MultipleLines me PhoneService ki poori information hai — PhoneService redundant hai, use training se hata denge.
  • InternetService: jab InternetService "No" hota hai, to OnlineSecurity, OnlineBackup, StreamingTV, StreamingMovies, DeviceProtection aur TechSupport sab "No internet service" hote hain. Fiber optic aur DSL ke case me picture utni clear nahi hai.
  • Chi-square test aur Cramer's V: categorical features ke beech correlation samajhne ke aur techniques bhi hain — chi-square test independence check karta hai, aur Cramer's V us relationship ki strength batata hai, jaise numeric variables ke liye Pearson correlation hota hai.
  • Contract vs Churn: stacked bar chart se dikhta hai ki month-to-month contract par 40% se zyada customers churn karte hain, one-year par lagbhag 15%, aur two-year par 5% se kam. Contract ek bahut useful feature hoga.

Churn se jude observations

  • Senior citizens: unka churn rate non-seniors se lagbhag double hai.
  • Gender, StreamingTV, StreamingMovies: inka churn rate par koi farak nahi dikhta.
  • Bada household: partner ya dependents hone se churn rate kam hota hai.
  • Multiple lines: phone line walon me multiple lines hone se churn rate badhta hai.
  • InternetService: fiber optic ka churn rate DSL se bahut zyada hai; bina internet walon ka sabse kam hai.
  • Add-ons: OnlineSecurity aur DeviceProtection jaise add-ons se churn rate kam hota hai.
  • PaperlessBilling: isse churn rate badhta hai. PaymentMethod me Electronic Check ka churn rate baaki methods se bahut zyada hai.

Numeric aur categorical ka interaction — DiffCharges

  • Idea: agar monthly charge kabhi na badle to tenure × MonthlyCharges = TotalCharges hona chahiye. Naye columns banate ho: AvgMonthlyCharge = TotalCharges / tenure, aur DiffCharges = MonthlyCharges − AvgMonthlyCharge.
  • NaN problem: tenure 0 wali 11 rows me divide-by-zero se NaN aata hai. replace(np.nan, 0) se use 0 kar dete ho — ye imputation hai, matlab unknown value ko reasonable value se replace karna. Yahan "koi difference nahi" ek reasonable assumption hai, warna tum wo useful rows kho dete.
  • Bucketization: pd.cut() se numeric column ko buckets me baant te ho — numeric feature categorical ban jata hai. DiffCharges ko 5 buckets me baantne par dikhta hai ki MonthlyCharges aur average charge ke beech bada difference (positive ya negative, dono taraf) hone par churn rate zyada hota hai.
  • MonthlyCharges: 3 buckets me baantne par churn rate charges ke saath badhta dikhta hai — sabse zyada churn 85.25 se 118.75 ke range me hai.
  • Bucket count: bahut kam buckets se important patterns miss ho sakte hain, bahut zyada se pattern noise me kho jata hai.
  • tenure aur TotalCharges: dono badhne par churn rate kam hota hai, aur inke beech correlation lagbhag 0.82 hai — bahut zyada correlated hain.
Yaad rakho: Missing value milte hi use delete mat karo — pehle poochho "yahan kya hona chahiye tha?" Yahan 11 khaali TotalCharges values ka matlab tha tenure 0, aur sahi fix 0.0 tha, rows delete karna nahi.

← Previous07 · Python me Custom ML Models Train Karna→ Next07.2 · Logistic Regression — Scikit-Learn se
07.2Chapter 7 · Training Custom ML Models in Python

Logistic Regression — Scikit-Learn se

Data explore karne ke baad ab tum features select karte ho, categorical features ko one-hot encoding se numeric banate ho, data ko train-test me baant te ho, aur scikit-learn se apna pehla logistic regression model train karte ho.

Feature selection — kya hatana hai

  • Copy pehle: df_2.copy() se copy banate ho aur usi me columns drop karte ho, taaki original data hamesha accessible rahe.
  • Non-predictive: gender, StreamingTV aur StreamingMovies ka churn rate par koi farak nahi dikha — inhe hata dete ho.
  • Redundant: PhoneService MultipleLines me already captured hai — use bhi hata dete ho, warna collinearity ki problem hogi. Collinearity ka matlab hai predictor variables ke beech high correlation, jisse regression coefficients ke estimates unreliable aur unstable ho jate hain — linear models me ye problem aur bhi badh jati hai.
  • customerID: ye har row ko uniquely identify karta hai. Model is value ko Churn se seedha jodna seekh lega, jo training data par to accha lagega, lekin naye customerID par bilkul kaam nahi karega. Isliye ise bhi drop karte ho.
  • TotalCharges: tenure se bahut zyada correlated (0.82) hai, isliye use bhi hata dete ho. DiffBuckets rakhte ho, baaki banaye hue intermediate columns hata dete ho.
  • Final: 15 feature columns aur 1 label, Churn, bachte hain.

One-hot encoding — categorical ko numeric banana

  • Idea: InternetService ke teen values No, DSL aur Fiber Optic ki one-hot encoding [1,0,0], [0,1,0] aur [0,0,1] hoti hai — har possible value ke liye ek naya column, jisme poochha jata hai "kya value ye hai?"
  • Binary features: Partner, Dependents, OnlineSecurity, OnlineBackup, DeviceProtection, TechSupport aur PaperlessBilling binary hain. Pehle "No internet service" ko "No" se replace karte ho, taaki ye columns sahi me binary ban jayein.
  • drop='if_binary': binary feature ko poori one-hot encoding ki bajay 0 ya 1 se replace kar deta hai.
  • fit_transform: fit ka matlab hai encoder feature values seekhta hai, transform ka matlab hai unhe encode karta hai. Baad me inverse_transform() se encoded values ko wapas original values me badal sakte ho.
  • Combine: numeric features aur encoded categorical features ko np.concatenate(..., axis=1) se side-by-side jodte ho. axis=1 columns jodta hai, axis=0 rows stack karta hai.
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder
numeric_columns = ['SeniorCitizen', 'tenure', 'MonthlyCharges']
categorical_columns = ['Partner', 'Dependents', 'MultipleLines',
    'InternetService', 'OnlineSecurity', 'OnlineBackup',
    'DeviceProtection', 'TechSupport', 'Contract',
    'PaperlessBilling', 'PaymentMethod', 'DiffBuckets']
ohe = OneHotEncoder(drop='if_binary')
X_cat_trans = ohe.fit_transform(X_cat)
X = np.concatenate((X_num.values, X_cat_trans.toarray()), axis=1)
y = df_prep['Churn'].values

Train-test split — generalization ke liye

  • train_test_split: scikit-learn ke model_selection module ka helper function hai. test_size=0.20 se 20% data test ke liye rakha jata hai.
  • random_state=113: isse split reproducible hota hai — dobara chalane par wahi rows train aur test me aayengi.
  • Sizes: training dataset me 5,634 examples aur 29 features hain one-hot encoding ke baad; test dataset me 1,409 examples hain.

Logistic regression — kaise kaam karta hai

  • Goal: do classes me se ek ki membership predict karna — yahan churn (Yes = 1, positive class) ya no-churn (No = 0, negative class). Output positive class ki predicted probability hoti hai.
  • Sigmoid function: linear combination f(x) = w0 + w1x1 + ... + wnxn ko sigmoid se pass karte ho: g(x) = 1 / (1 + exp(−f(x))). Iske values hamesha 0 aur 1 ke beech rehte hain, isliye use probability ki tarah interpret kar sakte ho.
  • Cross-entropy loss: linear regression me mean squared error use hota tha, yahan cross-entropy use hoti hai. Model 100% confident aur sahi ho to loss zero hota hai; confidence galat taraf badhe to loss tezi se badhta hai. Example: predicted probability 0.6 aur actual label 1 ho to contribution log(0.6) ≈ −0.222 hoti hai; 0.4 ho to log(0.4) ≈ −0.398 — matlab galat confidence par loss zyada.
  • Information theory: cross-entropy wahan se aayi hai — ye measure karti hai ki ek event ko represent karne ke liye kitni information chahiye jab tum ek probability distribution assume kar rahe ho lekin actual distribution alag hai.

Training — scaling ki wajah se convergence problem

  • Pehla attempt: LogisticRegression() bana kar fit(X_train, y_train) chalate ho to ConvergenceWarning aata hai — lbfgs iterations ki limit tak pahunch gaya, kyunki loss me improvement bahut chhota (default 10⁻⁴) nahi hua.
  • Wajah: features ke ranges bahut alag hain. Gradient descent ko samjho katori me ball ludhkane jaisa — gol katori me ball seedha neeche aati hai, lekin andakar (oblong) katori me woh idhar-udhar oscillate karti hai. Alag scales par curvature constant nahi rehta, isliye gradient descent wobble karta hai aur zyada iterations leta hai.
  • Fix: MinMaxScaler() se features ko 0 aur 1 ke beech rescale karte ho. Is baar model converge kar jata hai — ye ML me general best practice hai, sirf logistic regression ke liye nahi.
  • Training-serving skew: pehle test accuracy sirf lagbhag 48% aayi — coin flip se bhi behtar nahi! Wajah: training data scale kiya tha, test data nahi. Model ko woh range hi nahi mili jiski use training me aadat thi. Sahi tareeka: test data par scaler.transform() lagao (fit dobara nahi), to accuracy lagbhag 80% ho jati hai.
from sklearn.preprocessing import MinMaxScaler
scaler = MinMaxScaler()
X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
cls = LogisticRegression()
cls.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)

X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
cls.score(X_test_scaled, y_test)
Yaad rakho: Training time par fit_transform() use karo, prediction time par sirf transform() — transformer ko dobara fit karna training-serving skew paida karta hai aur results galat dikhata hai.

07.3Chapter 7 · Training Custom ML Models in Python

Classification Evaluation Metrics

Accuracy ek simple metric hai, lekin sirf accuracy dekhna kaafi nahi hai. Tumhara model 80% accurate hai — lekin kya woh business ke liye useful hai? Ye jaanne ke liye confusion matrix, precision aur recall dekhne padte hain.

Accuracy akeli kyun kaafi nahi

  • Tumhara model: test accuracy lagbhag 80% hai.
  • Baseline: ek model jo hamesha "no churn" predict kare, uski accuracy lagbhag 73.5% hogi — kyunki zyada customers churn nahi karte.
  • Business value: 80% vs 73.5% ka farak chhota lagta hai, lekin "no churn" wala model kabhi koi actionable insight nahi dega — woh ek bhi chhodne wale customer ko pakad hi nahi sakta, isliye uski business value practically zero hai.

Confusion matrix — chaar numbers me poori kahani

  • True positives (TP): actual churn, predicted churn. False negatives (FN): actual churn, predicted no-churn — ye chhoote hue customers hain.
  • False positives (FP): actual no-churn, predicted churn. True negatives (TN): actual no-churn, predicted no-churn.
  • Tumhara model: confusion matrix [[187, 185], [98, 939]] hai. Test set me 372 customers ne service chhodi (187 + 185) aur 1,037 ne rakhi (98 + 939).
  • Padhna: model ne 187 churners ko sahi pakda (TP), 185 ko miss kar diya (FN), 939 non-churners ko sahi pehchana (TN), aur 98 ko galat churner bataya (FP).
from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix
y_pred = cls.predict(X_test_scaled)
confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred, labels=['Yes', 'No'])

Precision aur recall

  • Recall (true positive rate): jin customers ne sach me account cancel kiya, unme se kitne percent ko model ne sahi pakda. Churn rokne ke liye ye bahut important hai — tum thodi accuracy ya precision sacrifice karke bhi recall badhana chahoge.
  • Precision (positive predictive power): jin customers ko model ne churner bataya, unme se kitne percent ne sach me cancel kiya.
  • Tumhare numbers: Precision 0.656 aur Recall 0.503 — matlab predicted churners me se 65.6% ne sach me cancel kiya, aur actual churners me se sirf 50.3% pakde gaye. Abhi improvement ki jagah hai, lekin ye model "no churn" wale model se bahut zyada business value deta hai.
  • Trade-off: recall badhane ke liye tumhe un customers ko bhi contact karna padega jo cancel karne wale nahi the — iska resource cost bhi hota hai, isliye balance chahiye.
from sklearn.metrics import precision_score, recall_score
print("Precision:", precision_score(y_test, y_pred,
      labels=['Yes', 'No'], pos_label='Yes'))
print("Recall:", recall_score(y_test, y_pred,
      labels=['Yes', 'No'], pos_label='Yes'))

Trained model se predictions serve karna

  • Problem: training data CSV me tha, lekin prediction ke liye aane wala data JSON format me ho sakta hai — web applications me ye bahut common hai.
  • Steps dobara: prediction time par wahi saare steps karne hote hain — TotalCharges ko float banana, DiffBuckets banana, extra columns drop karna, one-hot encoding aur min-max scaling.
  • JSON parse: json.loads() se JSON string ko Python dictionary me badalte ho, phir use ek-row DataFrame bana lete ho.
  • Buckets consistent rakho: pd.cut() me bins ki count ki bajay wahi cut points use karte ho jo training time par the — [-18.938, -11.295, -3.69, 3.915, 11.52, 19.125] — taaki buckets bilkul same rahein.
  • Function me band karo: saara preprocessing ek function me daal do, jaise custom_predict_routine(example), taaki prediction time par ek hi call me sab ho jaye.
  • Model save karna: joblib.dump(cls, 'filename.joblib') se trained model ko disk par save karte ho aur joblib.load() se wapas load karte ho. Ye sirf model ke liye nahi — transformers aur baaki objects ke liye bhi kaam karta hai.
  • Environment alag ho sakta hai: aksar predictions alag environment se serve hote hain — sirf model file nahi, preprocessing code aur transformers bhi saath le jaane hote hain.

Scikit-learn pipelines — sab kuch ek package me

  • Pipeline kya hai: transformers ka sequence, jisme aakhri object model hota hai. fit() saare transformers par fit_transform chalata hai aur phir model ko fit karta hai; predict() saare transformers ke transform order me lagata hai aur phir model se predict karta hai.
  • FunctionTransformer: Pandas wale steps (jo scikit-learn transformers nahi hain) ko pipeline me daalne ke liye use hota hai — ye ek Python function ko transformer bana deta hai.
  • ColumnTransformer: alag columns par alag transformations lagata hai — categorical par OneHotEncoder, numeric par MinMaxScaler.
  • Portability: poori Pipeline ko pickle ya joblib se export kar sakte ho — isme trained model ke saath fit hue transformers bhi hote hain, isliye serving time par consistency bani rehti hai.
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
pipe = Pipeline([('preproc', fn_transformer),
                 ('col_trans', col_transformer),
                 ('model', model)])
Yaad rakho: Accuracy dekh kar khush mat ho jao — pehle poochho ki "hamesha majority class predict karo" wala baseline kitna deta hai. Churn jaise use case me recall hi woh metric hai jo business value batata hai.

07.4Chapter 7 · Training Custom ML Models in Python

Keras se Neural Network Classifier

Scikit-learn se logistic regression ke baad ab tum wahi churn problem Keras se solve karte ho — ek neural network classifier bana kar. Data pehle se prepared hai, isliye tum seedha model definition, training aur evaluation par focus kar sakte ho.

Keras aur TensorFlow — background

  • TensorFlow: late 2015 me aaya tha, free aur open source SDK hai. Naam "tensor" (multi-dimensional array) aur "flow" (computation graph) se bana hai. Graph-based computation se behind-the-scenes optimization aur computation ko multiple devices par baantna aasan hota hai.
  • Keras: pehle ek alag Python interface tha neural networks banane ke liye. TensorFlow 2.0 (2019) se Keras TensorFlow ka official high-level interface ban gaya — building, training aur serving ke liye.
  • Tensor: dimensions wali array hoti hai; dimensions ki count ko rank kehte hain. Text ki ek line rank 1 tensor hai, ek page rank 2, aur ek poori book rank 3.

Labels encode karna aur datasets banana

  • LabelEncoder: Keras me labels string "Yes"/"No" nahi, numeric 1/0 hone chahiye. LabelEncoder se Yes ko 1 aur No ko 0 banate ho — Yes positive class hai.
  • tf.data.Dataset: data ingestion pipelines banane ke liye API hai — data batches me stream hota hai, isliye bade datasets aur multiple machines par training aasan hoti hai. Ye TensorFlow/Keras me best practice mani jati hai.
  • from_tensor_slices: NumPy array ki har row ko ek example manta hai. Features aur labels ka pair pass karte ho.
  • Batch size: training ke liye 128 aur test ke liye 1 rakha hai. Batch size ek hyperparameter hai — bada model ya bada example ho to batch size chhota rakhna chahiye, lekin bahut chhota batch training ko noisy bana deta hai aur converge hone me zyada time lagta hai.
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder
le = LabelEncoder()
y_train_enc = le.fit_transform(y_train)
y_test_enc = le.transform(y_test)

train_dataset = (tf.data.Dataset
    .from_tensor_slices((X_train_scaled, y_train_enc))
    .batch(128))

Model define karna — Sequential API

  • Dense layers: har neuron pichhli layer ke har neuron se connected hota hai — ye weighted sums banate hain.
  • Architecture: teen hidden layers — 64, 32 aur 16 neurons — har ek me ReLU activation. Output layer me 1 neuron aur sigmoid activation, taaki output positive class ki probability ban jaye.
  • input_shape: pehli layer me batana padta hai — yahan (28,) hai, matlab har example me 28 feature values hain one-hot encoding ke baad.
  • Compile: loss BinaryCrossentropy hai (wahi cross-entropy jo logistic regression me thi), metrics BinaryAccuracy, Precision aur Recall hain, aur optimizer Adam hai — neural networks ke liye ek accha default choice.
model = keras.Sequential([
    keras.layers.Dense(units=64, input_shape=(28,),
                       activation="relu", name="input_layer"),
    keras.layers.Dense(units=32, activation="relu", name="hidden_1"),
    keras.layers.Dense(units=16, activation="relu", name="hidden_2"),
    keras.layers.Dense(units=1, activation="sigmoid", name="output"),
])
loss_fn = keras.losses.BinaryCrossentropy()
metrics = [tf.keras.metrics.BinaryAccuracy(),
           tf.keras.metrics.Precision(),
           tf.keras.metrics.Recall()]
model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss=loss_fn, metrics=metrics)

Training — epochs aur early stopping

  • Epoch: poore dataset se ek poora pass. Training set me 5,634 examples aur batch size 128 hai, to ek epoch me 44 batches (steps) hote hain.
  • validation_data: optional argument hai, lekin training aur evaluation metrics ko side-by-side monitor karna acchi practice hai.
  • Converge hone ke signs: ek epoch se dusre epoch me improvement ruk jaye to training converge ho gayi hai. Dusra sign: evaluation dataset par performance bigadne lage — ye overfitting ka sign hai, aur training rok deni chahiye chahe training performance badh hi rahi ho.
  • Early stopping callback: callback training ke alag-alag stages par actions karta hai — jaise har epoch checkpoints save karna, ya performance stall hone par training rokna. patience=5 ka matlab hai 5 epochs tak stalled ya worsening performance ka wait karo; restore_best_weights=True se model apni best performance wale weights par wapas aa jata hai.
  • Training time: 100 epochs tak early stopping ke saath train karne me Colab par kuch minutes lagte hain.
early_stopping = keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(
    patience=5, restore_best_weights=True)
history = model.fit(x=train_dataset, epochs=100,
                    validation_data=test_dataset,
                    callbacks=[early_stopping])

Results — logistic regression se comparison

  • Evaluation: model.evaluate(x=test_dataset) se loss 0.4390, binary_accuracy 0.7928, precision 0.6418 aur recall 0.4866 aaye.
  • Comparison: neural network ki accuracy, precision aur recall teeno logistic regression se thodi kam rahi — iska matlab ye nahi ki neural network automatically behtar ya bura hai, bas ye ki is model ko aur tuning aur feature engineering ki zaroorat hai.
  • Serving: scikit-learn model ke liye banaya gaya custom prediction function dobara use karke Keras model se bhi predictions serve kar sakte ho.
Yaad rakho: Neural network hamesha simple model se behtar nahi hota. Yahan logistic regression ne neural network ko hara diya — model complexity badhane se pehle feature engineering aur tuning par dhyaan do.

07.5Chapter 7 · Training Custom ML Models in Python

Vertex AI par Custom Models

Colab me chhota dataset train karna aasan hai, lekin bade datasets par tumhe zyada compute chahiye hota hai. Vertex AI Training tumhe apna custom code ek containerized environment me, apni pasand ki machines ke cluster par train karne deta hai.

Vertex AI Training kaise kaam karta hai

  • Container: ek aisa computer samjho jisme hardware aur operating system abstract ho gaye hain, taaki developer sirf software par focus kar sake. Standard frameworks ke liye prebuilt containers milte hain — scikit-learn, TensorFlow, XGBoost aur PyTorch ke liye.
  • Resources temporary hote hain: Vertex AI training job ke duration ke liye hi resources provision karta hai, phir unhe hata deta hai. Isliye jo kuch bhi bachana hai — model, metrics — use job khatam hone se pehle Google Cloud Storage me save karna zaroori hai. Fayda ye hai ki tum sirf utne hi resources use karte ho jitne chahiye.
  • Steps: (1) dataset Google Cloud Storage, BigQuery ya Vertex AI managed datasets me available ho; (2) Python code ek single script me ikattha karo; (3) code update karo taaki results Cloud Storage bucket me save hon; (4) source code distribution banao.

Trainer package banana

  • Directory: Colab me !mkdir trainer se directory banate ho — ! ka matlab hai line ko Linux terminal command ki tarah chalao.
  • %%writefile magic: cell ke contents ko execute karne ki bajay file me likhta hai. Isse trainer/trainer.py me poora training code likhte ho — saare imports upar, metrics print karne ke liye print statements, aur aakhir me joblib.dump() se model ko Cloud Storage me save karna.
  • __init__.py: Python ko folder ko package samajhne ke liye is file ki zaroorat hoti hai — ye empty bhi ho sakti hai.
  • setup.py: package sahi tarike se install ho, ye ensure karta hai. Isme package ka naam (churn_sklearn), version (0.1), aur install_requires=['gcsfs'] hota hai taaki Cloud Storage FUSE kaam kare.
  • Source distribution: !python ./setup.py sdist --formats=gztar se tar.gz package banta hai, phir use gcloud storage cp se apne bucket me upload karte ho.
%%writefile setup.py
# Using setuptools to create a source distribution.
from setuptools import find_packages, setup
setup(
    name="churn_sklearn",
    version="0.1",
    packages=find_packages(),
    include_package_data=True,
    install_requires=['gcsfs'],
    description="Training package for customer churn.",
)

Cloud Console me training job submit karna

  • Job settings: Dataset — No managed dataset; Model training method — Custom training (advanced); Model name — churn; Pre-built container — scikit-learn framework, version 0.23; Package location — gs://your-bucket-name/trainer-0.1.tar.gz; Python module — trainer.trainer.
  • Compute: Region woh chuno jo tumhare bucket ke paas ho; Machine type n1-standard-4.
  • Runtime: training pipeline lagbhag 3 minutes me chal jati hai. Logs me print kiye hue metrics dikhte hain — Custom Jobs page par "churn-custom-job" kholo aur "View logs" par click karo.
  • Result: model .joblib file ke roop me save hota hai, jo jahan chahiye load karke predictions serve kar sakta hai.
  • Kab use karo: chhote datasets ke liye local ya Colab kaafi hai — Vertex AI par setup karna overkill lag sakta hai. Lekin dataset badhne par wahi process bade scale par kaam karta hai.
  • Exercise: wahi process Keras model se dobara karo — TensorFlow prebuilt container use karo, preprocessing code reuse karo (TensorFlow images me sklearn bhi hota hai), aur model save karne ke liye model.save() use karo, joblib ki bajay.
Yaad rakho: Vertex AI par resources job ke baad khatam ho jate hain — agar model ya metrics save nahi kiye to sab kuch kho jayega. Training script me print statements aur Cloud Storage save pehle se daal do.

← Previous07.4 · Keras se Neural Network Classifier→ Next08 · Custom Model Performance Improve Karna
08Chapter 8 · Improving Custom Model Performance

Custom Model Performance Improve Karna

Chapters 6 aur 7 me tumne data prepare karna aur custom models banana seekha. Is chapter me tum ek pehle se trained model se shuru karte ho aur use behtar banate ho — feature engineering aur hyperparameter tuning se, scikit-learn, Keras aur BigQuery ML teeno me.

Business use case: used car auction prices

  • Goal: used cars ki auction price (sellingprice) predict karna. Ek colleague ne scikit-learn me linear regression model train kiya hai, lekin woh business goal meet nahi kar raha.
  • Business goal: selling price me RMSE $2,000 ya usse kam hona chahiye — aur woh bhi MMR feature use kiye bina.
  • MMR kya hai: Manheim Market Report — wholesale prices ka leading indicator, jo pichhle 13 months ki 1 crore se zyada sales transactions par based hai. Dataset me MMR values hain, lekin future me ye feature milega ya nahi, ye certain nahi hai — isliye use nahi karna hai.
  • Dataset: 13 columns — year, make, model, trim, body, transmission, state, condition (0 se 5 rating), odometer, color, interior, mmr, aur label sellingprice. Training set me 385,000 rows hain. Data pehle se clean hai — missing aur galat values theek kar di gayi hain.
  • Teammate ka kaam: unhone model training ka code aur data split share kiya hai — aur ek alag test dataset bhi hai jo abhi tak use nahi hua, jisse final model verify karoge.

Train-validation-test split — teen datasets kyun

  • Training dataset: model train karne ke liye.
  • Validation dataset: alag-alag models ko compare karne ke liye. Jo model validation par best ho, wahi "final model" banta hai.
  • Test dataset: final independent check ke liye. Kyunki tumne final model validation performance dekh kar chuna hai, woh validation ki taraf biased ho sakta hai. Agar test par performance validation jaisi hi aaye to model ready hai; agar bahut buri aaye to production me jaane se pehle problem pakdi gayi.
  • Distributions similar honi chahiye: teeno datasets ki data distributions similar honi chahiye — describe(include='all') se check kar sakte ho. Alag distributions test par bade performance drop ki bahut common wajah hoti hain.
  • Reproducibility: team me kaam karte hue randomness se bacho — data split share karna behtar hota hai, ya random seed set karna, taaki comparisons fair rahein.

Baseline model — colleague ka linear regression

  • Data load: teen CSV files wget se download karke Pandas DataFrames me load karte ho — car_prices_train.csv, car_prices_valid.csv, car_prices_test.csv.
  • Unnamed: 0 column: CSV me ek extra column hai jo schema table me nahi thi — ye pehle wale DataFrame ka index hoga jo galti se column ban gaya. Iska target se koi lena-dena nahi, isliye drop kar dete ho.
  • Preprocessing pipeline: FunctionTransformer se Unnamed: 0 aur mmr columns drop karte ho; ColumnTransformer se categorical columns (make, model, trim, body, transmission, state, color, interior) par OneHotEncoder aur numeric columns (year, condition, odometer) par MinMaxScaler lagate ho. OneHotEncoder me handle_unknown='infrequent_if_exist' hai — unknown values ko infrequent category me daal deta hai.
  • Model: LinearRegression() pipeline ke aakhri step me, pipeline.fit(X_train, y_train) se train hota hai.
  • Baseline metrics (validation): R² lagbhag 0.876 — matlab features label ki variability ka 87.6% explain karte hain. RMSE lagbhag $3,384.60 aur MAE lagbhag $2,044.26. Business goal $2,000 RMSE se bahut door hai — ab improvement ki baari hai.
y_train = train_df['sellingprice']
X_train = train_df.drop('sellingprice', axis=1)
model = LinearRegression()
pipeline = Pipeline(steps=[('preproc_cols', preproc_cols),
                            ('col_transformer', col_transformer),
                            ('model', model)])
pipeline.fit(X_train, y_train)
Yaad rakho: Model select karne ke liye validation dataset aur final check ke liye test dataset — dono ka role alag hai. Test dataset ko model chunne me use kar liya to woh independent nahi rehta, aur uski verification ka matlab khatam ho jata hai.
Full code — Chapter 8 sklearn notebook (GitHub)

GitHub: maabel0712/low-code-ai — chapter8/sklearn_model.ipynb

!wget -q https://storage.googleapis.com/low-code-ai-book/car_prices_train.csv
!wget -q https://storage.googleapis.com/low-code-ai-book/car_prices_valid.csv
!wget -q https://storage.googleapis.com/low-code-ai-book/car_prices_test.csv

import pandas as pd

train_df = pd.read_csv('./car_prices_train.csv')
valid_df = pd.read_csv('./car_prices_valid.csv')
test_df = pd.read_csv('./car_prices_test.csv')

train_df.head()

train_df.describe(include='all')

valid_df.describe(include='all')

test_df.describe(include='all')

from sklearn.preprocessing import FunctionTransformer, OneHotEncoder, MinMaxScaler
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline

y_train = train_df['sellingprice']
X_train = train_df.drop('sellingprice', axis=1)

def drop_columns(df, columns):
    return df.drop(columns, axis=1)

preproc_cols = FunctionTransformer(drop_columns, kw_args={"columns":['Unnamed: 0', 'mmr']})

numeric_columns = ['year', 'condition', 'odometer']
categorical_columns = ['make', 'model', 'trim', 'body',
                       'transmission', 'state', 'color', 'interior']

col_transformer = ColumnTransformer(
  [('ohe', OneHotEncoder(drop='if_binary', handle_unknown='infrequent_if_exist'),
      categorical_columns),
   ('minmax', MinMaxScaler(), numeric_columns)])

model = LinearRegression()

pipeline = Pipeline(steps=[('preproc_cols' , preproc_cols),
                           ('col_transformer', col_transformer),
                           ('model', model)])

pipeline.fit(X_train, y_train)

import math
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error, mean_absolute_error

y_valid = valid_df['sellingprice']
X_valid = valid_df.drop('sellingprice', axis=1)

print('R2:', pipeline.score(X_valid, y_valid))
print('RMSE:',math.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_valid, pipeline.predict(X_valid))))
print('MAE:', mean_absolute_error(y_valid, pipeline.predict(X_valid)))

import pandas as pd

from sklearn.preprocessing import (OneHotEncoder, MinMaxScaler,
                                   FunctionTransformer,
                                   KBinsDiscretizer)
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline

y_train = train_df['sellingprice']
X_train = train_df.drop('sellingprice', axis=1)

def preproc_cols(df, drop_cols):
    return df.drop(drop_cols, axis=1)

drop_cols = FunctionTransformer(preproc_cols, kw_args={"drop_cols":['Unnamed: 0', 'mmr']})
ohe = OneHotEncoder(drop='if_binary', handle_unknown='infrequent_if_exist')
minmax = MinMaxScaler()
bucket_cond = KBinsDiscretizer(n_bins=10, encode='onehot', strategy='uniform')

numeric_columns = ['year', 'odometer']
categorical_columns = ['make', 'model', 'trim', 'body',
                       'transmission', 'state', 'color', 'interior']

col_transformer = ColumnTransformer(
  [('ohe', ohe, categorical_columns),
   ('minmax', minmax, numeric_columns),
   ('bucket_cond', bucket_cond, ['condition'])])

pipeline = Pipeline(steps=[('drop_cols' , drop_cols),
                           ('col_transformer', col_transformer),
                           ('model', model)])

pipeline.fit(X_train, y_train)

print('R2:', pipeline.score(X_valid, y_valid))
print('RMSE:',math.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_valid, pipeline.predict(X_valid))))
print('MAE:', mean_absolute_error(y_valid, pipeline.predict(X_valid)))

import pandas as pd

from sklearn.preprocessing import (OneHotEncoder, MinMaxScaler,
                                   FunctionTransformer,
                                   KBinsDiscretizer)
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline

y_train = train_df['sellingprice']
X_train = train_df.drop('sellingprice', axis=1)

def preproc_cols(df, drop_cols):

    df['model_trim'] = df['model'] + df['trim']
    df['model_trim'] = df['model_trim'].str.lower()

    df['color_interior'] = df['color'] + df['interior']
    df['color_interior'] = df['color_interior'].str.lower()

    return df.drop(drop_cols, axis=1)

drop_cols = FunctionTransformer(preproc_cols, kw_args={"drop_cols":['Unnamed: 0', 'mmr']})
ohe = OneHotEncoder(drop='if_binary', handle_unknown='infrequent_if_exist', min_frequency=1)
minmax = MinMaxScaler()
bucket_cond = KBinsDiscretizer(n_bins=10, encode='onehot',
    strategy='uniform')
bucket_odo = KBinsDiscretizer(n_bins=10, encode='onehot',
    strategy='quantile')
bucket_year = KBinsDiscretizer(n_bins=10, encode='onehot',
    strategy='uniform')

categorical_columns = ['make', 'model', 'trim', 'model_trim', 'body',
                       'transmission', 'state', 'color', 'interior',
                       'color_interior']

col_transformer = ColumnTransformer(
  [('ohe', ohe, categorical_columns),
   ('minmax', minmax, numeric_columns),
   ('bucket_cond', bucket_cond, ['condition']),
   ('bucket_odo', bucket_odo, ['odometer']),
   ('bucket_year', bucket_year, ['year'])]
   )

pipeline = Pipeline(steps=[('drop_cols' , drop_cols),
                           ('col_transformer', col_transformer),
                           ('model', model)])

grid_params = {'col_transformer__bucket_cond__n_bins': range(8,13),
               'col_transformer__bucket_odo__n_bins': range(8,13),
               'col_transformer__bucket_year__n_bins': range(8,13),
               'col_transformer__ohe__min_frequency': range(5)
              }

from sklearn.experimental import enable_halving_search_cv
from sklearn.model_selection import HalvingGridSearchCV

grid_search = HalvingGridSearchCV(pipeline, grid_params,
                                  cv=3, verbose=0,
                                  scoring='neg_mean_absolute_error')

grid_search.fit(X_train, y_train)
print(grid_search.best_params_)

y_valid = valid_df['sellingprice']
X_valid = valid_df.drop('sellingprice', axis=1)

print('MAE:', mean_absolute_error(y_valid, grid_search.predict(X_valid)))

import pandas as pd

!wget -q https://storage.googleapis.com/low-code-ai-book/car_prices_train.csv
!wget -q https://storage.googleapis.com/low-code-ai-book/car_prices_valid.csv
!wget -q https://storage.googleapis.com/low-code-ai-book/car_prices_test.csv

train_df = pd.read_csv('./car_prices_train.csv')
y_train = train_df['sellingprice']
X_train = train_df.drop('sellingprice', axis=1)

valid_df = pd.read_csv('./car_prices_valid.csv')
y_valid = valid_df['sellingprice']
X_valid = valid_df.drop('sellingprice', axis=1)

import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras.layers import StringLookup, HashedCrossing, Discretization, Concatenate

cat_cols = ['make', 'model', 'trim', 'body', 'transmission', 'state',      
            'color', 'interior']
num_cols = ['odometer', 'year', 'condition']

inputs = {}

for col in cat_cols:
  inputs[col] = tf.keras.Input(shape=(1,), name=col, 
                               dtype = tf.string)

for col in num_cols:
  inputs[col] = tf.keras.Input(shape=(1,), name=col, dtype = tf.int64)

preproc_layers = {}
for col in cat_cols:
  layer = StringLookup(output_mode='one_hot')
  layer.adapt(X_train[col])
  preproc_layers[col] = layer(inputs[col])

for col in num_cols:
  layer = Discretization(num_bins=10,  
                         output_mode='one_hot')
  layer.adapt(X_train[col])
  preproc_layers[col] = layer(inputs[col])

model_trim = tf.keras.layers.HashedCrossing(num_bins=1000, output_mode='one_hot')((inputs['model'], inputs['trim']))
color_int = tf.keras.layers.HashedCrossing(num_bins=400, output_mode='one_hot')((inputs['color'], inputs['interior']))

preproc_layers['model_trim'] = model_trim
preproc_layers['color_int'] = color_int

prepared_layer = Concatenate()(preproc_layers.values())
prepared_layer = tf.reshape(prepared_layer, [-1,3903])

hid_1 = tf.keras.layers.Dense(16, activation='relu')(prepared_layer)
hid_2 = tf.keras.layers.Dense(16, activation='relu')(hid_1)
output = tf.keras.layers.Dense(1)(hid_2)

model = tf.keras.Model(inputs=inputs, outputs=output)

model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='mae')

train_ds = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((dict(X_train), y_train)).batch(100)
valid_ds = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((dict(X_valid), y_valid)).batch(1000)

history = model.fit(
    x=train_ds,
    epochs=25,
    verbose=1,
    validation_data=valid_ds
)

!pip install -q keras-tuner

import keras_tuner as kt
from functools import partial

def _build_model_fn(hp, prepared_layer):

  units_1 = hp.Int('units_1', min_value=8, max_value=64, step=4)
  units_2 = hp.Int('units_2', min_value=4, max_value=64, step=4)
  units_3 = hp.Int('units_3', min_value=4, max_value=32, step=2)

  hid_1 = tf.keras.layers.Dense(units_1,     
                                activation='relu')(prepared_layer)
  hid_2 = tf.keras.layers.Dense(units_2, activation='relu')(hid_1)
  hid_3 = tf.keras.layers.Dense(units_3, activation='relu')(hid_2)
  output = tf.keras.layers.Dense(1, activation='linear')(hid_3)

  model = tf.keras.Model(inputs=inputs, outputs=output)

  model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='mae')

  return model

build_model = partial(_build_model_fn, prepared_layer=prepared_layer)

tuner = kt.BayesianOptimization(
    build_model,
    objective=kt.Objective("val_loss", direction="min"),
    max_trials=20)

tuner.search(
    x=train_ds,
    epochs=5,
    verbose=1,
    validation_data=valid_ds)

best_hps=tuner.get_best_hyperparameters(num_trials=1)[0]
print('units_1:', best_hps.get('units_1'))
print('units_2:', best_hps.get('units_2'))
print('units_3:', best_hps.get('units_3'))

best_model = tuner.hypermodel.build(best_hps)

early_stopping = tf.keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(monitor='val_loss', patience=5)

history = best_model.fit(
    x=train_ds,
    epochs=1000,
    verbose=1,
    callbacks = [early_stopping],
    validation_data=valid_ds
)

test_df = pd.read_csv('./car_prices_test.csv')
y_test = test_df['sellingprice']
X_test = test_df.drop('sellingprice', axis=1)
test_ds = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices(
                                            (dict(X_test),  
                                             y_test)).batch(1000)

best_model.evaluate(test_ds)
