## SQL statement to preprocess and explore a few rows of data.

SELECT
  * EXCEPT (int64_field_0, mmr, odometer, year, condition),
  ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(odometer,10) OVER() AS odo_bucket,
  ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(year, 10) OVER() AS year_bucket,
  ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(condition, 10) OVER() AS cond_bucket,
  ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(make,model)) AS make_model,
  ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(color,interior)) AS color_interior
FROM
  `car_sales_prices.car_prices_train`
LIMIT 10;

## CREATE MODEL statement for a linear model using the TRANSFORM statement.

CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL
  `car_sales_prices.linear_car_model` 
  TRANSFORM (
    * EXCEPT (int64_field_0, mmr, odometer, year, condition),
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(odometer,10) OVER() AS odo_bucket,
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(year, 10) OVER() AS year_bucket,
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(condition, 10) OVER() AS cond_bucket,
    ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(make,model)) AS make_model,
    ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(color,interior)) AS color_interior)
  OPTIONS (
    model_type='linear_reg',
    input_label_cols=['sellingprice'],
    data_split_method='NO_SPLIT') AS
SELECT
  *
FROM
  `car_sales_prices.car_prices_train`;

## ML.EVALUATE statement for linear_car_model.

SELECT mean_absolute_error
FROM ML.EVALUATE(MODEL `ddml.linear_car_model`,
    (SELECT * FROM `car_sales_prices.car_prices_valid`))

## ML.PREDICT statement for linear_car_model.

SELECT *
FROM ML.PREDICT(MODEL `ddml.linear_car_model`,
    (SELECT * FROM `car_sales_prices.car_prices_valid`));
    
## CREATE MODEL statement for DNN model.

CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL
  `car_sales_prices.dnn_car_model` 
  TRANSFORM (
    * EXCEPT (int64_field_0, mmr, odometer, year, condition),
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(odometer,10) OVER() AS odo_bucket,
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(year, 10) OVER() AS year_bucket,
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(condition, 10) OVER() AS cond_bucket,
    ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(make,model)) AS make_model,
    ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(color,interior)) AS color_interior)
  OPTIONS (
    model_type='dnn_regressor',
    hidden_units=[64, 32, 16],
    input_label_cols=['sellingprice'],
    data_split_method='NO_SPLIT') AS
SELECT
  *
FROM
  `car_sales_prices.car_prices_train`;

## Hyperparameter tuning job for DNN in BigQuery ML.

CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL
  `car_sales_prices.dnn_hp_car_model` 
  TRANSFORM (
    * EXCEPT (int64_field_0, mmr, odometer, year, condition),
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(odometer,10) OVER() AS odo_bucket,
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(year, 10) OVER() AS year_bucket,
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(condition, 10) OVER() AS cond_bucket,
    ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(make,model)) AS make_model,
    ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(color,interior)) AS color_interior)
  OPTIONS (
    model_type='dnn_regressor',
    hidden_units=hparam_candidates([STRUCT([64,32,16]), 
                                    STRUCT([32,16]),
                                    STRUCT([32])]),
    dropout=hparam_range(0,0.8),
    input_label_cols=['sellingprice'],
    num_trials = 10,

AS SELECT
  *
FROM
  `car_sales_prices.car_prices_train`;

08.1Chapter 8 · Improving Custom Model Performance

Scikit-Learn me Improvement — Feature Engineering

Aksar carefully banaye hue features, simple model ke saath bhi, bahut strong results dete hain. Model ko complicated banana hamesha sahi approach nahi hai — complex models ko zyada data aur zyada compute chahiye hota hai. Yahan tum scikit-learn pipeline me feature engineering se RMSE neeche laate ho.

Easy improvement — condition column me -1

  • Describe se pakad: train_df.describe() me condition column ka minimum -1.0 dikhta hai, jabki rating 0 se 5 ke beech honi chahiye. Ye ek magic number hai jo colleague se miss ho gaya — isliye extra pair of eyes hamesha valuable hoti hai.
  • Option 1: -1.0 ko 0.0 se replace karke ek naya binary feature condition_recorded banao — lekin ratings ka effect linear nahi hota.
  • Option 2 (chuna gaya): values ko bucketize karke one-hot encode karo — to "no rating" wala case baaki ratings se poori tarah alag treat hoga, aur buckets ki count tune ki ja sakti hai.
  • KBinsDiscretizer: scikit-learn ka transformer jo data ko buckets me baant ta hai. n_bins=10, encode='onehot', strategy='uniform' se 10 evenly-spaced buckets bante hain, aur -1.0 apne alag bucket me aata hai.
  • Result: RMSE $3,384.60 se gir kar $3,313.63 ho gaya — chhota improvement, lekin aisi chhoti pakad aksar bada farak laati hai.
from sklearn.preprocessing import KBinsDiscretizer
bucket_cond = KBinsDiscretizer(n_bins=10, encode='onehot',
                               strategy='uniform')

Unknown categories aur infrequent values

  • Warning: evaluation par warning aati hai — "Found unknown categories in columns [2, 3] during transform" — columns 2 aur 3 trim aur body hain. Matlab validation dataset me aisi values hain jo training me nahi thi.
  • Kitni rare: trim column me 124 values training me sirf ek baar aati hain, validation me 273 values sirf ek baar. Datasets ke beech aisi skew check karna data understanding ka important hissa hai.
  • min_frequency: OneHotEncoder ka parameter hai — jo categories isse kam baar aayein, unhe ek hi "infrequent" category me daal deta hai. Bahut zyada set karoge to bahut si categories ka contribution same ho jayega aur feature bekaar ho jayega; bahut kam set karoge to features ki count bahut badh jayegi aur har value ek-ek baar aayegi.
  • Experiment: min_frequency ko 1 set karke dobara train karne par performance bahut halki si hi badli — iska matlab hai ki 0 baar aane wali categories ko same mana gaya. Is parameter ko tuning me explore karenge.

Feature crosses — model + trim, color + interior

  • Problem: model aur trim ko alag-alag treat karna galat hai. Ek gaadi ka model kehna kaafi nahi — uske trims LX, EX, EX-L ho sakte hain. Aur "LX" trim alag models me bhi hota hai. Sirf trim dekh kar pata nahi chalta kaunsi gaadi hai.
  • One-hot encoding me problem: "LX" ka weight model se independent hota hai — alag models ke LX trims ko same treat kiya jata hai, jo galat hai.
  • Feature cross: do ya zyada features ko concatenate karke banaya gaya synthetic feature. Crossed feature ki value 1 hoti hai sirf jab dono features ke corresponding values hon — jaise ek specific model-trim pair ke liye 1, baaki pairs ke liye 0.
  • Implementation: Pandas me df['model_trim'] = df['model'] + df['trim'] aur lowercase kar dete ho taaki capitalization ke random differences se alag feature values na ban jayein. Aise hi color + interior ka cross banate ho.
  • Result: feature crosses se RMSE lagbhag $3,122.14 ho gaya — lagbhag 2% ki kami, aur goal ke aur paas. AutoML pehle wale chapters me aise features apne aap banata tha.
def preproc_cols(df, drop_cols):
    df['model_trim'] = df['model'] + df['trim']
    df['model_trim'] = df['model_trim'].str.lower()
    df['color_interior'] = df['color'] + df['interior']
    df['color_interior'] = df['color_interior'].str.lower()
    return df.drop(drop_cols, axis=1)
Yaad rakho: Feature crosses powerful hote hain, lekin soch-samajh kar banao — har cross se features ki count badhti hai, aur bahut zyada features overfitting la sakte hain. Exercise: RMSE ko 3,000 se neeche lane ke liye aur features bucketize aur cross karke dekho.

import pandas as pd

from sklearn.preprocessing import (OneHotEncoder, MinMaxScaler,
                                   FunctionTransformer,
                                   KBinsDiscretizer)
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline

y_train = train_df['sellingprice']
X_train = train_df.drop('sellingprice', axis=1)

def preproc_cols(df, drop_cols):
    return df.drop(drop_cols, axis=1)

drop_cols = FunctionTransformer(preproc_cols, kw_args={"drop_cols":['Unnamed: 0', 'mmr']})
ohe = OneHotEncoder(drop='if_binary', handle_unknown='infrequent_if_exist', min_frequency=1)
minmax = MinMaxScaler()
bucket_cond = KBinsDiscretizer(n_bins=10, encode='onehot', strategy='uniform')

numeric_columns = ['year', 'odometer']
categorical_columns = ['make', 'model', 'trim', 'body',
                       'transmission', 'state', 'color', 'interior']

col_transformer = ColumnTransformer(
  [('ohe', ohe, categorical_columns),
   ('minmax', minmax, numeric_columns),
   ('bucket_cond', bucket_cond, ['condition'])])

pipeline = Pipeline(steps=[('drop_cols' , drop_cols),
                           ('col_transformer', col_transformer),
                           ('model', model)])

pipeline.fit(X_train, y_train)

print('R2:', pipeline.score(X_valid, y_valid))
print('RMSE:',math.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_valid, pipeline.predict(X_valid))))
print('MAE:', mean_absolute_error(y_valid, pipeline.predict(X_valid)))

import pandas as pd

from sklearn.preprocessing import (OneHotEncoder, MinMaxScaler,
                                   FunctionTransformer,
                                   KBinsDiscretizer)
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline

y_train = train_df['sellingprice']
X_train = train_df.drop('sellingprice', axis=1)

def preproc_cols(df, drop_cols):

    df['model_trim'] = df['model'] + df['trim']
    df['model_trim'] = df['model_trim'].str.lower()

    df['color_interior'] = df['color'] + df['interior']
    df['color_interior'] = df['color_interior'].str.lower()

    return df.drop(drop_cols, axis=1)

drop_cols = FunctionTransformer(preproc_cols, kw_args={"drop_cols":['Unnamed: 0', 'mmr']})
ohe = OneHotEncoder(drop='if_binary', handle_unknown='infrequent_if_exist', min_frequency=1)
minmax = MinMaxScaler()
bucket_cond = KBinsDiscretizer(n_bins=10, encode='onehot',
    strategy='uniform')
bucket_odo = KBinsDiscretizer(n_bins=10, encode='onehot',
    strategy='quantile')
bucket_year = KBinsDiscretizer(n_bins=10, encode='onehot',
    strategy='uniform')

categorical_columns = ['make', 'model', 'trim', 'model_trim', 'body',
                       'transmission', 'state', 'color', 'interior',
                       'color_interior']

col_transformer = ColumnTransformer(
  [('ohe', ohe, categorical_columns),
   ('minmax', minmax, numeric_columns),
   ('bucket_cond', bucket_cond, ['condition']),
   ('bucket_odo', bucket_odo, ['odometer']),
   ('bucket_year', bucket_year, ['year'])]
   )

pipeline = Pipeline(steps=[('drop_cols' , drop_cols),
                           ('col_transformer', col_transformer),
                           ('model', model)])

grid_params = {'col_transformer__bucket_cond__n_bins': range(8,13),
               'col_transformer__bucket_odo__n_bins': range(8,13),
               'col_transformer__bucket_year__n_bins': range(8,13),
               'col_transformer__ohe__min_frequency': range(5)
              }

from sklearn.experimental import enable_halving_search_cv
from sklearn.model_selection import HalvingGridSearchCV

grid_search = HalvingGridSearchCV(pipeline, grid_params,
                                  cv=3, verbose=0,
                                  scoring='neg_mean_absolute_error')

grid_search.fit(X_train, y_train)
print(grid_search.best_params_)

y_valid = valid_df['sellingprice']
X_valid = valid_df.drop('sellingprice', axis=1)

print('MAE:', mean_absolute_error(y_valid, grid_search.predict(X_valid)))

08.2Chapter 8 · Improving Custom Model Performance

Hyperparameter Tuning — Scikit-Learn aur Keras

Feature engineering se RMSE $3,384 se $3,122 tak aa gaya, lekin $2,000 ka goal abhi door hai. Ab tum hyperparameters tune karte ho — pehle scikit-learn me halving grid search se, phir Keras me Keras Tuner aur Bayesian optimization se.

Hyperparameter kya hota hai

  • Definition: hyperparameter woh variable hai jo training ke dauran update nahi hota, lekin model architecture, feature engineering ya training process ko define karta hai — jaise hidden layers ki count, buckets ki count, learning rate ya batch size.
  • Example: condition feature ko bucketize karte hue tumne 10 buckets choose kiye the — ye ek arbitrary choice thi. 5 se 15 ke beech koi aur number behtar ho sakta hai. Bahut kam buckets se bade ranges ek jaise treat honge; bahut zyada buckets se har bucket me kam examples honge aur model overfit kar sakta hai.

Teen tuning strategies

  • Grid search: "sab kuch try karo aur dekho kya best hai". Do hyperparameters — ek ke 4 values, dusre ke 3 — to 12 combinations hain. Candidate ranges ke andar best hyperparameters pakke milte hain, lekin 4 hyperparameters × 10 values each = 10,000 models train karne padenge — jaldi infeasible ho jata hai.
  • Random search: candidates me se randomly kuch models choose karke train karta hai. Time control kar sakte ho, lekin bad luck se best model miss ho sakta hai.
  • Bayesian search (optimization): pehle randomly kuch models train karta hai, phir unke metrics dekh kar agle candidates choose karta hai — woh candidates jinse best metrics ki ummeed ho. Ye process repeat hota hai. Random search se zyada "intelligent" search hai, lekin ye bhi poora search space exhaust nahi karta.

Halving grid search scikit-learn me

  • Tune kiye gaye hyperparameters: odometer, condition aur year ke liye buckets ki count (range 8–12), aur OneHotEncoder ka min_frequency (range 1–5). Kul 625 candidate models.
  • Halving ka idea: pehle saare candidates ko training data ke chhote hisse par train karo, phir best-performing fraction ko rakh kar zyada data par train karo. Ye repeat karo jab tak best candidate na mil jaye.
  • Risk: jo model chhote data par accha ho woh poore data par accha na ho, aur jo chhote data par bura laga woh poore data par accha hota — phir bhi halving grid search random search se zyada effective hoti hai.
  • cv=3: cross-validation — har candidate ko training data ke alag splits par 3 baar evaluate karta hai. Zyada cv se zyada precise metrics milte hain lekin time bhi zyada lagta hai.
  • scoring: neg_root_mean_squared_error use hota hai — kyunki tuning methods score functions use karte hain (jo model behtar hone par badhni chahiye), aur RMSE loss hai (jo ghatna chahiye), isliye negative RMSE use karte hain.
  • Time: poora tuning Colab par 35–40 minutes leta hai.
  • Best hyperparameters: condition buckets 11, odometer buckets 12, year buckets 11, min_frequency 1.
  • Result: best model ka validation RMSE $2,915.02 — $3,300 se upar se shuru karke significant improvement hai.
grid_params = {'col_transformer__bucket_cond__n_bins': range(8, 13),
    'col_transformer__bucket_odo__n_bins': range(8, 13),
    'col_transformer__bucket_year__n_bins': range(8, 13),
    'col_transformer__ohe__min_frequency': range(1, 6)}
grid_search = HalvingGridSearchCV(pipeline, grid_params,
    cv=3, verbose=1, scoring='neg_root_mean_squared_error')
grid_search.fit(X_train, y_train)
print(grid_search.best_params_)

Keras preprocessing layers — pipeline ka Keras version

  • Discretization layer: numeric features ko bucketize karta hai, jaise scikit-learn ka KBinsDiscretizer. adapt() se training data dekh kar bucket boundaries choose karta hai. Example: 4 bins aur boundaries [0.0, 1.0, 2.0] hon to actual bins (-inf, 0.0), [0.0, 1.0), [1.0, 2.0) aur [2.0, +inf) hote hain.
  • StringLookup layer: string categorical columns ko encode karta hai — yahan output_mode='one_hot' se one-hot encoding. Unknown value aane par use '[UNK]' assign hota hai.
  • HashedCrossing layer: do categorical features ka feature cross banata hai. Hashing function string ko deterministic integer me badalti hai, aur usse bin choose hota hai. model_trim ke liye 1,000 bins aur color_interior ke liye 400 bins — kyunki model-trim ke 10 lakh se zyada combinations possible hain, aur color-interior ke lagbhag 300. Bins zyada rakhne se collision (do values ek hi bin me) ki chance kam hoti hai, lekin har bin ek feature hai, to trade-off hai.
  • Functional API: jab alag features par alag preprocessing ho to Sequential API kaam nahi karti — Functional API use hoti hai. Har feature ke liye tf.keras.Input banate ho (categorical ke liye dtype tf.string, numeric ke liye tf.int64), phir saare preprocessed outputs ko Concatenate() se jodte ho — kul 3,903 features ki tensor banti hai.

Keras neural network aur Keras Tuner

  • Architecture: do hidden layers, har ek me 16 neurons aur ReLU activation; output layer me 1 neuron, bina activation — regression me output ek single number hota hai. Loss MSE, optimizer Adam, training batch size 100, validation batch size 1000, 25 epochs.
  • Baseline Keras result: MSE lagbhag $10,719,103, matlab RMSE lagbhag $3,274 — tuning se pehle wale scikit-learn model jaisa hi. Architecture arbitrary thi, isliye improvement ki jagah hai.
  • Keras Tuner install: !pip install -q keras-tuner se install karte ho — Colab me default nahi hota.
  • build_model function: hyperparameters input le kar compiled model return karti hai. hp.Int('units_1', min_value=8, max_value=64, step=4) se integer hyperparameter define hota hai — possible values 8, 12, 16, ..., 64. Aise hi units_2 (4–64, step 4) aur units_3 (4–32, step 2). hp.Float, hp.Boolean aur hp.Choice bhi hote hain.
  • BayesianOptimization tuner: objective val_loss ko minimize karna, max_trials=20. Har candidate ko sirf 5 epochs train karte ho — aksar kuch epochs me hi pata chal jata hai kaunsa model behtar hoga.
  • Best trial: val_loss lagbhag $6,000,000, matlab RMSE lagbhag $2,470. Best hyperparameters: units_1=52, units_2=64, units_3=32.
  • Final training: best model ko early stopping (patience=5, monitor val_loss) ke saath 1000 epochs tak train karte ho — validation RMSE 2,000 se neeche aa jata hai. Goal meet ho gaya!
  • Test set verification: test dataset ab tak kabhi use nahi hua — best_model.evaluate(test_ds) se final check karte ho. Agar performance similar aaye to model deploy ke liye ready hai; agar bahut bura aaye to datasets ko recombine karke naya split bana kar process dobara shuru karo. Ek baar test data se decision le li to uski independence khatam — phir wahi test data dobara verification ke liye use nahi kar sakte.
tuner = kt.BayesianOptimization(
    build_model,
    objective=kt.Objective("val_loss", direction="min"),
    max_trials=20)
tuner.search(x=train_ds, epochs=5, verbose=1,
             validation_data=valid_ds)
best_hps = tuner.get_best_hyperparameters(num_trials=1)[0]
Yaad rakho: Tuning me har candidate ko poora train karna zaroori nahi hai — halving grid search aur kam epochs wali Keras Tuner search dono isi idea par kaam karte hain: pehle saste me chhanto, phir best candidates par zyada compute lagao.

## SQL statement in BigQuery to create dataset and load data into tables. Directions for using Console are in Chapter 8

CREATE SCHEMA car_sales_prices OPTIONS(location='US');

LOAD DATA OVERWRITE cars_sales_prices.car_prices_train
  FROM FILES(
    format='CSV',
    uris = ['gs://low-code-ai/chapter_8/car_prices_train.csv']
  );
 
 LOAD DATA OVERWRITE cars_sales_prices.car_prices_valid
  FROM FILES(
    format='CSV',
    uris = ['gs://low-code-ai/chapter_8/car_prices_valid.csv']
  );

LOAD DATA OVERWRITE cars_sales_prices.car_prices_test
  FROM FILES(
    format='CSV',
    uris = ['gs://low-code-ai/chapter_8/car_prices_test.csv']
  );
  
## SQL statement to preprocess and explore a few rows of data.

SELECT
  * EXCEPT (int64_field_0, mmr, odometer, year, condition),
  ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(odometer,10) OVER() AS odo_bucket,
  ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(year, 10) OVER() AS year_bucket,
  ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(condition, 10) OVER() AS cond_bucket,
  ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(make,model)) AS make_model,
  ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(color,interior)) AS color_interior
FROM
  `car_sales_prices.car_prices_train`
LIMIT 10;

## CREATE MODEL statement for a linear model using the TRANSFORM statement.

CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL
  `car_sales_prices.linear_car_model` 
  TRANSFORM (
    * EXCEPT (int64_field_0, mmr, odometer, year, condition),
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(odometer,10) OVER() AS odo_bucket,
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(year, 10) OVER() AS year_bucket,
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(condition, 10) OVER() AS cond_bucket,
    ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(make,model)) AS make_model,
    ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(color,interior)) AS color_interior)
  OPTIONS (
    model_type='linear_reg',
    input_label_cols=['sellingprice'],
    data_split_method='NO_SPLIT') AS
SELECT
  *
FROM
  `car_sales_prices.car_prices_train`;

## ML.EVALUATE statement for linear_car_model.

SELECT mean_absolute_error
FROM ML.EVALUATE(MODEL `ddml.linear_car_model`,
    (SELECT * FROM `car_sales_prices.car_prices_valid`))

## ML.PREDICT statement for linear_car_model.

SELECT *
FROM ML.PREDICT(MODEL `ddml.linear_car_model`,
    (SELECT * FROM `car_sales_prices.car_prices_valid`));
    
## CREATE MODEL statement for DNN model.

CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL
  `car_sales_prices.dnn_car_model` 
  TRANSFORM (
    * EXCEPT (int64_field_0, mmr, odometer, year, condition),
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(odometer,10) OVER() AS odo_bucket,
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(year, 10) OVER() AS year_bucket,
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(condition, 10) OVER() AS cond_bucket,
    ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(make,model)) AS make_model,
    ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(color,interior)) AS color_interior)
  OPTIONS (
    model_type='dnn_regressor',
    hidden_units=[64, 32, 16],
    input_label_cols=['sellingprice'],
    data_split_method='NO_SPLIT') AS
SELECT
  *
FROM
  `car_sales_prices.car_prices_train`;

## Hyperparameter tuning job for DNN in BigQuery ML.

CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL
  `car_sales_prices.dnn_hp_car_model` 
  TRANSFORM (
    * EXCEPT (int64_field_0, mmr, odometer, year, condition),
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(odometer,10) OVER() AS odo_bucket,
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(year, 10) OVER() AS year_bucket,
    ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(condition, 10) OVER() AS cond_bucket,
    ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(make,model)) AS make_model,
    ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(color,interior)) AS color_interior)
  OPTIONS (
    model_type='dnn_regressor',
    hidden_units=hparam_candidates([STRUCT([64,32,16]), 
                                    STRUCT([32,16]),
                                    STRUCT([32])]),
    dropout=hparam_range(0,0.8),
    input_label_cols=['sellingprice'],
    num_trials = 10,
    hparam_tuning_objectives=['mean_absolute_error']) 
AS SELECT
  *
FROM
  `car_sales_prices.car_prices_train`;


## Query using ML.TRIAL_INFO to see evaluation metrics for candidate models

SELECT
  *
FROM
  ML.TRIAL_INFO(MODEL `car_sales_prices.dnn_hp_car_model`)

08.3Chapter 8 · Improving Custom Model Performance

Hyperparameter Tuning BigQuery ML me

Wahi car price problem ab BigQuery ML me solve karte ho — SQL se. Feature engineering ke liye BigQuery ML ke apne functions hain, transformations ko TRANSFORM clause se model ke andar build karte ho, aur hyperparameter tuning CREATE MODEL statement me hi hoti hai.

Data load karna aur transformations

  • Tables: BigQuery me car_sales_prices dataset banao (US region), phir teen tables banao — car_prices_train, car_prices_valid, car_prices_test — Google Cloud Storage ki CSV files se, schema auto detect ke saath.
  • One-hot encoding: BigQuery ML me string columns automatically one-hot encode ho jate hain — iske liye kuch karna nahi padta.
  • ML.BUCKETIZE: column aur bucket endpoints ki list leta hai — endpoints tumhe pehle se pata hone chahiye.
  • ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE: column aur buckets ki count leta hai, aur data ko quantile-based buckets me baant ta hai. 4 buckets hon to pehla quartile pehle bucket me, dusra dusre me, aur aise hi. Output bin_n form me hota hai, jaise bin_10, aur phir BigQuery ML use bhi one-hot encode kar deta hai.
  • ML.FEATURE_CROSS: STRUCT me diye gaye columns ka feature cross banata hai. Do columns doge to ek cross milega, teen doge to har possible pair ka cross — kul teen. Syntax: ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(make, model)) — STRUCT keyword zaroori hai, bina iske error aayega. Output value1_value2 form me hota hai, jaise ek make-model pair ya red_red.
SELECT
  * EXCEPT (int64_field_0, mmr, odometer, year, condition),
  ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(odometer, 10) OVER() AS odo_bucket,
  ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(year, 10) OVER() AS year_bucket,
  ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(condition, 10) OVER() AS cond_bucket,
  ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(make, model)) AS make_model,
  ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(color, interior)) AS color_interior
FROM `car_sales_prices.car_prices_train`
LIMIT 10

TRANSFORM clause — transformations ko model me band karna

  • Problem: agar transformations karke naya table save karo aur us par model train karo, to prediction time par wahi transformations dobara karni padengi — lekin tumhe one-hot encoding kaise hui aur bucket endpoints kya the, ye pata nahi hoga.
  • Solution: CREATE MODEL me TRANSFORM clause likhte ho — transformation SQL model ke andar store ho jata hai. ML.PREDICT chalane par TRANSFORM clause input table par pehle execute hota hai, phir model ko predictions ke liye milta hai. Ye scikit-learn pipelines aur Keras preprocessing layers ka BigQuery ML version hai.
  • data_split_method='NO_SPLIT': kyunki tumhare paas alag validation dataset hai, poora training dataset training ke liye use hota hai — BigQuery ML apna split nahi karta.
  • Linear regression result: training RMSE lagbhag $3,000 (expected jaisa), lekin validation RMSE $8,000 se zyada! Ye overfitting ka classic example hai.
  • Wajah: feature crosses se 770,000 alag feature values ban gayi hain — examples ke comparison me bahut zyada features. Itne zyada features par model training data ko "memorize" kar leta hai aur naye data par fail hota hai.
  • DNN model: wahi TRANSFORM clause, sirf options badal kar — model_type='dnn_regressor', hidden_units=[64, 32, 16] — deep neural network regression model train ho jata hai.

Regularization — overfitting se ladna

  • Overfitting: model training dataset par evaluation datasets se bahut behtar perform kare — aksar isliye kyunki model data ko memorize kar leta hai aur general patterns miss kar deta hai. Iska main ilaaj hai model ki complexity kam karna.
  • L1/L2 regularization: loss function me ek penalty term jod dete hain. L2 me weights ke squares ka sum joda jata hai, L1 me weights ke absolute values ka sum. Lambda (regularization rate) control karta hai ki original loss ko complexity ke mukable kitna weight mile — lambda zyada ho to complexity par zyada penalty. L2 weights ko chhota karne ki koshish karta hai; L1 un weights ko zero ki taraf dhakel deta hai jo model ke liye influential nahi hain — sparse features (jaise feature crosses) ke liye bahut valuable hai. Dono ek saath use karna elastic net regularization kehlata hai.
  • Dropout: loss function par nahi, model par lagta hai training ke dauran. Har batch me hidden layers ke kuch percent neurons "band" kar diye jate hain — unke weighted sums zero set kar diye jate hain. Isse model training me bahut complex nahi banta. Prediction time par dropout nahi use hota, taaki model ki poori power mile.

Hyperparameter tuning BigQuery ML me

  • num_trials: tuning me kitne alag models train honge — yahan 10. num_parallel_trials se multiple trials parallel chala sakte ho — total resources same, lekin time kam lagta hai. Trade-off: Bayesian optimization har iteration se seekhta hai, to zyada parallel trials se iterations kam ho jati hain.
  • hparam_candidates: discrete choices ke liye — hidden_units ke liye teen options: [64, 32, 16], [32, 16], aur [32].
  • hparam_range: floating-point range ke liye — l1_reg 0 se 1, aur dropout 0 se 0.8 (hidden layers me kitne percent neurons dropout se affected hon).
  • hparam_tuning_objectives: ['mean_squared_error'] — RMSE optimize karna hai, isliye MSE objective hai.
  • Optimizer note: is query me optimizer='adagrad' specify karna zaroori hai — default optimizer Adam L1 regularization support nahi karta.
  • Time: tuning process lagbhag 1 hour leta hai.
  • Results dekhna: ML.TRIAL_INFO se saare trials aur unke hyperparameters dekh sakte ho, mean_squared_error ke hisaab se sort karke. ML.PREDICT use karoge to BigQuery by default best trial wala model use karta hai.
CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL
  `car_sales_prices.dnn_hp_car_model`
TRANSFORM (
  * EXCEPT (int64_field_0, mmr, odometer, year, condition),
  ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(odometer, 10) OVER() AS odo_bucket,
  ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(year, 10) OVER() AS year_bucket,
  ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(condition, 10) OVER() AS cond_bucket,
  ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(make, model)) AS make_model,
  ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(color, interior)) AS color_interior)
OPTIONS (
  model_type='dnn_regressor',
  optimizer='adagrad',
  hidden_units=hparam_candidates([STRUCT([64, 32, 16]),
      STRUCT([32, 16]), STRUCT([32])]),
  l1_reg=hparam_range(0, 1),
  dropout=hparam_range(0, 0.8),
  input_label_cols=['sellingprice'],
  num_trials=10,
  hparam_tuning_objectives=['mean_squared_error'])
AS SELECT * FROM `car_sales_prices.car_prices_train`;
Yaad rakho: Feature crosses se features ki count explode ho sakti hai — yahan 770,000 values bani aur validation RMSE $8,000 se upar chala gaya. Feature crosses ke saath L1 regularization lagana almost hamesha accha idea hai.

08.4Chapter 8 · Improving Custom Model Performance

Cloud Tuning — Vertex AI, SageMaker, Azure ML

Scikit-learn aur Keras local machine ya Colab par chhote datasets aur models ke liye wonderful hain. Lekin bahut bade datasets aur models par ye slow ho sakte hain, ya memory aur processing ki limits ki wajah se impossible bhi. Bade models ko train aur tune karna apne aap me ek art hai — public cloud providers ke tools ye kaam bahut aasan kar dete hain.

Kab cloud ki zaroorat padti hai

  • Scale ki problem: local machine ya Colab par bahut bada dataset train karna bahut time le sakta hai, ya memory khatam ho sakti hai. Cloud par tum apni pasand ke machines ke cluster par train kar sakte ho.
  • Tuning ka cost: hyperparameter tuning me tens ya hundreds of models train karne padte hain — cloud par parallel trials se ye time bahut kam ho jata hai.
  • Book ka scope: ye products custom code development ke nazariye se zyada involved hote hain, isliye book inme deep dive nahi karti — sirf options aur references deti hai.

Vertex AI Training aur Tuning

  • Training: Chapter 7 me tumne scikit-learn model ke liye Python module package karke Vertex AI Training par submit kiya tha. Wahi process is chapter ke scikit-learn ya Keras code ke liye bhi kaam karta hai.
  • Hyperparameter tuning service: Vertex AI Training ka hissa hai. cloudml-hypertune Python package se alag-alag trials apne metrics Vertex AI ko report karte hain, aur trials alag clusters par chal sakte hain.
  • Method: Keras Tuner ki tarah, Vertex AI bhi best hyperparameters dhoondhne ke liye Bayesian optimization use karta hai.
  • Details: official Vertex AI documentation me milengi.

Amazon SageMaker — Automatic Model Tuning (AMT)

  • Kya hai: SageMaker AMT hyperparameter tuning ke liye automatic service hai.
  • Flexibility: built-in algorithms, custom algorithms, ya SageMaker prebuilt containers — scikit-learn, TensorFlow aur PyTorch jaise ML frameworks ke liye — kisi ke saath bhi use kar sakte ho.
  • Details: SageMaker AMT documentation me milengi.

Azure Machine Learning

  • Kya hai: Azure ML me hyperparameter tuning Python client library aur command-line interface dono ka hissa hai.
  • Workflow: apna custom model apni pasand ke framework me likho, hyperparameters ko model banane wale function ke arguments banao, hyperparameter search space specify karo, aur job configuration specify karke Azure ML par hyperparameter sweep job submit karo.
  • Details: Azure Machine Learning documentation me milengi.

Chapter 8 ka summary — kya seekha

  • Scikit-learn: feature engineering (bucketization, feature crosses) aur halving grid search se RMSE $3,384.60 se $2,915.02 tak laaye.
  • Keras: preprocessing layers (Discretization, StringLookup, HashedCrossing) se wahi feature engineering dobara ki, aur Keras Tuner (Bayesian optimization) se best model ka validation RMSE 2,000 se neeche laaye — business goal meet hua.
  • BigQuery ML: ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE aur ML.FEATURE_CROSS se transformations, TRANSFORM clause se unhe model me band karna, aur CREATE MODEL me hparam_candidates aur hparam_range se tuning.
  • Lesson: no-code aur low-code solutions kam se kam ek great starting point hain, aur aksar bina custom code ke hi goal tak pahuncha dete hain. Lekin custom code explore karne ke liye data scientist hona zaroori nahi hai — aur isme hundreds of lines of code likhne ki bhi zaroorat nahi padti.
Yaad rakho: Bade models ke liye tuning strategy wahi rehti hai — grid, random ya Bayesian search — bas execution cloud par hota hai. Pehle chhote scale par approach validate karo, phir cloud par scale karo.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — Improving Custom Model Performance

09Chapter 9 · Next Steps in Your AI Journey

Next Steps in Your AI Journey

Is book me tumne seekha ki data se business decisions kaise drive karte hain, data ko ML ke nazariye se kaise samajhte hain, aur AutoML, BigQuery ML, scikit-learn aur TensorFlow se models kaise banate aur improve karte hain. Bahut logon ke liye ye kaafi hai — lekin kuch ke liye ye sirf ek lambi journey ki shuruaat hai.

Ab tak ki journey — recap

  • Enterprise ML workflow: business question se shuru karke data collection, preprocessing, EDA, feature selection, model training, evaluation, tuning aur deployment tak ka poora workflow.
  • Tools: AutoML se regression aur classification models, BigQuery ML se SQL me low-code models, scikit-learn aur TensorFlow/Keras se custom code models, aur phir feature engineering aur hyperparameter tuning se unhe improve karna.
  • Toolkit: tumhare paas ab ek powerful toolkit hai — lekin field tezi se badh rahi hai, aur naye tools aur developments sirf researchers ke liye nahi hain.

Data science me gehrai — definition

  • Data science kya hai: iski koi universally agreed definition nahi hai. Ek decent approximation ye hai ki data science woh discipline hai jo mathematics, statistics, computer science aur problem ke hisaab se dusre areas ke tools use karke datasets se insights nikaalti hai.
  • Structured data: is book ke saare datasets structured the — well-defined schema wale. Zyada business problems structured data se hi jude hote hain, aur tumne is par kaam karne ki wonderful skill set seekh li hai.
  • Unstructured data: images, videos, sound files aur text — schema ke bina data. ML mature hote hue unstructured data par kaam tezi se important ho raha hai, aur pichhle decade me is par bahut research hui hai.
  • Generative AI: aise models jo images, videos aur text generate karte hain — recent saalon me bahut popular aur fast-growing field ban gayi hai.
  • Explainability problem: models jitne complex hote hain, unhe samajhna utna mushkil hota hai. Linear regression me weights se feature importance clear thi; ek hidden layer wale neural network me bhi weights aur feature importance ka easy connection nahi rehta — aur bahut bade models me to aur bhi mushkil hai.

Aage ke resources — kahan se seekho

  • Unstructured data: Kaggle MNIST competition aur tutorials, Google ML Crash Course on Image Classification, Keras/TensorFlow me word embeddings, BERT preprocessing, scikit-learn me text data, aur Yelp review dataset (review scores predict karne ke liye).
  • Generative AI: craiyon.com jaise free tools se khel kar dekho, aur ChatGPT 101 jaisa course generative AI ke use aur implications samajhne ke liye.
  • Explainable AI: XAI par ek mashhoor guidebook hai jo black-box models ko explainable banane ke tareeke deti hai.
  • MLOps: MLOps par introductory resources aur continuous delivery/automation pipelines wale guides, aur ML systems design par ek mashhoor O'Reilly book.
Yaad rakho: Ye book sirf shuruaat thi. ML aur AI ki demand pichhle decade me exponentially badhi hai aur aage bhi badhti rahegi — tum apni interest ke hisaab se kisi bhi direction me ja sakte ho.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — Next Steps in Your AI Journey

09.1Chapter 9 · Next Steps in Your AI Journey

Data Science me Gehrai — Unstructured Data

Unstructured data ka matlab hai data bina schema ke — images aur text iske classic examples hain. ML models ultimately mathematical functions hain jo numeric inputs lete hain aur numeric outputs dete hain — to image ya sentence ko numeric input kaise banayein?

Image data — pixels hi numbers hain

  • Grayscale image: pixels ka grid hoti hai. Ek low-resolution handwritten digit "2" ki image 12 × 12 pixels ki hai. Pixel values 0 se 255 ke beech hoti hain — 0 black, 255 white, aur beech ki values gray ke alag shades.
  • Color image: teen channels hote hain — red, green aur blue (RGB). Har pixel ke liye har channel ki value 0 se 255 hoti hai. White [255, 255, 255] hai aur yellow [255, 255, 0] hai.
  • ML ke liye: black-and-white image 2D array hai aur color image 3D array — yehi tumhare image models ke numeric inputs hain.
  • MNIST dataset: handwritten digit recognition ka "hello world" example. 60,000 training images aur 10,000 test images, 10 digits (0–9) ke beech well balanced, har image 28 × 28 grayscale.
  • Multiclass classification: model har digit ki probability predict karta hai, aur sabse likely digit ko predicted label mana jata hai. Linear classification aur neural network classifiers yahan bhi waise hi kaam karte hain jaise Chapter 7 me, lekin image data ke liye convolutional layers jaise extra tools bhi bahut useful hote hain.

Text data — words ko numbers banana

  • Use case: customer reviews ke comments se samajhna ki unhone positive ya negative rating kyun di — iske liye text ko numeric data me badalna padta hai.
  • One-hot encoding: sabse simple tareeka — categorical data jaisa hi. Vocabulary ['red', 'blue', 'green'] ho to 'blue' ki encoding [0, 1, 0] hogi. Lekin har alag word ki alag value se feature bahut high-dimensional ho jata hai, aur rare words ko model seekh hi nahi pata.
  • N-grams: n words ke continuous sequences. Sentence "The cow jumped over the moon" ke 2-grams (bigrams) hain ['The cow', 'cow jumped', 'jumped over', 'over the', 'the moon']. Spam detection ke liye 3-grams aur 4-grams individual words se zyada useful hote hain — jaise spam email me "You have won the lottery and are now rich!" sentence me "won", "the" aur "lottery" alag-alag context nahi dete, lekin 3-gram "won the lottery" turant red flag hai.
  • Word embeddings: word ko kuch dimensions me represent karte hain taaki uska meaning aur dusre words se relationship capture ho. Example: king ko [0.5, 0.7] se represent kar sakte hain. Ideally similar words paas hote hain — dog aur puppy paas, cat aur kitten paas. Aur dog-puppy ke beech ki distance aur direction, cat-kitten ke beech jaisi hi hoti hai — jaise sheep aur lamb ke beech bhi hogi.
  • BERT: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers — text input ko numeric input me badalne ka popular tareeka hai. Word embeddings aksar specific problem ke context me train kiye jate hain.
Yaad rakho: Image ko samajhna aasan hai — woh pehle se hi numbers ka grid hai. Text mushkil hai kyunki words ka meaning context se aata hai — isliye n-grams aur embeddings jaise techniques chahiye hoti hain.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — Next Steps in Your AI Journey

09.2Chapter 9 · Next Steps in Your AI Journey

Generative AI aur Explainable AI

Ab tak ke models discriminative the — woh batate the ki ek instance kis class ka hai. Generative models ulta kaam karte hain — label se instance generate karte hain. Aur models jitne bade hote hain, unhe explain karna utna mushkil hota hai — yahan explainable AI (XAI) aata hai.

Generative AI — discriminative se ulta

  • Discriminative models: goal hota hai predict karna ki instance kis class ka hai — jaise transaction fraudulent hai ya legitimate.
  • Generative models: inverse problem — label se instance generate karte hain. Example: label "a cat playing a banjo" diya jaye to uski image generate hoti hai. craiyon.com jaise free tools se aise models se khel sakte ho.
  • Chatbots: ChatGPT aur Bard generative AI ke chatbot examples hain. Inke peeche large language models (LLMs) hain — bade datasets par train kiye gaye, massive parameters wale language models. Example: ChatGPT ke peeche wala original model GPT-3.5 ke 175 billion se zyada parameters the aur uska corpus aadhe trillion se zyada tokens ka tha.
  • Products me: generative AI capabilities ab bahut se commercial products me aa rahi hain — jaise search engines aur code assistants me.
  • Ethics: generative AI ki society me bhoomika aur uske responsible use par bahut interesting conversations ho rahi hain — ye is book ke scope se bahar hai, lekin aage badhte hue ye conversations bahut important hain.

Explainable AI — XAI ki categories

  • Background: Chapters 4 aur 5 me feature attributions dekhe the, aur Chapter 6 me structured data ke liye XAI ka introduction tha. XAI techniques unstructured data (images, text) ke liye bhi exist karti hain.
  • Intrinsic techniques: model ki structure se explanations deti hain. Linear models aur decision trees intrinsically explainable hote hain — linear model me weights hi features ki relative importance batate hain.
  • Post hoc techniques: model train hone ke baad uski predictions se uska behavior samajhti hain. Ye aksar evaluation dataset ke ek hisse par train ki jati hain.
  • Local vs global: local techniques ek single instance par focus karti hain — is specific prediction ke peeche kya wajah thi. Global techniques poore dataset par model ka behavior dekhti hain. Local techniques ke results ko dataset par aggregate karke global technique bana sakte ho.
  • Model-agnostic vs model-specific: model-agnostic techniques data ko alter karke dekhti hain ki predictions kaise badalti hain. Model-specific techniques ek specific model type ke liye hoti hain — jaise tree-based models ke liye directional feature importances, aur neural networks ke liye integrated gradients.

Permutation feature importance (PFI)

  • Kya hai: AutoML me dekhi gayi feature attributions isi se compute hoti hain. Pehle dataset par model ka loss compute karo. Phir pehle column ko permute karke (uski values ko shuffle karke, baaki columns ko waisa hi rakh kar) loss dobara compute karo.
  • Score: original loss aur permuted loss ka difference us feature ki importance ka score hota hai. Ye har column ke liye repeat karo, phir scores ko normalize karo taaki sab normalized scores ka sum 1 ho jaye.
  • Caveat: PFI permutation ki randomness par depend karta hai — isliye aksar ek column ke liye multiple permutations karke average nikaalte hain.

Integrated gradients — neural networks ke liye

  • Idea: neural networks differentiable models hote hain — yehi property gradient descent me loss minimize karne ke liye bhi use hoti hai. Integrated gradients dekhte hain ki features badalne par predictions kaise badalti hain, aur un changes ko accumulate karte hain.
  • Example — fireboat image: model ne ek fireboat ki photo ko sahi classify kiya. Kyun? Baseline ke roop me ek poori black image lo. Phir pixels ko proportionally bright karte hue original image tak jao, har step par dekho ki "fireboat" ki predicted probability kitni badli. Har pixel ke liye ye rates of change accumulate karo — jinke accumulated values sabse zyada hain, woh pixels prediction ke liye sabse important hain.
  • Result: integrated gradients ne boat se nikalne wali paani ki streams ko highlight kiya — wahi wajah thi jisse model ne photo ko fireboat pehchana.
  • Baseline: aksar black image hoti hai, lekin white image ya random noise bhi use ho sakti hai, circumstance ke hisaab se.
Yaad rakho: Intrinsic explainability sirf simple models me milti hai. Complex models ke liye post hoc techniques chahiye hoti hain — aur local explanation ko aggregate karke global picture bhi bana sakte ho.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — Next Steps in Your AI Journey

09.3Chapter 9 · Next Steps in Your AI Journey

MLOps — Continuous Training aur Evaluation

Chapter 7 me tumne churn model train karke notebook me predictions serve kiye — lekin production me model pahunchana isse bahut bada kaam hai. MLOps woh discipline hai jo model ke aas-paas ke saare kaam sambhalti hai: infrastructure, deployment, monitoring aur updates.

MLOps kya hai

  • Definition: ML operations, ya MLOps, model ke alawa baaki saare tasks manage karne ki discipline hai — infrastructure manage karna, model kaise deploy aur access hoga ye decide karna, aur model ko monitor karke samay par update karna.
  • Hidden complexity: production ML me ML code sirf ek chhota hissa hota hai — data ready karna, compute infrastructure, resource consumption optimize karna, model ko consumers ke liye usable banana, aur time ke saath monitor karna — ye sab usse bahut bada kaam hai.
  • Roles: ye aksar ML engineers, data engineers aur data scientists ki responsibility hoti hai. Lekin tum kisi bhi role me ho, production concerns ki high-level samajh bahut valuable hai.
  • Collaboration: ek company me ek hi person sab kuch nahi karta — acchi communication key hai. Model banane wale ke roop me tum acchi notes share kar sakte ho: kaunse tools aur data sources use hue, kya preprocessing chahiye, aur prediction time par model ko kaunse features chahiye.
  • Preprocessing model ke andar: scikit-learn transformers ya Keras preprocessing layers se preprocessing logic ko model ke andar daalna engineers ke liye training aur prediction pipelines deploy karna aasan bana deta hai.

Drift — model kyun kharab hota hai

  • Fraud example: Chapter 5 me AutoML se fraud classification model train kiya tha — dataset par performance acchi thi. Kuch months production me rehne ke baad support teams ko customers se fraudulent transactions ki zyada reports milne lagi — model ne unme se bahut si ko flag hi nahi kiya. Kya hua?
  • Data drift: underlying data distribution me change. Example: ek naya type ka fraudulent transaction aa gaya jo original training dataset me tha hi nahi — model use pakad hi nahi sakta.
  • Concept drift: features aur labels ke beech ka relationship hi badal jata hai. Example: retail demand forecasting — shopping trends time ke saath badalte hain, aur wahi product alag times par alag tareeke se bikta hai. Product nahi badla, lekin product aur sales ka relationship badal gaya.

Continuous training aur continuous evaluation

  • Continuous training: model ko automatically retrain karne ka process, kisi criterion ke basis par. Criterion aksar time ya model performance par based hota hai — jaise har week retrain karna, ya tab retrain karna jab customers dwara report ki gayi missed fraudulent transactions ek certain percentage se zyada ho jayein. Production models ke liye ye bahut common aur important practice hai.
  • Continuous evaluation: retrain kab karna hai, ye decide karne me madad karta hai, aur model ki performance monitor karne ka important hissa hai. Model naye data par predict karta rehta hai, aur naye data ka ek sample label kiya jata hai — aksar domain experts labels dete hain. Phir model ko in naye labels ke against evaluate karte ho. Agar performance time ke saath girne lage to ye drift ka sign hai aur retrain ka time ho sakta hai.
  • Teamwork: ye concerns tumhari direct responsibility na bhi hon, phir bhi in tools aur concerns se aware rehna tumhe behtar collaborator banata hai — aur tum apne approach me aise decisions le sakte ho jo dusron ka kaam aasan kar dein.
Yaad rakho: Production me model daalna finish line nahi hai — drift ki wajah se performance time ke saath girti hai. Continuous evaluation se pata chalta hai kab retrain karna hai, aur continuous training se model fresh rehta hai.
SOURCESource: Low-Code AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — Next Steps in Your AI Journey

F1End Matter · Interview FAQs
Interview FAQs
ML interviews (current era) ke liye — AutoML se lekar MLOps tak, 36 sawaal-jawaab. Har jawaab isi book ke concepts par aadharit hai.
Q01 No-code, low-code aur custom code ML me kya farak hai, aur kab kya use karna chahiye?
No-code solutions jaise AutoML best hain jab tumhare paas ML expertise nahi hai ya tumhe jaldi benchmark model chahiye — ye feature engineering aur hyperparameter tuning khud sambhalte hain. Low-code solutions jaise BigQuery ML best hain jab tumhe thodi customization chahiye aur tumhara data tool ki constraints me fit hota hai, jaise structured data par SQL se model banana. Custom code solutions jaise scikit-learn, Keras ya PyTorch sabse flexible hain — kisi bhi data type aur objective par kaam karte hain, lekin inme sabse zyada time aur expertise lagti hai. Decision time, dataset, problem type aur tumhari apni expertise dekh kar lo.
Q02 AutoML kya hai aur ye kab custom model se behtar hota hai?
AutoML ek no-code approach hai jo model selection, feature engineering aur hyperparameter tuning ko automate kar deta hai — tum sirf data aur target dete ho, aur woh best model dhoondhta hai. Ye rapid prototyping aur benchmark banane ke liye best hai, aur aksar production me bhi kaafi hota hai. Custom models tab behtar hote hain jab tumhe full control chahiye ho, koi custom transformation ya deployment chahiye ho, ya AutoML tumhara problem type support na karta ho. Kaafi time aur effort ke saath custom solutions AutoML se outperform kar sakte hain, lekin incremental gain aksar jaldi production me pahunchne ke fayde se chhota hota hai.
Q03 BigQuery ML kya hai aur iske fayde kya hain?
BigQuery ML Google BigQuery ke andar SQL se ML models banane aur train karne ki service hai — data ko move kiye bina, wahi SQL likh kar jo tum pehle se jante ho. Isme linear regression, logistic regression, DNN aur aur bhi model types hain, aur string columns automatically one-hot encode ho jate hain. Iska sabse bada fayda hai ki SQL jaanne wale log bina Python sikhe models bana sakte hain, aur TRANSFORM clause se preprocessing model ke andar store ho jata hai taaki prediction time par wahi transformations lagen.
Q04 Regression aur classification me kya farak hai?
Regression me tum ek continuous numeric value predict karte ho — jaise gaadi ki auction price ya power plant ki output. Classification me tum ek discrete class predict karte ho — jaise customer churn karega ya nahi, ya transaction fraud hai ya legitimate. Regression ko RMSE aur MAE jaise metrics se evaluate karte hain, aur classification ko accuracy, precision, recall aur confusion matrix se. Dono ke loss functions bhi alag hote hain — regression me mean squared error, classification me cross-entropy.
Q05 Logistic regression kaise kaam karta hai?
Logistic regression linear combination f(x) = w0 + w1x1 + ... + wnxn ko sigmoid function se pass karta hai: g(x) = 1 / (1 + exp(-f(x))). Sigmoid ki values hamesha 0 aur 1 ke beech rehti hain, isliye output ko positive class ki probability ki tarah interpret kar sakte ho. Training me cross-entropy loss minimize ki jati hai — model jitna confident aur galat hoga, loss utna tezi se badhega. Ye binary classification ke liye ek simple lekin bahut strong baseline hai.
Q06 Accuracy, precision aur recall me kya farak hai, aur kab kaunsa metric important hai?
Accuracy sahi predictions ka overall percentage hai. Precision batata hai ki jinhe model ne positive bataya, unme se kitne sach me positive the — matlab false alarms kitne kam hain. Recall batata hai ki actual positives me se kitne ko model ne pakda — matlab kitne miss hue. Churn rokne ya fraud pakadne jaise cases me recall zyada important hai, kyunki ek bhi churner ya fraud miss karna mehenga padta hai. Accuracy akeli misleading ho sakti hai — jaise churn data me hamesha 'no churn' predict karne par bhi 73.5% accuracy mil jati hai, lekin us model ki business value zero hai.
Q07 Confusion matrix kya hoti hai aur use kaise padhte hain?
Confusion matrix predictions ko chaar hisson me baant ti hai: true positives (actual positive, predicted positive), false negatives (actual positive, predicted negative — miss hue cases), false positives (actual negative, predicted positive — false alarms), aur true negatives (actual negative, predicted negative). Churn model ka matrix [[187, 185], [98, 939]] tha — 187 churners sahi pakde, 185 miss hue, 939 non-churners sahi pehchane, 98 galat flag hue. Isi se precision (187 / (187+98) = 0.656) aur recall (187 / (187+185) = 0.503) nikaale jate hain.
Q08 Overfitting kya hai aur use kaise pehchanein aur rokein?
Overfitting tab hota hai jab model training data par evaluation data se bahut behtar perform kare — model data ko memorize kar leta hai aur general patterns miss kar deta hai. Ise pehchanne ka tareeka hai training aur validation metrics compare karna — jaise BigQuery ML wale linear model me training RMSE lagbhag $3,000 tha lekin validation RMSE $8,000 se zyada. Rokne ke tareeke hain: zyada data, simpler model, regularization (L1/L2, dropout), early stopping, aur feature count kam karna — jaise 770,000 feature-cross values ne overfitting karwaya tha.
Q09 L1 aur L2 regularization me kya farak hai?
Dono loss function me ek penalty term jodte hain taaki model ki complexity kam ho. L2 regularization weights ke squares ka sum jodti hai — ye weights ko chhota karne ki koshish karti hai. L1 regularization weights ke absolute values ka sum jodti hai — ye un weights ko zero ki taraf dhakel deti hai jo influential nahi hain, jo sparse features ke liye bahut valuable hai, jaise feature crosses. Dono ek saath use karna elastic net kehlata hai. Lambda (regularization rate) control karta hai ki penalty kitni strong ho.
Q10 Dropout kya hai aur ye overfitting kaise rokta hai?
Dropout ek regularization technique hai jo training ke dauran har batch me hidden layers ke kuch percent neurons ko 'band' kar deti hai — unke weighted sums zero set kar diye jate hain. Isse model kisi ek neuron ya feature par zyada depend nahi kar pata aur zyada robust banta hai. Prediction time par dropout use nahi hota, taaki model ki poori power mile. BigQuery ML me dropout ko 0 se 0.8 ke range me tune kiya ja sakta hai.
Q11 Hyperparameter aur parameter me kya farak hai?
Parameters woh values hain jo model training ke dauran seekhta hai — jaise linear regression ke weights. Hyperparameters woh settings hain jo tum training se pehle set karte ho aur jo training ke dauran update nahi hote — jaise hidden layers ki count, neurons per layer, learning rate, batch size, aur bucketization me buckets ki count. Hyperparameters ko tune karne ke liye grid search, random search ya Bayesian optimization use karte hain.
Q12 Grid search, random search aur Bayesian optimization me kya farak hai?
Grid search saare combinations try karta hai — candidate ranges ke andar best hyperparameters pakke milte hain, lekin 4 hyperparameters × 10 values = 10,000 models train karne pad sakte hain, jo jaldi infeasible ho jata hai. Random search randomly kuch candidates try karta hai — time control kar sakte ho, lekin best model miss ho sakta hai. Bayesian optimization pehle kuch random models train karke unke results se seekhta hai aur agle candidates intelligently choose karta hai — random search se zyada efficient hai, lekin ye bhi poora search space exhaust nahi karta.
Q13 Halving grid search kya hai?
Halving grid search grid search ka efficient variant hai. Pehle saare candidate models ko training data ke chhote hisse par train karte ho, phir best-performing fraction ko rakh kar zyada data par train karte ho, aur ye repeat karte ho jab tak best candidate na mil jaye. Car price problem me 625 candidates the aur poora tuning Colab par 35-40 minutes leta tha. Iska risk hai ki chhote data par bura lagne wala model poore data par accha hota, lekin ye random search se zyada effective hoti hai.
Q14 Feature engineering kya hai aur ye itni important kyun hai?
Feature engineering raw data se useful features banana hai — jaise bucketization, one-hot encoding, aur feature crosses. Aksar carefully banaye hue features, simple model ke saath bhi, bahut strong results dete hain. Car price problem me condition ko bucketize karne se RMSE $3,384 se $3,313 hua, aur model-trim aur color-interior feature crosses se $3,122 tak aa gaya. Model ko complicated banana hamesha sahi approach nahi hai — complex models ko zyada data aur compute chahiye hota hai.
Q15 Feature cross kya hota hai? Example do.
Feature cross do ya zyada features ko concatenate karke banaya gaya synthetic feature hai. Example: car ka model aur trim alag-alag kaafi nahi hain — 'LX' trim alag models me bhi hota hai, aur ek model ke alag trims hote hain, isliye model_trim cross banate hain jisme 'CR-V LX' ek alag value hai. BigQuery ML me ye ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(make, model)) se banta hai, aur Keras me HashedCrossing layer se. Feature crosses powerful hote hain lekin features ki count bahut badha dete hain — yahan 770,000 values ban gayi thi, jisse overfitting hua.
Q16 One-hot encoding kya hai aur kab use karte hain?
One-hot encoding categorical feature ko numeric representation me badalti hai — har possible value ke liye ek naya binary column banta hai. Example: InternetService ke values No, DSL aur Fiber Optic ki encoding [1,0,0], [0,1,0] aur [0,0,1] hoti hai. Binary features ke liye scikit-learn me drop='if_binary' se sirf 0/1 use hota hai. BigQuery ML me string columns automatically one-hot encode ho jate hain, aur Keras me StringLookup layer ye kaam karta hai.
Q17 Bucketization kya hai aur iske fayde kya hain?
Bucketization numeric column ko value ranges (buckets) me baant kar categorical bana deti hai. Example: DiffCharges ko 5 buckets me baantne par dikha ki monthly charge aur average charge ke beech bada difference hone par churn rate zyada hota hai — ye pattern numeric form me dikhai nahi deta tha. Pandas me pd.cut(), scikit-learn me KBinsDiscretizer, Keras me Discretization layer, aur BigQuery ML me ML.BUCKETIZE ya ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE use hote hain. Bucket count ka dhyaan rakho — bahut kam se patterns miss hote hain, bahut zyada se noise badhta hai.
Q18 Train-validation-test split kyun karte hain? Sirf train-test kyun nahi?
Training set model train karne ke liye, validation set alag-alag models compare karne aur hyperparameters tune karne ke liye, aur test set final independent verification ke liye hota hai. Agar tum sirf train-test use karo aur test par dekh kar model chuno, to woh model test ki taraf biased ho jata hai. Car price problem me validation par best model chuna gaya aur test par final check kiya gaya. Teenon datasets ki distributions similar honi chahiye, warna test par bada performance drop aata hai.
Q19 Training-serving skew kya hai aur use kaise rokte hain?
Training-serving skew tab hota hai jab prediction time par data ko woh transformations na milen jo training time par mili thi. Classic example: churn model me training data MinMaxScaler se scale kiya tha lekin test data nahi — accuracy 80% ki bajay 48% aa gayi. Rokne ke tareeke hain: training time par fit_transform aur prediction time par sirf transform use karo, saari preprocessing ek function ya pipeline me band karo, aur scikit-learn Pipeline, Keras preprocessing layers ya BigQuery ML TRANSFORM clause use karo taaki transformations model ke saath hi travel karen.
Q20 Scikit-learn Pipeline kya hai aur iske fayde kya hain?
Pipeline transformers ka sequence hai jisme aakhri object model hota hai. Fit karne par saare transformers par fit_transform chalta hai aur phir model fit hota hai; predict karne par saare transformers ke transform order me lagte hain aur phir model predict karta hai. FunctionTransformer se Pandas wale steps aur ColumnTransformer se alag columns par alag transformations pipeline me daal sakte ho. Sabse bada fayda hai portability — poori pipeline ko joblib ya pickle se export kar sakte ho, jisme trained model ke saath fit hue transformers bhi hote hain, isliye serving time par consistency bani rehti hai.
Q21 Keras me Sequential API aur Functional API me kya farak hai?
Sequential API layers ki simple list se model banati hai — jab model ek straight stack ho to ye kaafi hai, jaise Chapter 7 ka churn classifier (Dense 64-32-16). Functional API tab use hoti hai jab alag inputs par alag processing ho — jaise Chapter 8 me har feature par alag preprocessing layer (StringLookup, Discretization, HashedCrossing) lagi thi, phir sabko Concatenate karke neural network me dala gaya. Functional API me har layer ko apna input explicitly specify karna padta hai.
Q22 Early stopping kya hai aur patience ka kya matlab hai?
Early stopping ek callback hai jo training ko rok deta hai jab evaluation performance improve hona band ho jaye ya bigadne lage — ye overfitting se bachata hai. Patience batata hai ki kitne epochs tak stalled ya worsening performance ka wait karna hai — jaise patience=5 ka matlab hai 5 epochs tak wait karo, kyunki training me randomness se thoda noise hota hai. Restore_best_weights=True se model apni best performance wale weights par wapas aa jata hai, taaki waiting period me hui kharabi bhi undo ho jaye.
Q23 Keras Tuner kaise kaam karta hai?
Keras Tuner hyperparameters tune karne ka package hai. Tum ek build_model function banate ho jo hyperparameters input le kar compiled model return karta hai — jaise hp.Int('units_1', min_value=8, max_value=64, step=4) se hidden layer ke neurons define karte ho. Phir ek tuner banate ho, jaise BayesianOptimization, jisme objective (val_loss minimize karna) aur max_trials (jaise 20) set karte ho. Tuner har candidate ko kuch epochs train karke best hyperparameters dhoondhta hai — car price problem me best units 52, 64 aur 32 mile aur validation RMSE 2,000 se neeche aa gaya.
Q24 RMSE aur MAE me kya farak hai?
Dono regression metrics hain jo prediction error ko original units me batate hain. MAE errors ka average absolute value hai — har error ko barabar weight milta hai. RMSE errors ke squares ka mean lekar square root nikalta hai — bade errors ko zyada penalty milti hai, isliye outliers se zyada affected hota hai. Car price baseline model me RMSE lagbhag $3,384.60 aur MAE lagbhag $2,044.26 tha. Business goal RMSE $2,000 ya kam tha, isliye tuning me neg_root_mean_squared_error ko score banakar optimize kiya gaya.
Q25 BigQuery ML me TRANSFORM clause kyun zaroori hai?
Agar tum transformations karke naya table save karo aur us par model train karo, to prediction time par wahi transformations dobara karni padengi — lekin tumhe one-hot encoding kaise hui aur bucket endpoints kya the, ye pata nahi hoga. TRANSFORM clause transformation SQL ko model ke andar store kar deta hai, aur ML.PREDICT chalane par woh input table par pehle execute hota hai. Ye scikit-learn pipelines aur Keras preprocessing layers ka BigQuery ML version hai — training-serving skew se bachne ka tareeka.
Q26 Imputation kya hai? Example do.
Imputation unknown ya missing values ko reasonable values se replace karne ka process hai. Churn dataset me 11 rows me TotalCharges khaali string thi kyunki tenure 0 tha — pehla month hone ki wajah se abhi charge hi nahi hua tha, isliye use 0.0 se replace kiya gaya. DiffCharges me divide-by-zero se aaye NaN values ko bhi 0 se replace kiya gaya, kyunki 'koi difference nahi' ek reasonable assumption thi. Bina imputation ke tum wo useful rows kho dete. Bade datasets me agar missing data kisi ek group par focused na ho to data omit karna bhi ek strategy hai.
Q27 Collinearity kya hai aur ye model ko kaise nuksan pahunchati hai?
Collinearity tab hoti hai jab predictor variables ke beech high correlation ho — jaise churn dataset me tenure aur TotalCharges ka correlation lagbhag 0.82 tha, aur PhoneService MultipleLines me already captured tha. Isse regression coefficients ke estimates unreliable aur unstable ho jate hain, aur ye problem linear models me aur bhi badh jati hai. Isse bachne ka ek tareeka hai collinear columns ke set me se sirf ek column rakhna — jaise PhoneService aur TotalCharges ko drop kar diya gaya tha.
Q28 Unstructured data kya hai aur images ko ML model me kaise use karte hain?
Unstructured data woh hai jiska koi schema nahi hota — images, videos, sound files aur text. Images pehle se hi numbers ka grid hoti hain: grayscale image me har pixel ki value 0 se 255 hoti hai (0 black, 255 white), aur color image me har pixel ke teen RGB channels hote hain. Yehi arrays image models ke numeric inputs hain. MNIST dataset handwritten digit recognition ka 'hello world' hai — 60,000 training aur 10,000 test images, har ek 28 × 28 grayscale. Image classification multiclass classification hai, aur convolutional layers isme bahut useful hote hain.
Q29 Word embeddings aur n-grams kya hain?
Dono text ko numeric data me badalne ke tareeke hain. N-grams n words ke continuous sequences hote hain — jaise 'The cow jumped over the moon' ke bigrams 'The cow', 'cow jumped' hain. Spam detection me 3-grams aur 4-grams individual words se zyada useful hote hain, kyunki 'won the lottery' jaisa 3-gram turant red flag hai jabki 'won' akela context nahi deta. Word embeddings words ko kuch dimensions me represent karte hain taaki meaning aur relationships capture hon — jaise dog aur puppy paas hote hain, cat aur kitten paas, aur dog-puppy ke beech ki direction cat-kitten jaisi hoti hai. BERT text ko numeric input me badalne ka popular tareeka hai.
Q30 Generative AI aur discriminative AI me kya farak hai?
Discriminative models predict karte hain ki ek instance kis class ka hai — jaise transaction fraud hai ya legitimate. Generative models ulta kaam karte hain — label se instance generate karte hain, jaise 'a cat playing a banjo' label se uski image banana. Chatbots jaise ChatGPT aur Bard generative AI hain, aur inke peeche large language models (LLMs) hote hain — jaise GPT-3.5 ke 175 billion se zyada parameters the aur uska corpus aadhe trillion se zyada tokens ka tha. Generative AI image generation, chatbots aur code assistants jaise products me use ho rahi hai.
Q31 Explainable AI (XAI) kya hai? Intrinsic aur post hoc techniques me kya farak hai?
XAI woh techniques hain jo batati hain ki model ne ek prediction kyun ki. Intrinsic techniques model ki structure se explanations deti hain — linear models aur decision trees intrinsically explainable hote hain, kyunki linear model me weights hi feature importance batate hain. Post hoc techniques model train hone ke baad uski predictions se behavior samajhti hain. Inhe local (ek instance ki explanation) ya global (poore dataset ka behavior) me baanta jata hai, aur model-agnostic (kisi bhi model par kaam kare) ya model-specific (jaise neural networks ke liye integrated gradients) me bhi.
Q32 Permutation feature importance (PFI) kaise kaam karta hai?
PFI me pehle dataset par model ka loss compute karte ho, phir ek column ki values ko shuffle (permute) karke loss dobara compute karte ho — baaki columns waisi hi rehti hain. Original loss aur permuted loss ka difference us feature ki importance ka score hota hai. Ye har column ke liye repeat karte ho aur scores ko normalize karte ho taaki unka sum 1 ho jaye. Ye AutoML me dikhne wali feature attributions compute karne ka tareeka hai. Isme permutation ki randomness hoti hai, isliye aksar multiple permutations karke average nikaalte hain.
Q33 Integrated gradients kya hai?
Integrated gradients neural networks ke liye ek model-specific XAI technique hai. Ye is baat ka fayda uthati hai ki neural networks differentiable hote hain. Ek baseline image (aksar poori black image) se shuru karke pixels ko proportionally bright karte hue original image tak jate hain, aur har step par dekhte hain ki predicted probability kitni badli. Har pixel ke liye ye rates of change accumulate karte hain — sabse zyada accumulated value wale pixels prediction ke liye sabse important hote hain. Fireboat wale example me isne boat se nikalne wali paani ki streams ko highlight kiya tha.
Q34 MLOps kya hai aur ye kyun zaroori hai?
MLOps (ML operations) model ke alawa baaki saare tasks manage karne ki discipline hai — infrastructure, deployment, resource optimization, aur monitoring aur updates. Production ML me ML code sirf ek chhota hissa hota hai — baaki kaam usse bahut bada hai. Ye aksar ML engineers, data engineers aur data scientists ki responsibility hoti hai, lekin model banane wale ko bhi iski high-level samajh honi chahiye taaki woh acchi notes share kar sake aur preprocessing ko model ke andar daal kar engineers ka kaam aasan kar sake.
Q35 Data drift aur concept drift me kya farak hai?
Data drift me underlying data distribution badal jati hai — jaise ek naya type ka fraudulent transaction aa jaye jo original training dataset me tha hi nahi, to model use pakad hi nahi sakta. Concept drift me features aur labels ke beech ka relationship badal jata hai — jaise retail demand forecasting me shopping trends badalne par wahi product alag times par alag tareeke se bikta hai. Product nahi badla, lekin product aur sales ka relationship badal gaya. Dono se model ki performance time ke saath girti hai.
Q36 Continuous training aur continuous evaluation kya hain?
Continuous training model ko automatically retrain karne ka process hai, kisi criterion ke basis par — jaise har week retrain karna, ya tab retrain karna jab missed fraudulent transactions ek certain percentage se zyada ho jayein. Continuous evaluation me naye data ka ek sample label kiya jata hai (aksar domain experts se) aur model ko un naye labels ke against evaluate karte hain. Agar performance time ke saath girne lage to ye drift ka sign hai aur retrain ka time ho sakta hai. Production models ke liye ye dono bahut common aur important practices hain.
